A soft-return paragraph like 'context\nAI-1: action' starts with 'context', so the regex fails, occurrences is empty, and the flush returns false (logs flush.warn: Paragraph not found). title: [FIX] show_tab('Import') times out waiting for sidebar button — reproducible, not a setup-timing flake
description:
tests/test_import.py::test_import_access_filter fails at scn_target.ui.show_tab("Import")
(scn/ui.py:953) — Locator.wait_for: Timeout 30000ms exceeded waiting for
get_by_role("button", name="Import", exact=True) to become visible.

CONFIRMED REPRODUCIBLE, NOT A FLAKE (2026-06-20):
Failed identically on two separate full runs:
  1. test-results/runs/test_import_access_filter_20260620T021416Z.* — total
     leadup to show_tab() was 135.83s (scn_sibling/scn_other did full
     move_doc_to_folder+sync()+seed-paragraph+sync() setup).
  2. test-results/runs/test_import_access_filter_20260620T025406Z.* — same
     test, AFTER rewriting scn_sibling/scn_other to use seed_row+
     set_docdata_row instead of real sync() (perf fix, same commit/session).
     Leadup to show_tab() dropped to 67.83s — but the failure occurred at
     the exact same call, same symptom, same 30s timeout.
Eliminating ~68s of unrelated setup latency did not change the outcome, so
this is not timing/staleness from slow leadup — it's a real, reproducible
defect in show_tab()/open_sidebar(), or in how the addon iframe is found.

DIAGNOSTIC SCREENSHOT IS MISLEADING — DO NOT TRUST IT AT FACE VALUE:
Both failures' captured screenshot shows the doc's iframe with a "Take out
of trash" button, which looks like the doc was already trashed when
show_tab() timed out. It wasn't. tests/conftest.py's
pytest_runtest_makereport hookwrapper (line 32) only fires after
report.when=="call", i.e. after the ENTIRE test function returns — including
its own `finally:` block, which sequentially calls end_journey_session for
every session (~17s of further HTTP calls). Cross-referencing the Axiom GAS
log for the docId involved in run 1 confirms 'journey.end trashed=<docId>'
landed ~5.5s AFTER show_tab's FAIL event was logged, and the actual
screenshot (taken by the conftest hook) can only happen after ALL FOUR
sessions' end_journey_session calls finish — at least ~17s later still. So
the trash banner is a late-capture artifact of normal test cleanup, not
evidence of the doc's real state at the moment of timeout.

THE REAL CLUE: at the time of that (late) screenshot, the diagnostics also
list 'Import' as a literally VISIBLE button in the
addons.gsuite.google.com iframe:
  buttons=['', '', 'Sync', 'Import', 'Notify', 'Insert Tracker', 'User Guide']
So the button renders somewhere on the page, yet
self._current_card.frame.get_by_role("button", name="Import", exact=True)
(scn/ui.py:964-967), scoped to the specific Playwright frame handle captured
by open_sidebar() (scn/ui.py:541), times out finding it. Working hypothesis:
the add-on iframe gets torn down and a fresh instance attached sometime
after open_sidebar() caches _current_card.frame, leaving a stale frame
handle that will never report the button visible even though a *current*
instance of that same iframe does show it.

NEXT STEP: read open_sidebar() and how _current_card is captured/cached
(scn/ui.py:541, _sidebar_card() at line 827) to confirm/refute the stale-
frame hypothesis. Consider whether _current_card needs to re-resolve the
frame (by URL/selector) rather than reuse a cached Frame object across
multiple show_tab() calls in the same session.

SEPARATE BUT RELATED FOLLOW-UP (do not fix as part of this bug, file
separately): show_tab() and the other bare-.wait_for() UiDriver methods
(sidebar_sync, insert_tracker_button, sidebar_delete) never call
self.capture_failure() on timeout, unlike create_action() (scn/ui.py:728-753)
which does. That's why this bug's only diagnostics came from the late,
misleading conftest fallback hook instead of a screenshot taken at the true
moment of failure. CLAUDE.md already states the rule ("Add a new bounded
wait? Route its failure through capture_failure") — these methods predate
it or were missed.
close_reason: Root cause: show_tab() located buttons via get_by_role(name=label, exact=True), matching ARIA accessible name not visible text. CardService's .setAltText() on the Import button (a11y improvement, commit d5a26442) diverges accessible name from visible label, breaking exact-name matching even though the button is visible/correct/not-stale. Fixed by matching text content via .filter(has_text=...) instead. Secondary stale-deployment issue (IMPORT_LIST.done -> importList.done tag rename not yet redeployed) fixed via npm run deploy:test. Verified: tests/test_import.py full file (4 tests) passes. Details in bd memory 3zl5-aria-label-vs-text-locator.

title: [INF] Add call-tree correlation ID to GAS-side logging (no shared id across a multi-step invocation's sub-events)
description:
Surfaced during journey-logging/Axiom rollout (gts-ishz.1, 2026-06-19) while
analyzing real Axiom data from a pytest run. Re-analyze independently in a fresh
session -- don't just take this writeup as given; verify the gap still exists and
re-derive the right fix shape before implementing.

Observed gap: GasLogger.log() entries have no field correlating which sub-events
belong to one specific invocation of a multi-step operation. Checked concretely:
src/SyncManager.js's syncAll() (~line 282-385) logs 'sync.all.start' once, then
loops logging 'sync.scanned'/'sync.complete' per doc -- nothing ties a *specific*
syncAll() run to *its* per-doc sub-events except inferring from time-proximity.
That's exactly the fragile manual reconstruction this whole project exists to
eliminate (see docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md's own motivating case).

docId (single doc's sync chain) and the Python side's run_id (test node name, added
in gts-ishz.1) happen to correlate some things incidentally, but neither was
designed as a correlation key, and there's no equivalent for "this one syncAll()
run across N docs" or other multi-step entry points (journey session, import flows).

Candidate direction (verify/re-derive, don't assume): a small opId/traceId stamped
automatically onto every GasLogger.log() entry for the duration of one top-level
invocation -- same additive pattern as the version auto-stamp added in
gts-ishz.1 (GasLogger.log() now stamps BUILD_INFO.version on every entry
without touching ~190 call sites). E.g. GasLogger.withOp(opId, fn) or a module-level
"current op" set at syncAll()'s start and cleared at its end. Start with syncAll()
and the journey session begin/end pair as the first two entry points -- low risk,
no existing tag strings change.

Why P1: this is structural, not a data-volume problem -- no amount of additional
logged history fixes the lack of a correlation key later. Cheap to add now while
volume is still low; expensive to retrofit once dashboards/queries depend on
time-window-based correlation as a workaround.

AC (draft, re-validate before coding):
- A single syncAll() invocation's sub-events (sync.all.start, every per-doc
  sync.scanned/sync.complete, sync.all.complete) share one queryable correlation
  field in Axiom that uniquely identifies that invocation (not derivable from time
  proximity alone).
- Existing tag strings/log call sites outside the touched entry points are
  unchanged (additive only).
- Demonstrate the new field by running two concurrent or back-to-back syncAll()
  invocations and showing they're cleanly separable by the new field alone.
notes:
Re-verified independently: gap confirmed real (GasLogger.log() entries had no correlation field; syncAll()'s sync.all.start/sync.scanned×N/sync.complete×N/sync.all.complete were only inferable by time-proximity).

Implemented: GasLogger.startOp()/endOp() (module-level _currentOp, Utilities.getUuid(), stamped as entry.op on every log() call while set; also threaded into the Axiom row mapping in _postToAxiom). Wired into syncAll() only (start at top, end in the existing finally block alongside flush()).

Scope correction vs the draft AC: the journey-session begin/end pair (WebApp.js _handleJourneySession) does NOT have the gap this bead targets — each handler invocation (begin_journey_session, end_journey_session) emits exactly ONE log() call, so there are no within-invocation sub-events to correlate; docId already links begin/end across the two separate doPost executions. Did not wire op there. Documented this finding in the new doc debt bead (gts-1nln) so it isn't re-litigated.

Verification: tests/test_sync_all.py::test_sync_all_op_correlation (new) — two syncAll() sweeps against 2 real docs, asserts all of one sweep's sub-events share exactly one op id and that a second sweep gets a different one. Proved non-vacuous: reverted the GasLogger.js/SyncManager.js changes via git stash, redeployed TEST, confirmed the test fails with op missing entirely (not a fence artifact) — then restored, redeployed, reconfirmed pass. Full tests/test_sync_all.py (3 tests) green after restore.

Follow-ups filed: gts-j8cn (cross-invocation parentOp propagation, addon→WebApp), gts-x94a (tag taxonomy, pre-existing), gts-1nln (doc debt, blocked by this bead).
close_reason: op-id correlation implemented for syncAll() and verified non-vacuous; journey-session scoped out (no actual gap there); doc debt + follow-ups filed

title: [FIX] _insertActionChip throws 'Element does not contain the specified child element' when cursor is in an empty paragraph
description:
Reproduced 2x manually via @-menu Create action in a brand-new doc (clasp logs):
  CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER fires -> _submitCreateAction -> _insertActionChip throws at
  EditorAddonCard.js:663: cursorPara.getChildIndex(cursorElement)

Root cause: in src/EditorAddonCard.js _insertActionChip (~line 644-672), when
cursor.getElement() returns the PARAGRAPH itself (empty paragraph, e.g. first
line of a new doc, no Text child yet), the while-loop at 656-659 does not
execute, so cursorPara === cursorElement. getChildIndex(cursorElement) then
throws because a paragraph is not its own child.

Pre-code contract:
- Entry point: EditorAddonCard._submitCreateAction (CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER -> _insertActionChip)
- Log tags: CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER (start), CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.done / .error (existing, on success/insert-failure path), and the GAS exception log for this crash (currently uncaught -> generic _submitCreateAction Exception in clasp logs)
- Fix: when cursorElement === cursorPara (cursor element is already the
  containing paragraph/list-item), skip the getChildIndex/sibling-offset walk
  -- paraOffset stays equal to cursorOffset (no preceding siblings in an empty
  paragraph).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. _insertActionChip no longer throws when cursor.getElement() returns the
   containing paragraph/list-item directly (empty paragraph case).
2. paraOffset computed correctly (= cursorOffset) for the empty-paragraph case.
3. Existing non-empty-paragraph behavior (cursorElement is a TEXT/inline child)
   unchanged -- sibling-offset walk still runs in that case.
4. Manual repro (new doc, @create, fill form, submit) succeeds: chip inserted,
   CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.done logged, no _submitCreateAction exception.
notes:
RESOLVED. Root-cause fix (skip getChildIndex/sibling-walk when
cursorElement === cursorPara, the empty-paragraph case) was already in HEAD
(cddf488, EditorAddonCard.js:663-676) and is correct per AC1-3.

AC4 closed this session:
- Found _submitCreateAction never called GasLogger.flush() on any return
  path (every other entry point in EditorAddonCard.js does), so
  CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.* entries never reached the Drive log files the test
  harness polls. Wrapped the whole function body in try/catch (mirrors
  onLinkPreview) and added GasLogger.flush() after every
  CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.* log call. Uncaught exceptions now log
  CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.error and are caught by the existing
  _check_gas_errors fail-fast.
- tests/test_journey.py Act 4: added gas_log_dir fence + assert_log for
  CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.done around scn.ui.create_action() (which already
  drives the empty-paragraph path via Ctrl+End+Enter -> @create).
- Extracted assert_log/assert_no_log into tests/helpers/gas_log.py (was
  duplicated in test_team_scope.py).

Live-verified (npm run deploy:test + pytest tests/test_journey.py):
CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER fired, INSERT_CHIP.done (AI-14, cursorIndex:1),
CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.done all logged with no error/exception. Journey fails
later at Act 5 on the unrelated pre-existing gts-o5py (chip-hover
timing).

AC3 (non-empty-paragraph sibling-offset branch) remains untested -
recorded via bd remember, no new bead (avoids twin-ticket proliferation for
a coverage-only gap).
close_reason: Empty-paragraph cursor fix verified live (CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.done logged); AC4 closed via _submitCreateAction flush+try/catch and new journey assertion

title: [TST] R1-impl: implement drainable UI surface in engine + session
description: Implement the spec produced by R1-design: make Surface.UI drainable so verify(on=UI, within=…) routes through the expectation queue and obeys the drain invariant, removing test_journey.py deviation D2. Touches scn/engine.py (drain handling for UI), scn/session.py (checkpoint read() UI closure + within= poll), and scn/ui.py (live read used by the closure). Build strictly to the --design field populated by R1-design.
design:
DESIGN (R1-design, gts-80mo.1 → this bead). Build strictly to this. Honor §16
vocabulary and §16.11 decisions verbatim. Authoritative algorithm: scenario-harness-design.md §4.

== GOAL ==
Make Surface.UI a first-class, drainable surface so verify(on=UI[, within=…]) enqueues and
drains through the expectation queue like every other surface, and remove test_journey.py
deviation D2. Today session.checkpoint()'s read() closure returns [] for Surface.UI
(scn/session.py, the trailing `return []` in `read`), so any UI expectation can never match
and D2 routes around the queue with a direct scn.ui.expect_alt() assertion.

== CORE MODEL DECISION (binding; refines §4.4) ==
UI is LIVE-ONLY and drained at a STEP checkpoint during the Playwright phase. It is NOT
observed at INTEGRITY (INTEGRITY is a file-download reconcile and "never runs mid-Playwright",
§16.3 #5; the browser card may be gone by then). Therefore:
  - INTEGRITY's observable set EXCLUDES UI: obs = {DOC, SHEET, TRACKER} (+ CONSISTENCY pseudo).
  - UI expectations are always target=AUTO and must be drained by a STEP whose observable set
    includes UI, placed right after the gesture in the Playwright phase.
  - A UI expectation that never drains rides to close() and fails the drain invariant — this is
    the correct "UI coverage hole" signal, unchanged from §4.6.

== 1. read(UI) CLOSURE CONTRACT (scn/session.py + scn/ui.py) ==
The read closure built in ScenarioSession.checkpoint() must, for Surface.UI, delegate to the
live Playwright driver instead of returning []:

    if surface == Surface.UI:
        return self.ui.read_current() if self.ui is not None else []

read_current() is a NEW method on UiDriver (scn/ui.py). Unlike DOC/SHEET/TRACKER (which download
a complete document), the UI surface has no "whole document" — it observes the CURRENTLY-RENDERED
context: self._current_card (the card set by the last hover()/open_sidebar()/set_status()). It
returns a list[ai] parsed from that live frame, doc-scoped implicitly (the card is this doc's
chip/sidebar). Contract:
  - If self._current_card is None → return [] (no UI context to read).
  - For the current card, build ONE ai with at minimum:
      * action_id — from the card header text matching r"AI-\d+" (the "AI-N:" header; cf.
        test_journey.py rwz AC1, card header contains created.action_id + ":").
      * status    — from the card's currently-active status indicator (the rendered brand-NUTS
        status icon / selected status control), read via its aria-label/alt/title.
      * action    — (optional, best-effort) the header text after "AI-N:".
  - Return [that_ai]. (Sidebar homepage card may expose multiple rows "AI-N • topLabel"; if a
    sidebar context is the current card, return one ai per visible row. Card/preview context
    returns the single previewed action.)
The driver owns ALL selectors/frames/waits (§16.8 / §16.11 #8) — read_current holds the card-DOM
knowledge; the engine and session see only list[ai].

== 2. HOW AN Expectation WITH surfaces={UI} IS MATCHED (scn/assertions.py) ==
verify(ai, on=UI) enqueues Expectation(surfaces=frozenset({UI}), remaining={UI}, target=AUTO,
kind="PRESENT_CONSISTENT", within=<arg>). No new enqueuer needed — the existing verify() path
already handles on=Surface.UI; only the read closure and assertion scope change.

At drain, engine calls check_present_consistent(e.expected, read(UI), Surface.UI, e.tag). Add a
UI-surface carve-out in check_present_consistent, mirroring the existing TRACKER carve-out for
assignee_name (assertions.py lines 99-109):
  - On surface == Surface.UI, enforce ONLY: identity (action_id exact-match if pinned, else a
    valid AI-N) AND status (if "status" in expected). SKIP the action-text equality check, the
    assignee email check, and the assignee_name check.
  - Rationale: durable field correctness (text, assignee, name) is owned by DOC/SHEET/TRACKER;
    the UI surface's job is to confirm the LIVE card reflects the post-gesture state (status),
    which is exactly §16.10 Act 5's intent ("card/doc returns updated ≤10s"). This keeps
    read_current's required evidence to the two fields a card reliably exposes (id + status).

== 3. within= BOUNDED-POLL SEMANTICS ON THE UI SURFACE (scn/engine.py) ==
§4.5 step 2: "within ⇒ bounded poll on the UI surface until pass or timeout." The engine does NOT
implement within today (it reads once via the per-drain _cache). Add bounded polling in the
per-surface evaluation loop of CheckpointEngine.drain (engine.py ~lines 158-173):

  For each surface in observable_here:
    if e.within and surface == Surface.UI:
        error = _poll_until_pass(read, surface, e, check_fn, within=e.within)
    else:
        actuals = get_actuals(surface)            # unchanged; cached single read
        error = check_fn(e.expected, actuals, surface, e.tag)
    # existing pass / WARN-drop / FAIL-raise handling is UNCHANGED below this point.

  check_fn is check_present_consistent or check_absent selected by e.kind, as today.

  _poll_until_pass(read, surface, e, check_fn, within):
    - parse within ("10s"/"500ms") to seconds via an ENGINE-LOCAL helper (regex (\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(s|ms);
      do NOT import scn.ui — engine must stay browser-agnostic / playwright-free).
    - deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds; interval = 0.5s (constant).
    - loop: actuals = read(surface)   # FRESH read each iteration — BYPASS _cache so live DOM is
                                       # re-captured (read_current re-reads self._current_card).
            err = check_fn(e.expected, actuals, surface, e.tag)
            if err is None: return None
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline: return err   # last error
            time.sleep(interval)
    - On timeout the returned err flows into the EXISTING severity handling: FAIL → AssertionError;
      WARN → record warning + drop surface (so it does not dangle). No new branch needed.

  within is honored ONLY for Surface.UI. For non-UI surfaces a set within is ignored (single
  cached read) — document this; §4.5 scopes the poll to the UI surface.

== 4. RECONCILING LIVE UI OBSERVATION WITH THE SNAPSHOT RULE (§4.2) ==
No conflict — the snapshot rule governs the EXPECTED side only. e.expected is frozen at enqueue
(e.g. created.status="In Progress" pinned BEFORE verify(on=UI)), and stays immutable. The ACTUAL
side is what within re-captures: each poll iteration re-reads the live card and compares it to the
immutable snapshot until the card converges (status icon becomes "In Progress") or the timeout
fires. The snapshot is the stationary target; the live read is the moving actual. This is the
entire purpose of within and is fully consistent with §4.2. (Same discipline as the journey's
DOC/SHEET pins: pin the ai, then enqueue, so the snapshot captures the intended post-gesture state.)

== 5. REPLACE D2 DIRECT ASSERTIONS WITH QUEUE-ROUTED verify(on=UI) (tests/test_journey.py) ==
Current D2 (test_journey.py ~line 220-222, inside the `if _act4_done:` block):

    created.status = "In Progress"
    # D2: verify(on=UI) not implemented — direct card assertion covers the same intent
    scn.expect_alt(scn.ui.locate(alt="In Progress", next=True), "In Progress")
    scn.verify(created, on=SHEET, at=INTEGRITY)
    scn.checkpoint(INTEGRITY)

    scn.ui.set_status(card, "In Progress")
    created.status = "In Progress"
    scn.verify(created, on=UI, within="10s")            # enqueue; bounded live poll
    scn.checkpoint(STEP, on=frozenset({Surface.UI}))    # drain UI live, in-browser (no INTEGRITY)
    scn.verify(created, on=SHEET, at=INTEGRITY)         # durable async sheet → defer
    scn.checkpoint(INTEGRITY)                           # docx+xlsx+tracker+consistency (UI excluded)

title: [FIX] Dirty flag re-set after sync due to WriteGuard cross-execution gap
description: After WebApp doPost writes to the sheet and clears Dirty, the onActionSheetEdit trigger fires in a separate GAS execution. The SYNC_IN_PROGRESS script property already exists as a cross-execution guard but is not being set/cleared correctly in the WebApp write path. Fix: ensure SYNC_IN_PROGRESS is set before WebApp writes to the sheet and cleared after, so onActionSheetEdit skips the re-stamp.

Also verify document title consistency: the ActionSheet Document column HYPERLINK display text must match the current document title (from docTitle passed on sync). This catches gts-8in (title not refreshed on existing rows).

This is not optional cleanup — it's part of test design from inception. For UC-C specifically, the 3-way consistency check (floating action ↔ ActionSheet ↔ tracker table across all fields) is a primary responsibility. Create a shared consistency helper (e.g., verify_consistency()) usable by all UC tests. Document the pattern in test module docstring so future tests follow it automatically. title: Process: AC postconditions must be operationalized as reconciliation invariants
description: Related to gts-1ar: UC-B AC language in docs/CONTEXT.md has informal postconditions ('Both authoritative sides match') but operationalized AC bullets that are mutation-scoped. This split allows test design to choose either interpretation. Solution: when writing UC acceptance criteria, postconditions must be expressed as verifiable invariants (e.g., 'every floating action in the doc and its corresponding ActionSheet row agree on action text and status') so tests derive naturally from them. For each UC that involves sync or state mutation, the AC postcondition should explicitly require full-state agreement (or named invariants that require full-state checks). This applies retroactively to UC-A, UC-B, and must be baked into UC-C/UC-D AC before fixtures are written.
close_reason: Closed

title: Defect: UC-B tests verify mutations, not full-state reconciliation
description: UC-B test suite (test_uc_b.py) validates that specific mutations propagate correctly but does NOT verify comprehensive state consistency. Tests check 'did Variant 1 status change from Open to Done?' but not 'do ALL floating actions, ALL ActionSheet rows, and (for UC-C) ALL tracker table rows have consistent data across all fields?' Consistency includes: assignee (email + name match), action text, status, NamedRangeId, ID, Assigned Date, Last Modified — not just text/status. Current tests find 6 rows and check 3 specific mutations; they never verify that all 6 rows are consistent on all fields, or that every floating action is represented, or that no orphaned rows exist. This is mutation verification (sufficient for catching implementation bugs in specific fields) but insufficient for detecting state corruption (row dropped, field drifted on unmutated action, orphaned rows). Root cause: AC language allows mutation-scoped implementation; test design inherited that scope. Staged LL file: docs/lessons-learned/2026-05-25-test-mutation-verification-vs-state-reconciliation.md
notes: Discovered during review of test strategy for UC-C/D. Root cause analysis in gts-j5u. Test design gate in gts-qea blocks UC-C and UC-D implementation.
close_reason: Closed

title: [IMP] Preserve inline character formatting (bold/italic) round-trip in action text
description:
Same objective as gts-dr8j, next increment: an author's formatting carries meaning, and action text should read in the spreadsheet the way it was written in the doc. gts-dr8j established that for soft returns (line structure); this covers inline CHARACTER formatting — bold and italic at minimum, with underline/strikethrough as candidates — surviving doc -> sheet -> doc.

Today every path is plain-string. Both directions need work:

SCAN (doc -> sheet). Both parsers read para.getText() (SyncManager.js _parseParagraphAsFloatingAction, _parseSoftReturnParagraphActions), which returns characters with no style information. Style is available — DocumentApp via editAsText().isBold(offset)/isItalic(offset), or the REST GET the flush path already performs, where each element.textRun carries a textStyle. Note the flush GET is already fetched per-doc (_FLUSH_FIELDS) and may be the cheaper source.

STORE (sheet). Action text is written with setValue() at every site (WebApp.js _handleUpsertActionRows / _handleSyncActionRows, and _normalizeActionText returns a plain string). Sheets supports per-run styling via RichTextValue (setRichTextValue/getRichTextValue), which is the natural durable store and is what makes the formatting visible to a human reading the sheet — the actual point of the bead.

FLUSH (sheet -> doc). THE CRUX, and the direct analogue of the space-collapse gts-dr8j removed: _actionTextStyleRequest (SyncManager.js:1761) applies a UNIFORM updateTextStyle across the entire action-text range with explicit 'bold: !!cfg.bold, italic: !!cfg.italic' and fields='bold,italic,underline,foregroundColor,weightedFontFamily'. Any inline formatting the scan preserved is flattened by this single request on every flush. Preserving inline runs in the sheet is worthless until this is resolved — exactly why gts-dr8j blocked gts-dou2 rather than the reverse.

Entry points affected: every flush call site funnelling through _buildFlushRequests (sidebar status-set, preview-card status tap, syncDocument batch, sheetWins in _handleSyncActionRows), plus _applyActionFragment (EditorAddonCard.js) on the chip-insert/import path, which builds the same fragment independently.
design:
Open questions for the implementer:

1. How do the Config-sourced uniform style (gts-d99c, _actionTextStyleRequest) and per-run inline formatting compose? Candidates: (a) Config sets the BASE style, emitted first, with inline runs applied after as narrower updateTextStyle requests; (b) drop bold/italic from the Config uniform request's 'fields' mask so it no longer asserts them, letting inline runs own those attributes; (c) treat Config style as authoritative and accept that inline formatting is lost. This is the decision the bead lives or dies on — resolve it before writing code, and note (b) changes existing gts-d99c behavior, so check whether any test asserts uniform bold/italic today.

2. What is the representation in transit? The doPost payload is JSON and actionText is a bare string. Inline runs need a shape — e.g. actionText plus a parallel runs:[{start,end,bold,italic}] array — which is a CONTRACT CHANGE (ContractSchema.js) affecting upsert_action_rows / sync_action_rows and their ATDD test routes. Prefer an additive optional field so an older client keeps working.

3. Where does identity comparison land? _rowIdentityKey (WebApp.js) and the doc-vs-sheet action-text comparisons in VerifySync.js and TrackerTable.js _trackerRowsMatch all compare plain strings, and gts-dr8j had to normalize line-break SPELLING at all three to stop spurious mismatches. Decide explicitly whether formatting participates in row identity/consistency (a bolded word changing should probably not orphan a row or force a tracker re-render) — likely: compare plain text only, carry formatting as payload.

4. Which surfaces render it? The tracker table renders action text into cells via DocumentApp (TrackerTable.js), and the sidebar / preview / board-listing cards render HTML. Each needs a decision: honour the formatting, or deliberately flatten. Flattening is acceptable if stated, but should not be silent.

5. Test oracle: mostly SPECIFIABLE (a bold run over a known offset range is a precise assertion), so test-first per the oracle-ordering rule. The .docx reader already added for gts-dr8j (tests/helpers/doc_inspect.py paragraph_texts_with_breaks) is the model: read w:b / w:i on the runs rather than trusting para.text. The Config-composition question in (1) may warrant a Slice review since 'looks right' is partly perceptual — justify if chosen.

6. Scope discipline: bold/italic first. Colour, font family, size, links, and highlight are a much larger surface (and collide with the chip link + badge styling _buildFlushRequests already applies) — funnel them, do not pull them in.
acceptance_criteria:
- An action authored in a doc with a bold and an italic span inside its action text shows that formatting in the Actions sheet cell (RichTextValue or agreed equivalent), not as plain text.
- A flush triggered afterwards (sidebar status-set, and separately a syncDocument batch flush) leaves the doc's inline formatting intact — the spans still bold/italic over the same words, not uniformly styled and not stripped, verified by reading the exported .docx runs rather than plain text.
- Round trip is idempotent: scan -> flush -> rescan yields the same spans, so repeated syncs do not degrade formatting.
- A bolded word changing does not orphan the sheet row, mark it Dirty forever, or force a tracker re-render on every sync (question 3 resolved and covered).
- The Config-sourced action-text style (gts-d99c) still applies as its ADR/AC intends; whatever composition rule question 1 settles on is documented and asserted.
- Proven-to-fail: each new formatting assertion is demonstrated failing against a build that flattens the formatting, per the project backstop rule — a green-only assertion is unverified here for the same reason it was for gts-dr8j.
- Paired [TST] bead created at AC freeze per the twin-ticket rule.

comments.author: Stuart Donaldson
comments.text:
Design question 1 partly resolved empirically (2026-07-26), while the gts-dr8j context was still warm. Two findings:

1. THE CRUX IS CONDITIONAL ON CONFIG — this reframes severity. _readActionFormatConfig (SyncManager.js:1671) initialises 'result = { aiToken: _DEFAULT_AI_TOKEN_STYLE, actionText: null }' and only populates actionText when a Config sheet row with key 'action_text' exists. _actionTextStyleRequest then opens with 'if (!cfg) return null'. So in the DEFAULT configuration the uniform updateTextStyle is never emitted, and inline formatting would likely survive a flush untouched. The flattening only bites for users who have configured an action_text Config row. Consequences: (a) severity is lower than the description implies, but the failure is WORSE for being conditional — formatting silently survives for most users and is destroyed for configured ones, which is the kind of bug that gets reported as 'intermittent'; (b) the test matrix must cover BOTH Config states, and a test written only against a default-config fixture would pass while the real defect ships. Verify this null path before relying on it.

2. NOTHING TESTS THE UNIFORM STYLE TODAY. Grepping tests/ for bold|italic returns nothing on action text, and no test file references d99c / configFormat / action_format at all. So gts-d99c's action-text styling is entirely uncovered. This cuts two ways: option (b) below breaks no existing test, but there is also no recorded executable intent to check a change against — the 'check whether any test asserts uniform bold/italic today' step in the design field is answered, and the answer is 'no test does, and that is its own coverage gap'. Under the entry-point coverage invariant that gap arguably wants its own [TST] bead; not filed, flagging for a human call.

RECOMMENDATION on the composition rule: option (b) — drop 'bold,italic' from the Config request's fields mask so it stops asserting those two attributes, letting inline runs own them, while Config keeps owning colour/font/size/underline. Rationale: it is the smallest change that makes the two features compose rather than compete, it needs no ordering guarantees between requests (unlike (a), where a base-then-override sequence has to be provably ordered inside one batchUpdate), and it preserves the visual intent of gts-d99c for every attribute a user actually configures action_text for. Cost: a user who set bold:true expecting ALL action text bold loses that; given finding 2, no test asserts it, but this IS a behavior change to a shipped feature and should be confirmed with the developer, not assumed.

title: [TST] verify_consistency doc_name oracle reads .docx core_properties.title, not the real title
description:
scn/session.py:596-614 (verify_consistency, Surface.SHEET) resolves the document's 'actual current title' from the exported .docx core_properties.title:

    current_title = docx.Document(io.BytesIO(docx_bytes)).core_properties.title or None

Google Docs' .docx export does not carry the real document title into that core property — it comes back as the literal placeholder 'Word Document'. The gts-k1g9 staleness check then compares the sheet's cached doc_name (the correct Drive filename) against that placeholder and always fails:

    AssertionError: col7 document_formula doc_name stale for '<docId>/AI-10':
      expected='Word Document', actual='GActionSheet-Test-journey-20260726-f0b1'

This is an oracle bug, not a product bug: the assertion cannot pass regardless of what the code does, because the value it treats as ground truth is a constant. Found while establishing the gts-dr8j regression baseline (2026-07-26); it is the sole cause of the current test_journey failure and was already red in the 2026-07-24 full run.

Note the check it replaced (doc_name merely non-null) was weaker but at least satisfiable. Whatever replaces this must actually be able to observe a rename.
design: Which oracle? DriveApp/Drive API file name is the authoritative title and already reachable from the harness; a GAS test-support route returning DocumentApp.getName() is another option. Confirm whether any other assertion in the suite depends on core_properties.title before changing the reader.
acceptance_criteria: verify_consistency's doc_name comparison sources the document's current title from an oracle that reflects real renames (e.g. the Drive API file name, or a GAS test route returning DocumentApp.getName()) rather than .docx core_properties.title. test_journey's col7 assertion passes on an unrenamed doc AND is demonstrated to fail on a doc renamed after its sheet row was written — proving the staleness check gts-k1g9 wanted still has teeth.

title: [FIX] Insert true soft returns (Shift+Enter) via Docs REST API on flush
description:
Flush (sheet->doc write) uses the Docs REST API's batchUpdate/insertText
directly (SyncManager.js:_buildFlushRequests), not the higher-level
DocumentApp service. Multi-line action text (soft-return continuation
lines, e.g. "action text\nline 2") must currently be flattened to a single
space before insertText, because:

- A bare \n in insertText's text field creates a new paragraph (hard
  return) — confirmed, documented Docs API behavior.
- A bare \r or \v is silently dropped by insertText, concatenating lines
  with NO separator at all — confirmed by prior testing, see gts-kkm7.5's
  description: "the raw \r/\v characters aren't meaningful to the Docs
  REST API's insertText ... so they're silently dropped on reinsertion."

This means gts-dou2 (soft-return continuation lines collapsed to spaces in
action text) is not worth fixing at the sheet-storage layer alone: the
scan side already correctly preserves soft returns per-paragraph (AI-N:
token to end of paragraph, _parseSoftReturnParagraphActions), but nothing
is gained unless the write-back (flush) side can actually reinsert a real
soft return into the doc via the REST API. Confirmed with the user
(2026-07-25) that this is the actual goal — round-trip fidelity, not just
sheet display.

Entry points affected: any flush call site that funnels through
_buildFlushRequests (sidebar status-set, preview-card status tap,
syncDocument's batch flush, sheetWins path in _handleSyncActionRows).
design:
Open questions for the implementer:
1. Does the Docs API v1 public REST surface support inserting a soft line
   break at all? (No lineBreak structural element appears in the public
   Paragraph.elements schema as of last check — this may require finding
   the correct character/encoding, or may be a genuine API gap.)
2. If a specific Unicode character is the right encoding for a soft
   return in insertText's text field, what is it, and why did the
   previous attempt with \v/\r (gts-kkm7.5) get silently dropped instead
   of working? Was that attempt technically correct but done at a time
   when the text had already been mangled upstream, or is \v genuinely
   not accepted by insertText?
3. If no direct insertText-based mechanism exists, what's the fallback:
   e.g. structuring the request as multiple insertText/insertPageBreak-
   style requests per line with explicit index bookkeeping, or dropping
   to the older DocumentApp service for this specific write (mixing
   REST batchUpdate and DocumentApp in the same flush is currently
   avoided for performance/batching reasons per gts-kkm7 epic — would
   need to weigh that tradeoff explicitly if DocumentApp turns out to be
   the only working path).
4. Verify empirically against a real test doc before committing to an
   approach — this is a perceptual/empirical question about undocumented
   or under-documented API behavior, not something to resolve by reading
   docs alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- A working Docs REST API v1 batchUpdate mechanism is identified (and
  proven against a live test doc, not just documentation) that inserts a
  genuine soft line break (Shift+Enter) within a single paragraph —
  distinguishable from a hard paragraph break, and matching what
  DocumentApp/getText() reports as a soft return (\r or \v depending on
  runtime) when the doc is rescanned afterward.
- _buildFlushRequests (SyncManager.js) is updated to use this mechanism
  instead of _normalizeActionText's space-collapse, for multi-line
  actionText.
- Round-trip test: doc has AI-N: action with soft-return continuation
  lines -> sync (scan doc->sheet, preserving newlines per gts-dou2) ->
  trigger a flush (e.g. sidebar status change) -> rescan the doc and
  confirm the paragraph still has the original soft-return line breaks
  (not hard paragraph breaks, not concatenated with no separator, not
  flattened to spaces).
- gts-dou2's three tests plus this new flush round-trip test all pass.
- gts-kkm7.5 can be closed or superseded by this bead once resolved.
close_reason: Resolved: U+000B (vertical tab) is the Docs REST insertText soft-line-break character. \r is stripped per InsertTextRequest's documented U+000C-U+001F range (the real cause of gts-kkm7.5); \n creates a new Paragraph; U+000B is in neither bucket. Implemented in _toSoftReturnText + _buildFlushRequests, with three consuming sites hardened. Proven on a live doc plus two negative controls. Committed d65c472 on fix/gts-dr8j-soft-returns. regression=verified: zero new failures vs baseline.

comments.author: Stuart Donaldson
comments.text:

Mechanism: U+000B (vertical tab) is the soft-line-break char for insertText. Per InsertTextRequest's docs, control chars U+0000-U+0008 and U+000C-U+001F are stripped — \r (U+000D) is inside that range, which is the real reason the gts-kkm7.5 attempt lost the breaks; \n creates a new Paragraph; U+000B is in neither bucket. Proven on a live doc plus two deployed-and-reverted negative controls.

title: [INF] Live wall-clock timestamps for pytest test start/finish
description:
Full-suite pytest runs (test:full) currently only allow reconstructing per-test timing after the fact from junit.xml (suite-level timestamp + per-test duration, summed serially). There is no live timestamp in the raw run log, and no correlation hook to GAS/Axiom-side logs. Add pytest hooks to tests/conftest.py that print wall-clock start/finish timestamps per test to stdout, so a captured run log (per project convention: route long-running test output to a file, not tail) carries real timestamps without post-hoc reconstruction.

## Context
Requested after evaluating test-full-run.txt (2026-07-24 full-suite run, 11 failures): timeline had to be reconstructed by summing junit.xml per-test durations from the suite-level start timestamp to determine whether failures clustered (single outage) or were scattered (recurring flake). That reconstruction only works because tests run serially; it should be a first-class capability.
acceptance_criteria: Running pnpm run test:full and inspecting the captured log shows a wall-clock timestamp (e.g. HH:MM:SS) on both the start and finish/outcome line of every test. Timestamps are also still available in junit.xml (unchanged). No change to test pass/fail behavior.
close_reason: Added pytest_runtest_logstart/logfinish hooks in tests/conftest.py, writing HH:MM:SS timestamps via terminalreporter (bypasses capture, no -s needed). Verified against tests/test_ai_n_token.py.

title: [FIX] created_date format/timezone mismatch on SHEET surface
description:
scn/assertions.py:144 compares created_date via exact string equality. Expected value is ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds + 'Z' (JS-generated, e.g. '2026-07-25T04:50:05.110Z'); actual value read from SHEET is space-separated, no 'Z', 6-digit microseconds, and exactly 7 hours earlier (UTC->PDT offset), e.g. '2026-07-24 21:50:05.110000' -- looks like a Python datetime str() of a naive local-time value from the SheetReader. Fails every time created_date is asserted on SHEET.

## Context
Surfaced by full-suite run test-full-run.txt (2026-07-24 21:49-21:50). Both failures show the identical 7-hour offset and format pattern, so this is deterministic, not flaky.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_sidebar.py::test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync and test_tracker_insert_button pass; created_date read from SHEET is normalized to the same ISO-8601 UTC format used elsewhere (or the comparison normalizes both sides) before exact-match comparison.
close_reason: Fixed: scn/surfaces.py keeps SHEET created_date/modified_date as raw datetime; scn/assertions.py normalizes both sides (America/Los_Angeles-naive xlsx datetime vs ISO-8601 UTC string) to UTC before comparing. Verified: unit suite green, live test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync + test_tracker_insert_button pass.

title: [FIX] Soft-return continuation lines collapsed to spaces in action text
description:
Floating-action scanner joins soft-return (Shift+Enter) continuation lines with a space instead of preserving the newline when writing/reading action text. Reproduced deterministically (not flaky) by 3 tests in tests/test_floating_action_scanner.py: test_soft_return_continuation_in_action_text, test_soft_return_bare_ai_with_continuation, test_soft_return_context_and_multiline_action. Expected e.g. 'action text\ncontinuation line', actual 'action text continuation line' after sync to SHEET.

## Context
Surfaced by full-suite run test-full-run.txt (2026-07-24 21:33-21:35), all three tests fail identically on the same run. Root cause suspected in the doc-scan or sheet-write join logic (likely Array.join(' ') where '\n' is expected).
acceptance_criteria: All three test_soft_return_* tests in tests/test_floating_action_scanner.py pass; action text round-trips through doc->sheet sync with embedded newlines preserved (not collapsed to spaces).
notes: Blocked on gts-dr8j: preserving newlines in the sheet alone has no value without a working flush-side (sheet->doc) soft-return reinsertion mechanism. Confirmed with user 2026-07-25. Sheet-write change reverted; only the harmless _normalizeLineEndings dedup refactor (SyncManager.js/WebApp.js) remains in the tree, uncommitted.
close_reason: Fixed by gts-dr8j (commit d65c472): WebApp.js _normalizeActionText now preserves the line break and normalizes only its spelling, which was only safe once flush could reinsert a real soft return. All three test_soft_return_* tests pass — they were failing at the 2026-07-24 baseline and pass now.

title: Notes for Stuart follow-ups
description: This bead collects notes for follow-ups that will hopefully not polute or convolute the list of beads when looking for what is ready to act on.
notes:
Lesson groupings to scan for - User/Group directory management
- OAuth experience when stale
- Testing file access / group membership given external email
bd-run-beads test gate ran the full 331-test regression suite (mostly live-Google E2E, ~30s/test) unconditionally after a test-only [TST] bead (gts-79dw.4.2) that added one new xfail-only test file with zero production code changes. Cost ~1hr of wasted wait/kill-and-retry, plus masked the real issue (stale .auth/user.json Playwright cookie -> 401s) under 'looks hung'. Follow-up: figure out whether bd-run-beads/pytest gate should (a) scope the gate to changed-area tests for TST-only/low-risk beads with the full suite deferred to a merge-gate step, (b) surface *why* a long/blanket regression run is warranted before spending the time (should have been explicit, per CLAUDE.md's oracle-ordering + backstop rules, not a silent blanket default), and (c) fail fast / distinguish 'slow but progressing' from 'stalled' in the runner's own output so a human doesn't have to reverse-engineer a dot-string to tell them apart. Investigate bd-run-beads.py gate config options and whether a lighter default gate is safe under the twin-ticket/entry-point-coverage invariant.
Correction/detail on the above: bd-run-beads.py's auto-detect gate (script lines ~354-364) has no per-bead scoping logic at all -- it just probes for a working whole-suite 'pytest -q' invocation and uses that unconditionally for every bead. It does accept an explicit override (-t/--test-cmd, '' to disable) but nothing in the tool chooses that override based on bead type/risk -- a human has to pass it. Separately: the SECOND full-regression run in that session (the one killed after ~7min) was not the tool's doing -- at that point the orchestrator wasn't running at all; I (the agent) was manually finishing the bead by hand and chose to mirror the tool's default full-suite gate instead of scoping to the change, for a test-only bead with zero production code touched. That was my own bad default, not bd-run-beads.py's. Two distinct fixes to consider: (1) give bd-run-beads.py bead-type-aware default scoping (e.g. TST-only beads with no src/ diff could default to a narrower gate, or at least print why the full suite is warranted before running it), (2) agent-side: don't reflexively reuse a tool's blanket gate command when manually finishing a bead -- scope to what changed unless there's a stated reason not to.

title: [INF] Provision NUUC-Dispatch GCP project + OAuth Web client (Spike S1)
description:
Operator GCP-console tasks that BLOCK Spike S1 (gts-79dw.1). Split out of
gts-hc6v on 2026-07-21/22: hc6v provisions the EXISTING GActionSheet GCP project
(cloud-logging-test-494622) for ADR-0017 Phase 2 chip-link editing only. Spike S1 needs a
SEPARATE, standalone GCP project because (a) the OAuth consent-screen User Type is
project-wide -- Internal (Workspace-org-only) vs External (any Google account) can't coexist,
and GActionSheet's add-on install story depends on staying Internal/private while Spike S1
needs External+Published; (b) the Workspace Marketplace SDK is one-per-GCP-project, so a
second published surface can't share GActionSheet's project. See
knowledge-base/references/workspace-addon-setup.md and docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md.

This new project hosts NUUC-Dispatch, a standalone Apps Script Web App (not a Workspace
Add-on) scoped for now to Spike S1's identity-verification harness only.

1) Create a new GCP project (separate from cloud-logging-test-494622).
2) Enable Apps Script API (and Workspace Add-ons API only if ever needed later -- not
   required for a plain Web App).
3) OAuth consent screen: User type External, publishing status In production/Published,
   scopes openid + email (profile optional). Non-sensitive scopes => no Google
   verification/security review.
4) OAuth 2.0 Client ID, type 'Web application', in this new GCP project. Register the
   sdonaldson-nl.github.io origin as an Authorized JavaScript origin (GIS sign-in from
   NUUC-Static/pub/AS/index.html runs there).
5) Create the NUUC-Dispatch Apps Script project (clasp create, standalone) and bind it to
   this new GCP project (Apps Script editor -> Project Settings -> change GCP project).
6) Store GIS_CLIENT_ID in NUUC-Dispatch's Script Properties (deploy:test). GIS_CLIENT_SECRET
   only needed later if Milestone 1 moves off pure GIS ID-token verification to a
   server-side code exchange -- not required for Spike S1's tokeninfo-based verify.
7) Provide the resulting scriptId + GIS_CLIENT_ID back so NUUC-Dispatch/.clasp.json and
   NUUC-Static/pub/AS/index.html's placeholder client-id constant can be filled in.

Repo scaffolding (NUUC-Dispatch GAS project, NUUC-Static/pub/AS static harness) is done in
parallel and does not block on this -- see NUUC-Dispatch/SETUP.md for the human-facing version
of this same checklist.
acceptance_criteria: New GCP project created (separate from cloud-logging-test-494622); Apps Script API enabled; OAuth consent screen External + Published, scopes openid/email; OAuth 2.0 Web application client with sdonaldson-nl.github.io registered as an Authorized JavaScript origin; NUUC-Dispatch Apps Script project bound to this GCP project; GIS_CLIENT_ID present in NUUC-Dispatch deploy:test Script Properties.

title: [INF] Spike S2: verify a gmail/external email's read/write access to a board folder/doc, incl. domain-managed group
description:
SPIKE (throwaway, gating). Prove the deployer-context backend can determine, for a VERIFIED external @gmail (from Spike S1), whether it has READ vs WRITE access to the board FOLDER (not just the individual doc) — CRITICALLY including access conferred only through a DOMAIN-MANAGED Google Group whose member is external. This is the load-bearing unknown for the folder-scoped ACL (requirements R3/R4/R5/R7). Full plan + assumptions A4/A5/A6: docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md sections 2 and 6. Supersedes the per-document, deployer-vs-user-scope framing in the sibling build bead gts-1hyh, which it blocks.

Harness: reuse Spike S1's static page + verified email. Page calls doPost route spike_check_access, text/plain body { email, folderId, docId }. Backend (deployer context) computes:
  folderAccess = DriveApp.getFolderById(folderId).getAccess(email)
  docAccess    = DriveApp.getFileById(docId).getAccess(email)
Same SPIKE_ENABLED gate + deploy:test as S1.

Test matrix (seed each state on the real board folder first):
  (a) external email w/ direct VIEW on folder  -> expect VIEW
  (b) external email w/ direct EDIT on folder   -> expect EDIT
  (c) external email NO direct grant but MEMBER of a domain-managed Google Group holding VIEW/EDIT -> expect VIEW/EDIT  [THE case]
  (d) external email w/ nothing -> expect NONE
  (e) folder link-shared 'anyone with link' -> observe whether getAccess over-grants

Fallback (only if (c) returns NONE/unknown): Drive.Permissions.list(folderId) to find type:'group' grants + roles, then AdminDirectory.Members.hasMember(groupKey, externalEmail) per matching group (works for external members BECAUSE the group is domain-managed). Enable Admin SDK Directory advanced service.
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Entry point: doPost action 'spike_check_access' (body { email, folderId, docId }), SPIKE_ENABLED-gated.
(2) Completion log tag: GasLogger 'webapp.spike.access' with data { folderAccess, docAccess, method } (method = 'getAccess' | 'adminSdk').
(3) Output schema: JSON { email, folderId, docId, folderAccess:'NONE|VIEW|COMMENT|EDIT|OWNER', docAccess:same, method:'getAccess|adminSdk', groupExpandUsed:boolean }.
Cap mapping under test (A6): VIEW/COMMENT => read tier; EDIT/OWNER => write tier (sync). Safe default = DENY when access cannot be positively confirmed.
Inherited open question from gts-1hyh: deployer must be able to READ the folder's effective access — validate this holds for the board folder the deployer owns/can see (it should, unlike arbitrary end-user docs).
Fail path: if neither getAccess nor Admin-SDK fallback resolves case (c), the folder-scoped domain-group model (R3/R7) is NOT achievable as specified — record and fall back options: per-doc getAccess, explicit allowlist, or require direct (non-group) sharing.
acceptance_criteria: A definitive, REPRODUCIBLE read/write/none verdict for an external @gmail whose ONLY access is via a domain-managed group (case c) — either from getAccess directly or the Admin-SDK fallback. Cases (a),(b),(d) return the expected access level. Case (e) does NOT silently grant access to a non-member (negative). Result (pass/fail per A4,A5,A6) + which method resolved case (c) recorded in docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md.
notes: Unblocked 2026-07-22: NUUC-Dispatch ND-9es (Spike S1) PASSED — all four assumptions A1/A2/A3/A7 confirmed, RESULT block in docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md §5. S1 harness (https://nuuc-it.github.io/Static/pub/AS/) and verified-identity backend are live on NUUC-Dispatch TEST and reusable for this spike.
close_reason: Spike S2 PASS. Load-bearing case (c) confirmed: getAccess() alone does NOT expand group membership (A4 refuted as literally stated), but the Admin SDK fallback (Drive.Permissions.list + AdminDirectory.Members.get, not .hasMember which rejects external memberKeys) correctly resolves group-conferred access for an external @gmail member of a domain-managed group, tested against the real Communications Shared Drive. Cases (a)/(b)/(d) also PASS. Case (e) blocked by Drive policy at the Shared Drive root (informative negative, not a failure) — deferred, non-blocking. Gate (§7) cleared; GTaskSheet-1hyh unblocked. Full result + gotchas: docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md §6, knowledge-base/references/gas-admin-directory-external-groups.md.

title: [INF] Spike S1: verifiable Google identity from a static GitHub Pages page via GAS doGet/doPost
description:
SPIKE (throwaway, gating). Prove a static page on a genuinely different origin (github.io) can obtain a VERIFIABLE Google identity for a personal @gmail AND an external account, and that GAS (deployer context) can verify it. De-risks the static-first-party + GIS architecture that would REVISE ADR-0017 (which currently chooses auth-code redirect on /exec, external host rejected). Full plan + assumptions A1/A2/A3/A7: docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md sections 2 and 5.

Harness: one static index.html published via GitHub Pages (spike repo or gh-pages branch; a dedicated static-only repo is a LATER concern). Page runs GIS 'Sign in with Google', obtains an ID token (scopes: openid email), then calls our WebApp two ways to exercise BOTH interfaces cross-origin:
  - doPost route spike_verify_identity, text/plain body { idToken }
  - doGet ?cmd=spike_verify_identity&idToken=...
Backend verifies via https://oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo?id_token=... (UrlFetchApp), checks aud==our client id, iss, exp, and returns { verified, sub, email, email_verified }.

Spike GAS routes MUST sit behind a SPIKE_ENABLED flag (default false, like PROBE.js) so they cannot expose in a real deployment. Deploy with 'pnpm run deploy:test' (never clasp directly). Uses text/plain bodies to stay a CORS simple request (A7).
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Entry points: doPost action 'spike_verify_identity' (body { idToken }); doGet cmd 'spike_verify_identity' (?idToken=). Both gated by SPIKE_ENABLED, bypassing WEBAPP_SECRET (external caller has no secret).
(2) Completion log tag: GasLogger 'webapp.spike.identity' with data { verified, hasSub, emailVerified } (never log the raw token).
(3) Output schema: JSON { verified:boolean, sub:string, email:string, email_verified:boolean, aud_ok:boolean, iss_ok:boolean, exp_ok:boolean }.
CORS check (A1): confirm BOTH hops (/exec -> script.googleusercontent.com) return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * from the github.io origin. Verify from the real browser, not file://.
Open decision recorded, not resolved here: tokeninfo endpoint (simple, low-volume) vs local JWKS/RS256 (higher volume) — spike uses tokeninfo.
Fail path: if consent/verification friction appears for external accounts, or a CORS hop blocks, STOP and re-open static-vs-/exec-auth-code (ADR-0017) — record which assumption failed in the plan doc.
acceptance_criteria: Backend logs+returns a VERIFIED email+sub for (a) a personal @gmail and (b) an external (non-northlakeuu.org) account, with aud/iss/exp all validated. description:

title: [INF] UC-C/D reconciliation spec approval + CLAUDE.md reconciliation-discipline rule
description:
Carries forward item 4 of gts-mpi9 (closed 2026-06-18 without this item -- deliberately deferred, not converted to a tracked issue at the time). LL source: docs/lessons-learned/resolved/2026-05-25-test-mutation-verification-vs-state-reconciliation.md. Root cause: UC-B/UC-C/UC-D acceptance criteria state postconditions as informal prose ('both sides match') rather than falsifiable state invariants, so test design (delta-proof: inject mutation, verify it reached the destination) never grew a full reconciliation pass. The docTitle/docName staleness code defect embedded in the same LL is already fixed separately (gts-8in, closed; verified in src/WebApp.js:923-941 the doc-wins branch unconditionally refreshes the HYPERLINK formula).

2026-07-02 investigation: confirmed CLAUDE.md and implementation-gate SKILL.md have zero reconciliation-discipline content (grep clean) -- BUT this is not a green-field gap. Three existing mechanisms already cover most of it:
1. scn/session.py:626 verify_all_expectations() + scn/assertions.py:27 check_present_consistent() -- the real cross-surface consistency checker. Per-action, compares DOC+SHEET(+TRACKER) and checks action text, action_id, status, assignee email, assignee_name (TRACKER only, deliberately -- DOC/SHEET store GAS-derived names that legitimately differ from directory names). This IS the mechanism the LL asked for, but (a) opt-in per action -- a test only gets the check for actions it explicitly hands to verify_all_expectations(), not a blanket sweep of everything in the doc, and (b) field coverage stops short of the LL's list: no NamedRangeId/globalId comparison, no Assigned Date/Last Modified comparison, no document-name check at all (the ai dataclass in scn/ai.py has no fields for any of these).
2. verify_consistency(scope=DOC) -- calls GAS verify_action_rows (checks ONE thing: DocData.teamId vs live Drive teamScope property -- team-scope drift, unrelated to action-field consistency) + verify_chip_integrity (checks doc-side chip RENDERING: status icon matches, globalId embedded in link, status token matches icon). Real integrity checking, but for rendering/team-scope correctness, not storage-location agreement.
3. verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) -- sweeps every row in the sheet unconditionally (not opt-in), but only asserts doc_name is non-null and sync_status isn't an error state -- does NOT check doc_name is CORRECT (matches the doc's current title), so it would not have caught the original stale-name-after-rename bug even today.

Net: the plumbing is ~90% there via verify_all_expectations. The real gap is narrower than 'write a reconciliation-discipline rule from scratch': (a) extend check_present_consistent/ai with the missing fields, (b) decide whether UC-C/D tests must call verify_all_expectations for every action touched (not just the one under test) to get full sweep coverage.
design:
Revised design (2026-07-02, performance-aware) -- supersedes the prior verify_all_expectations-for-every-action recommendation:

PERFORMANCE FINDING: engine.py's drain() (scn/engine.py:202-207) already memoizes surface reads per checkpoint via a local _cache dict -- get_actuals(surface) downloads DOC/SHEET/TRACKER at most once per drain() call regardless of how many expectations need that surface. BUT the CONSISTENCY obligation (scn/engine.py:250-258, read_consistency()) has NO equivalent memoization: it is called once per expectation with needs_consistency=True that isn't yet consistency_discharged, inside the same per-expectation for-loop (line 211). read_consistency() (scn/session.py:861-862) is a thin wrapper straight to self.verify_consistency() -- two live GAS HTTP round trips (verify_action_rows + verify_chip_integrity), no caching. So N verify_all_expectations() calls drained at the same INTEGRITY checkpoint currently cost N x 2 GAS round trips, not 1x -- a real, unintended cost multiplier already latent in the code, not yet biting because current test usage is disciplined (grep-verified: test_journey.py and test_journey_acts_1_3.py each call verify_all_expectations() exactly twice total, always immediately followed by a single checkpoint(INTEGRITY) -- i.e. the existing convention already matches 'one or two times, at/after the delta, not after every mutation'). My earlier recommendation to require verify_all_expectations() for every action a UC-C/D scenario touches would have exercised this latent N-multiplier directly and made it a real cost, contrary to the goal.

Revised plan, cheapest-and-safest first:
1. (Do this regardless of anything else) Memoize read_consistency() per drain() call the same way get_actuals is memoized -- a local flag/cache in drain() (scn/engine.py) so consistency is fetched at most once per checkpoint no matter how many expectations require it. This is a small, self-contained fix, independent of any convention decision, and removes the latent multiplier risk for good -- makes the mechanism safe to use more liberally later without a performance tradeoff forcing restraint.
2. Field extension (globalId/NamedRangeId, Assigned Date, Last Modified) to ai dataclass + check_present_consistent -- ZERO added network cost, since it only adds comparisons against data already present in the cached surface reads (get_actuals). Still recommended, unchanged from before.
3. Document-name-correctness check -- add to verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) (already a single per-call GAS-free artifact check, called explicitly by a test, not auto-fired per action) so it does not add an extra network round trip either -- cost is bounded by however many times a test calls verify_consistency() directly, which is already sparse by convention.
4. Testing convention: KEEP current discipline (verify_all_expectations 1-2x per test, at/after the delta) rather than expanding to 'every touched action' -- matches your steer that per-mutation consistency checks are unlikely to catch anything an end-of-scenario check wouldn't, and keeps runtime in check. UC-C/D tests should follow the same pattern test_journey.py already uses: deltas via verify()/set_status()/etc., ONE verify_all_expectations() call covering the net state before the closing INTEGRITY checkpoint (or two, if there's a meaningful mid-scenario state to pin), not one per action.
5. Open question narrowed: is (1) worth doing as a standalone perf fix now (independent of this issue), or bundled with (2)/(3) since they touch the same drain/consistency code path anyway? Recommend bundling -- same PR, same reviewer context.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) read_consistency() memoized per drain() call (engine.py), ai dataclass + check_present_consistent extended with globalId/dates (zero added network cost), SHEET-scope doc-name-correctness check added, and UC-C/D tests follow the existing 1-2-calls-per-test verify_all_expectations convention (not per-action); or (b) explicitly declined/deferred again with a dated rationale recorded on this issue.
close_reason: Superseded: bundled into twin-ticket pair GTaskSheet-k1g9 [INF] (implementation: memoize read_consistency() per drain, extend ai/check_present_consistent with globalId+dates, add SHEET doc-name-correctness check) + GTaskSheet-dxz3 [TST] (proof-of-effectiveness tests for all three). Performance finding (2026-07-02): read_consistency() is uncached per drain() unlike get_actuals -- would cost Nx GAS round trips if verify_all_expectations were called per-action as originally proposed; fixed at the mechanism level instead of expanding test-authoring convention. UC-C/D tests keep the existing 1-2-calls-per-test verify_all_expectations discipline, not per-action calls.

title: [INF] Oracle-driven ordering lever — prove then promote to DevStandard T23
description: Lever under test: 'ordering is oracle-driven; coverage-before-merge is the invariant.' A refinement of DevStandard T23 (review-fidelity phasing) that (a) separates test-first ORDERING (negotiable) from COVERAGE-before-merge (invariant), (b) sharpens the Slice trigger into the oracle test (specifiable vs perceptual), (c) adds the cost-asymmetry-is-diagnostic heuristic, (d) binds the three existing guardrails to the relaxed ordering. Deployed 2026-07-01 as project-local lever in: CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy, .claude/skills/implementation-gate/SKILL.md Step 4 (v2.2). Portable spec: docs/methodology/oracle-ordering-lever.md.

title: [FIX] Soft-return chars lost on sidebar status-set flush (doc-rescan path bypasses normalization)
description:
Pre-code contract:
- Bug: an action item with soft-return (Shift+Enter) continuation lines, e.g.
  "AI-12: first line\nSecond line\nThird line (In Progress)", renders correctly
  after a normal sync, but loses all line breaks after a sidebar status change
  -- becomes "AI-12: first lineSecond lineThird line (In Review)" with zero
  separator.
- Root cause: WebApp.js's _normalizeActionText() (added f8dc3a6, gts-2eui/755o)
  strips \v/\n/\r to a single space, but only at the four sheet-write call sites
  (_handleUpsertActionRows/_handleSyncActionRows insert+update). sidebarSetStatus
  (WorkspaceAddonCard.js) never touches the sheet -- it rescans the live doc via
  _scanFloatingActions -> _parseParagraphAsFloatingAction, which reads para.getText()
  raw (no normalization), and passes that actionText straight into
  _flushActionParagraphs. The raw \r/\v characters aren't meaningful to the Docs
  REST API's insertText (neither paragraph-break \n nor soft-break \v in this
  runtime's representation), so they're silently dropped on reinsertion.
- Fix: normalize actionText once inside _buildFlushRequests (SyncManager.js,
  gts-kkm7.3's new shared helper) using the same \v/\n/\r -> single-space
  collapse as WebApp.js's _normalizeActionText -- this is now the one chokepoint
  every flush call site (sidebar status-set, preview-card status tap, syncDocument's
  batch flush) passes through, so a single fix point covers all of them regardless
  of whether actionText came from the sheet (already normalized) or a live doc
  rescan (not yet normalized). Idempotent on already-normalized text.
- Completion log tag: flush.done (existing) -- no new tag needed, this is an
  input-sanitization fix, not a new code path.
- Output schema test will assert against: sidebarSetStatus (patch_action_status
  fast path) on an action whose doc paragraph has \v/\r soft-return continuation
  lines must, after the status-set flush, leave the doc paragraph as a single
  line with no missing separators (space-joined) -- not concatenated, not split
  into extra hard paragraphs.
close_reason: Superseded by gts-dr8j (commit d65c472), per that bead's AC. This bead's fix was to space-collapse actionText in _buildFlushRequests; gts-dr8j replaces that with a real soft return (U+000B). Its root-cause analysis was also half wrong: \r IS silently dropped by insertText (documented U+000C-U+001F stripping), but \v is not — it is the character that works.

title: [IMP] Batch chip-flush GET+batchUpdate per doc in _flushActionParagraph path
description:
Pre-code contract:
- Entry point: SyncManager.js syncDocument()'s flushIds loop (line ~233-238, also EditorAddonCard.js:474 and WorkspaceAddonCard.js:727 single-item call sites) currently calls _flushActionParagraph(docId, token, N, globalId, ...) once per changed action item, each doing its own GET (https://docs.googleapis.com/v1/documents/{docId}?fields=...) + its own :batchUpdate. Refactor to a single GET of the doc body per doc, locate paragraph indices for all toFlush action items from that one payload, build the combined requests[] array across all of them, submit one :batchUpdate.
- Keep the single-item call sites (EditorAddonCard.js:474, WorkspaceAddonCard.js:727 - interactive single-action edits) working via the same underlying batched function called with a one-element list, so there is one implementation, not two copies (reuse requirement).
- Completion log tag: flush.done - extend payload to report batchSize (number of action items flushed in that one GET+batchUpdate) alongside existing copies (paragraph occurrences), so a multi-item batched flush is distinguishable from a single-item one in Axiom traces.
- Output schema test will assert against: for a doc with N>1 action items all needing a flush in the same sync, (a) exactly one GET to docs.googleapis.com and one :batchUpdate fire for that doc, (b) every action item's paragraph (text, status icon, chip link) is updated correctly, matching today's per-call output, (c) a flush failure for one action item among N does not abort the others (existing _remarkRowDirty per-item retry behavior must be preserved per item, not per whole doc).

title: [IMP] Replace per-doc DriveApp trash/modified checks with single files.list pass
description:

title: [EPIC] Sync performance: batch per-doc REST calls
description:

  some contextual text

  Second line
  AI: My new action
  Another line

where each line break is a soft return (Shift+Enter, \n in DocumentApp getText()), keeping everything in a single paragraph element. The scanner currently misses all AI tokens that do not appear at the start of the paragraph, and cannot handle multiple AI tokens within one paragraph. This is a live regression: the user is authoring this pattern and sync produces no sheet rows.

AC-2: A single paragraph containing multiple AI tokens separated by soft returns (e.g. AI-1: ... 
 Second line 
 AI: ... 
 Another line) produces one sheet row per token after sync. The bare AI: token is assigned the next available N.
AC-3: Leading contextual text before the first AI token in the paragraph is not included in any action text and does not produce a sheet row of its own.
AC-4: The full pattern 'some contextual text
AI-1: My action
Second line
AI: My new action
Another line' (single paragraph, all soft returns) syncs to exactly two sheet rows with correct actionText values.
close_reason: All 4 AC tests pass. Root cause: DocumentApp getText() returns soft returns as \r not \n; fixed by normalizing line endings in scanner before processing.

local.settings.json (mirrors GasLogger.js's AXIOM_TOKEN+AXIOM_DATASET gate).

   poll Axiom for it, record elapsed latency. Used as a health check (fail fast if

2. Sentinel/watermark technique for assert_no_log: instead of a bare N-second
   absence window (unsound against ingest latency -- see gts-ishz comment
   thread), POST a fresh sentinel via the axiom_probe route immediately after the
   action under test, wait until THAT sentinel is observably queryable in Axiom,
   then check the suspect tag is absent from everything observed up to that point.
   Sentinel landing proves ingest has caught up to "now"; absence is then sound.

clear_logs()/wait_for_log()/assert_log()/collect_logs() keep their current
signatures (log_dir, match_fn, timeout_s, poll_s, after) -- under the Axiom
backend, log_dir is ignored/unused and queries go to the configured dataset
instead. File backend behavior is unchanged (used when Axiom isn't configured).

  assert_no_log, collect_logs (Python) and clearLogs, waitForLogEntry,
  waitForLogTag (JS)

- Output schema: return value shape (parsed log entry dict/object) unchanged
  between backends

- All 7+ existing Python call sites and probe.test.js pass unmodified (no source
  changes to call sites themselves) against the new backend-selecting gas_log.py.

- assert_no_log uses the sentinel-watermark technique under the Axiom backend

  fixture other tests/fixtures can read the measured latency from.
- File backend (no Axiom configured) behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged from

title: [INF] Split overloaded sync.warn tag into doc-not-found sub-events; fix Doc not found/Doc Not Found msg-casing split
description:

sync.warn is 58/200 (29%) of all events in the sample, the single largest bucket, and it's overloaded:

Same logical condition, two different msg strings -- Axiom facets on msg can't group them as one bucket; the live sample showed an even 29/29 split.
2. Same tag, two different real conditions, disambiguated only by free-text msg: 'doc trashed during sync sweep' (SyncManager.js, err: 'Document is in Trash') vs 'doc confirmed not found via WebApp mark' (WebApp.js, carries marked: <count> instead). docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md SS4.1's own stated principle ('name every event by what it actually did') argues these should be distinct sub-events, not one tag + msg-text disambiguation.
3. Related, lower priority: sync.skip (28/200, 14% of the same sample) carries no msg/reason at all -- just docId. Only one skip path exists today (unchanged since last sync, src/SyncManager.js:378) so it's unambiguous, but cheap to add msg: 'unchanged since last sync' while touching this file for the rename anyway.

Decide and document the sub-event split for sync.warn's two conditions (e.g. sync.docNotFound.trashed / sync.docNotFound.confirmed) -- re-verify call sites first, this audit is a snapshot.
Standardize on one msg string (or drop msg as the disambiguator in favor of the tag itself) for the doc-not-found condition; fix the casing split at src/SyncManager.js:83/90/371 vs src/WebApp.js:1055.
Add msg: 'unchanged since last sync' to src/SyncManager.js:378's sync.skip call.

Added msg to sync.skip. Verified no test asserts on the old tag/msg strings (tests only check the persisted Sync Status sheet column). Committed 3d9ab77.

Redundant/shadowing version field: GasLogger.log() already auto-stamps a top-level version from BUILD_INFO on every entry (src/GasLogger.js:101-102), and _postToAxiom's Object.assign applies e.data AFTER the base row -- so any call site that also passes version: BUILD_INFO.value inside data (src/EditorAddonCard.js:52 LINK_PREVIEW, src/SyncManager.js:287 sync.all.start.identity) silently overwrites the auto-stamped field in the Axiom row. Harmless today (same value) but fragile and should be removed -- version/op/ts/tag are reserved/auto fields that call sites must never set inside data.
3. verify_chip_integrity.done (src/WebApp.js:965) is a third tag-casing variant (snake_case domain) missed in x94a's first-pass grep -- add to that rename map as verify.chipIntegrity.done.
4. NOT a bug, document so a future cleanup doesn't 'fix' it: global_id (snake_case) in the test.* tags (src/WebApp.js patch_action_status/edit_action_row/delete_action_row) intentionally mirrors the WebApp JSON wire-contract field name (src/ContractSchema.js), which is itself deliberately snake_case -- distinct from internal GAS camelCase. Leave as-is.
5. NOT a bug: masterDocId (template doc, read-only) vs cloneId/testDocId (the per-session clone) vs generic docId are three genuinely distinct entity roles in TestFixtures.js/WebApp.js, not duplicate names for the same thing.

Full key-frequency table and call-site detail in knowledge-base/staging/gaslogger-tag-taxonomy.md.

One documented parameter-key standard (msg = human description, err = error value/exception, <noun>Count for counts, ok = operation success boolean, found = existence-check boolean, reserved auto fields ts/tag/version/op never set inside data) that every existing call site's data object is checked against.

title: [IMP] Propagate correlation/op id from addon calls into WebApp invocations (caller-linked, not adopted)
description:
Follow-up to gts-65g1 (per-invocation op id via GasLogger.startOp()/endOp()). That bead scopes op id correlation to a single GAS execution (syncAll() and similar). This bead extends correlation across the addon->WebApp HTTP boundary (UrlFetchApp calls into doPost/doGet entry points) so a user action in the add-on UI can be traced through into the webapp execution it triggers.

Do not start until gts-65g1 is closed -- this depends on the op-id mechanism it introduces.

Candidate design (verify/re-derive at start time, don't assume): do NOT have the webapp side adopt the caller's op id verbatim (that would break the 'op id is unique per execution' invariant and collapse concurrent/replayed invocations together). Instead:
- Add an optional receivedOpId param to GasLogger.startOp(receivedOpId). The webapp execution still mints its own fresh op id (Utilities.getUuid()) for itself.
- If receivedOpId was supplied, stamp it onto every log entry as a separate field (e.g. parentOp) alongside the execution's own op id.
- Add a GasLogger.getCurrentOp() getter so the add-on side can read its own current op id before issuing the UrlFetchApp call.
- Add-on call sites need to place that op id into the request payload; the webapp entry point needs to read it out and pass it into startOp().

This is the trace-id/span-id shape from distributed tracing: op = this execution's own span, parentOp = the caller's span. Gives a queryable causal chain (op=X for one execution's own logs, parentOp=X for everything it caused) without conflating separate executions under one shared id.
close_reason: Addon->WebApp op-id correlation (parentOp) implemented and wired into doPost + 5 production call sites. Also: _syncTeamScope now trusts DocData.teamId mirror instead of re-reading Drive on every sync (perf), with a teamScope-drift check in verify_action_rows as the compensating control (proven via new test_team_scope.py S9, induced-drift scenario). Gap instrumentation added: all 5 browser_page fixtures now emit launch/teardown timing to Axiom via new emit_standalone_event(). Verified live: test_team_scope.py (incl S9) + test_sync_all.py all green against deployed TEST. Commit b856e8e.
