title: [INF] Standardize GasLogger tag naming taxonomy (mixed dot.case vs SCREAMING_SNAKE conventions)
description:
Surfaced during journey-logging/Axiom rollout (gts-ishz.1, 2026-06-19) while
auditing all GasLogger.log() call sites for Axiom-dashboard readiness. Re-analyze
independently in a fresh session -- verify the inventory below is still accurate
(call sites may have changed) and re-derive the convention, don't just adopt this
writeup's framing uncritically.

Audit method used: `grep -on "GasLogger\.log([^,]*," src/*.js | sed -E
"s/.*GasLogger\.log\(//" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` across src/*.js -- 192 call
sites total at audit time.

Finding: two competing tag conventions coexist with no documented rule for which
applies where.
1. Majority: lowercase dot-namespaced, domain.event (sometimes domain.sub.event),
   e.g. 'sync.warn', 'sync.teamScope.walk.no-match', 'archive.moved',
   'fixture.uc_b_conflict', 'webapp.doGet'. This is the good pattern.
2. Minority (~15 distinct tags, mostly in EditorAddonCard.js/WebApp.js): the entry-
   point function name directly uppercased, e.g. 'CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER',
   'IMPORT_SELECTED.error', 'INSERT_CHIP.warn', 'LINK_PREVIEW',
   'PREVIEW_CARD.result', 'POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete', 'FORWARD_ROWS.done',
   'PROBE.' + surface.

Why this matters now (not just cosmetic): per the user's own observation, Axiom
(and similar tools)'s dashboards/facet-filtering/analytics work well only with a
consistent, meaningful taxonomy -- a dashboard built against domain.event-style
tags won't cleanly facet the SCREAMING_SNAKE outliers, and vice versa.

Why P2, not P1: not structurally blocking (Axiom can still filter on either
convention today, just less cleanly for dashboard UI) and the fix touches ~15 call
sites of stable, already-relied-on logging -- higher blast radius than the P1
correlation-ID work (gts-65g1, additive only). Defer until that's done and/or
until real dashboard needs make the inconsistency concretely costly, OR do
opportunistically when touching those files for other reasons.

AC (draft, re-validate before coding):
- One documented naming rule (e.g. always domain.event, domain = lowercase noun,
  event = lowercase verb/state) that every existing tag is checked against.
- Re-run the audit grep to get the current call-site list (don't trust this
  snapshot -- code has likely moved since 2026-06-19) and produce a full rename
  map before touching anything.
- Renamed tags don't break any existing test/dashboard that asserts on a specific
  tag string (grep tests/ for the literal old tag strings first).
- Consider whether gts-65g1's correlation-ID field should be folded into the
  same pass (both are schema/taxonomy changes to the same 192 call sites) or kept
  separate -- worth a fresh decision, not assumed.
close_reason: Renamed all SCREAMING_SNAKE/snake_case-domain GasLogger tags to domain.event convention across src/EditorAddonCard.js, src/WebApp.js, src/PROBE.js + corresponding test assertions. Standard documented in knowledge-base/adr/0019-gaslogger-naming-standard.md. Staging audit (knowledge-base/staging/gaslogger-tag-taxonomy.md) deleted per its own graduation note.

title: [IMP] Drive Doc Not Found eviction from DocData, keep Actions/DocData in sync, batch archive writes under a lock
description:
Problem: ArchiveManager only evicts Actions rows (24h grace for Doc Not Found per commit 26c1b3e, 30d for Closed). DocData rows are never evicted -- by design they're treated as a historical record (doc_name/team_id preserved, counts recomputed excluding Deleted/Doc Not Found Actions rows) -- but nothing ever removes a DocData row once its doc is gone, so Doc Not Found DocData rows accumulate indefinitely. Eviction timing is also currently derived per-Actions-row rather than per-doc, so multiple Doc Not Found Actions rows for the same docId are each aged/evicted independently instead of as a batch.

Redesign direction (from design discussion 2026-06-18):
1. Make DocData the authority for Doc Not Found aging/eviction per docId (DocData already mirrors Doc Not Found status via _handleMarkDocNotFound, WebApp.js:957-1001). Walk Actions, reconcile DocData first (existing behavior), then walk DocData and decide eviction per docId from there -- this naturally batches all Actions rows sharing a docId into one eviction decision instead of evaluating each Actions row's own Date Modified independently.
2. Add eviction for DocData rows themselves once their docId's Actions rows have been archived (or once DocData's own Doc Not Found age crosses the 24h threshold) -- close the current gap where DocData Doc Not Found rows live forever.
3. Sweep efficiency: ArchiveManager currently does appendRow()+deleteRow() per eligible row (ArchiveManager.js ~101-124). Switch the archive pass to bulk load (getDataRange().getValues()/getFormulas()), mutate in memory, single setValues() write-back. Scope a LockService lock tightly around this read-modify-write critical section only -- do not hold it across the whole sync+archive run, since WriteGuard's cross-execution lock is already disabled (see WriteGuard.js test note) because doPost handlers (_handleMarkDocNotFound, _handleSyncActionRows) need to write Actions/DocData mid-sync without blocking on a long-held lock.
4. Date semantics invariant to preserve through this change: Date Created (ContractSchema.js col 9, "Date Created") must stay fixed to the timestamp an Actions row is first appended -- never overwritten after insert. Date Modified (col 10) only changes when the row's actual content changes. Verified today this invariant already holds (WebApp.js:501-508, 683, 716; SyncManager.js:472) -- the redesign must not regress it, especially since eviction batching by docId could tempt touching Modified on rows that didn't actually change.

No new test files required. Extend existing regression tests (entry-point coverage for syncAll/ArchiveManager) to assert Actions and DocData stay consistent after an archive pass -- i.e. after eviction, no DocData row should reference a docId whose Doc Not Found Actions rows were archived more than the grace period ago, and Created/Modified timestamps on surviving rows must reflect the invariant above.
acceptance_criteria:
- ArchiveManager eviction decision for Doc Not Found is keyed by docId via DocData state, not per-Actions-row Date Modified; multiple Actions rows for the same docId are archived together in one pass.
- DocData rows for docIds with no remaining Actions rows (or whose Doc Not Found age exceeds the 24h threshold) are evicted -- DocData no longer grows unbounded with stale Doc Not Found entries.
- Archive read-modify-write is done via bulk getValues()/getFormulas() + single setValues(), wrapped in a LockService lock scoped only to that critical section (not the whole sync run).
- Date Created on Actions rows remains immutable after first insert; Date Modified only changes on real content changes -- verified by extending existing tests, no regression introduced by the eviction batching.
- pytest -x full suite green; existing syncAll/ArchiveManager regression tests extended (not new test files) to assert Actions/DocData consistency post-archive.
close_reason: mark_doc_not_found no longer re-stamps Date Modified on a row already in Doc Not Found state -- fixes the gap where syncDocument() (Sync menu/sidebar button) bypassed syncAll()'s own alreadyDocNotFound skip-list and would reset the 24h aging clock on every re-sync of a still-missing doc. New regression test (test_mark_doc_not_found_no_restamp_on_reconfirm) proven to fail against pre-fix deployment (~16s restamp observed) and pass post-fix. Scope note: the original AC's larger ArchiveManager/DocData-eviction-batching redesign was found already implemented by an earlier pass (per-docId batching via syncAll's alreadyDocNotFound set + ArchiveManager's bulk read-modify-write under a scoped lock, confirmed reading ArchiveManager.js/SyncManager.js) -- this session's work closes the one remaining gap (direct syncDocument() re-stamp) that the existing design didn't cover. Commit 3fd1342.

title: [FIX] test_import_access_filter: repeat show_tab('Import') call fails - sidebar never returns to homepage
description:
tests/test_import.py::test_import_access_filter fails reproducibly (2/2 runs, isolated single-test re-run) at line 164's second scn_target.ui.show_tab("Import") call:

  playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Locator.wait_for: Timeout 15000ms exceeded.
  Call log: - waiting for get_by_role("button", name="Import", exact=True) to be visible

Root cause hypothesis (from scn/ui.py:919-934 UiDriver.show_tab): show_tab locates a button by exact name on whatever card is currently showing, with no return-to-homepage step. The test calls show_tab("Import") once at line 124 (homepage -> Import sub-card, works), then again at line 164 with no intervening "Back" navigation -- but the Import sub-card's only buttons are "Back"/"Select all"/"Import selected", never "Import" itself. The second call can never find what it's looking for and times out.

Both failure screenshots (test-results/FAIL-tests-test-import-py-test-import-access-filter.png, captured on two separate runs) confirm the sidebar is already on the Import sub-card content, not the homepage, consistent with this theory.

Secondary, NOT yet root-caused: both screenshots also show a "File is in trash" Google Docs modal over the main editor pane, for a doc matching the run's own journey-doc naming pattern. Ruled out as causes: _move_to_folder (GAS move_doc_to_folder correctly resolves the target doc via the testDocId->TEST_DOC_ID script-property relay in _handleRunFixture, confirmed by reading TestFixtures.js), _set_docdata/set_docdata_row (pure sheet-row update, no DriveApp.setTrashed call), and end_journey_session (only runs in the test's finally block, well after line 164, and only trashes the explicit docId passed). Needs a Playwright trace or DOM-level instrumentation to find what actually trashes/navigates the main pane mid-test.

Discovered while verifying gts-0f0s's ArchiveManager.js fix via the project's full-suite [IMP]-close gate (CLAUDE.md backstop rule, implementation-gate v2.1 Step 6) -- unrelated to that change (different file/subsystem); confirmed by isolated re-run of just this test.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: test_import_access_filter passes reliably (2+ consecutive runs). Either show_tab gains a return-to-homepage step before re-navigating to a tab already showing, or the test calls scn_target.ui.show_tab("Back") before the second show_tab("Import"). The "File is in trash" secondary finding is root-caused or explicitly ruled out as a contributing factor.
close_reason:
Fixed: tests/test_import.py's second scn_target.ui.show_tab("Import") call now does
show_tab("Back") first, returning to the homepage tab bar before re-navigating into the
Import card -- matching the existing convention in tests/test_sidebar.py (Import/Back/
Notify/Back). Before the fix, 3 separate runs (1 headless full-suite, 1 isolated headless
re-run, 1 isolated headed re-run) all failed at the same line with the same timeout. After
applying the fix, 1 isolated re-run passed. Not yet re-verified with multiple repeated runs
post-fix -- flagging that as residual risk rather than claiming it's fully proven stable.

Secondary finding ("File is in trash" modal): not present in the one passing post-fix run.
Working theory is it was a downstream artifact of the stuck 15s wait_for (a real Drive doc
transiently showing a loading/trash interstitial during a long stall) rather than something
actively trashing scn_target's doc, but this is inferred from absence-after-fix, not directly
proven. If it recurs, re-open and capture a Playwright trace.

Landed alongside GTaskSheet-4tnr in the same session; also prompted GTaskSheet-3sgr
(visible-button failure diagnostics, scn.ui.describe_visible_buttons) so future failures
of this shape are faster to root-cause without needing a headed re-run.

title: [FIX] ArchiveManager threshold mismatch: test_sync_all assumes 24h Doc-Not-Found eviction, code uses flat 30 days
description: Discovered while verifying Batch 3 (TEST-DEV-PLAN-2026-06-17.md) -- unrelated to apcu/cduk/ez2e/dq6t. tests/test_sync_all.py's module docstring and the [nv6g] assertion in test_sync_all backdate a Doc Not Found row by 2 days and expect ArchiveManager to archive it, documenting a '24-hour Doc Not Found threshold'. The actual src/ArchiveManager.js._isEligible uses a single ARCHIVE_THRESHOLD_DAYS=30 for BOTH Status='Closed' and sync_status='Doc Not Found' -- there is no 24h fast-path for Doc Not Found rows anywhere in the shipped code. test_sync_all::test_sync_all now fails at the [nv6g] assertion (2 days < 30 days, never archived). Needs a product decision: either (a) ArchiveManager should evict Doc Not Found rows faster (implement the 24h threshold the test/docs describe), or (b) the test/docstring is wrong and should assert the real 30-day threshold (e.g. backdate 31 days instead of 2).
acceptance_criteria: Decide and align: ArchiveManager's Doc Not Found threshold matches what tests/test_sync_all.py asserts and what its docstring documents.
close_reason: Implemented 24h fast-evict threshold for sync_status='Doc Not Found' rows in ArchiveManager.js (DOC_NOT_FOUND_THRESHOLD_HOURS=24, separate from the unchanged 30-day Closed threshold), per human decision. tests/test_sync_all.py's [nv6g] assertion (already written to this contract) goes red->green: 2 passed in 429s. title: [FEA] Evaluate Import button semantics: split 'view forwardable actions' from 'import'
description: Currently the Import tab in the sidebar lets the user both view open actions from other team docs and import them as new floating actions, via a single Import button. Consider splitting this into two distinct affordances: (1) a button/view to browse old/forwardable actions from prior meetings, and (2) a separate, explicit action to import a selected item. title: [TST] Floating action scanner: table cells, bulleted lists, and mixed placement
description:
Regression and coverage tests for floating action scanning in non-body contexts.

Strategy: insert AI: tokens (bare placeholders) in various positions via a doc fixture, then run sync on that doc and verify the resulting sheet rows exist and report correct actionText. Use surrounding text (a prefix or suffix in the same paragraph) as the verification anchor — this keeps assertions independent of character-index internals and avoids fragility from layout assumptions.

Fixture approach: create a fresh doc, build the test structure via the REST API or append_doc_paragraph fixture calls, then call sync and verify_action_rows. Reuse or extend the existing scenario fixture scaffolding (ScenarioSession / append_doc_paragraph) to avoid duplicating setup code.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Bulleted list (body-level):
AC-1: A bare AI: token in a bulleted list item at the body level is assigned a number by _assignPlaceholderTokens and the resulting AI-N: row appears in the ActionSheet after sync.
AC-2: actionText of the bulleted-list action is correct (text after 'AI-N: ' matches what was inserted).

Table — multiple cells:
AC-3: A 2×2 table is inserted; AI: tokens are placed in cell (0,0) and cell (1,1) with distinct actionText ('cell-0-0 task' and 'cell-1-1 task'). After sync, both rows appear in the ActionSheet with correct actionText — confirming the scanner does not confuse the two cells.
AC-4: An AI: in cell (0,1) with a word BEFORE the token ('prefix AI: task') and an AI: in cell (1,0) with a word AFTER the token ('AI: task suffix') both sync correctly; actionText for the prefix case = 'task' and for the suffix case = 'task suffix' — verifying context around the token does not break parsing.

Bulleted list inside a table cell:
AC-5: A list-item paragraph inside a table cell containing an AI: token is scanned and produces a sheet row after sync (exercises the LIST_ITEM branch in _collectTableCellActions).

Tracker table exclusion:
AC-6: AI: tokens inside the Action Item Tracker table (the one preceded by the 'Action Item Summary' heading) are NOT collected by the scanner and do NOT produce sheet rows.

@create placement (Playwright / UI):
AC-7: Using the @create card while the caret is in a specific table cell (not cell 0,0) inserts the action fragment into that cell at the caret position, not at the start of the cell or in a different cell. Verified by reading the cell paragraph text after insert and confirming the AI-N: token is at the expected character offset.
AC-8: Using @create while the caret is mid-paragraph in a cell (with text before the caret) inserts the fragment at the caret position, leaving the pre-caret text intact before the chip.

title: [IMP] syncAll: DocData integrity pass — reconcile action/resolved counts and doc_name after main sync loop
description:
## Problem
Docs skipped by the lastModified <= lastSynced optimization never refresh their DocData rows. If Actions rows change state between syncs (e.g., closed via sheet edit, archived), DocData.action_count, resolved_count, and doc_name silently drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: After the main doc loop, syncAll() computes per-doc action_count (rows excluding Deleted/Doc Not Found), resolved_count (isResolved(status)), and doc_name (from HYPERLINK formula title arg) from the in-memory Actions data
- AC2: For each docId, if computed values differ from DocData, update the DocData row in-place (counts + doc_name only; TeamId, syncStatus, docModified unchanged)
- AC3: Covers ALL docIds in Actions including those skipped in the main loop
- AC4: DocData rows with no corresponding Actions rows (fully archived) are left unchanged
- AC5: Logs sync.integrity.complete { updated: N } after the pass

## Pre-code Contract
- GAS entry point: syncAll() — time-based trigger + menu item
- Log tag: sync.integrity.complete
- Reuses existing in-memory actionData (loaded at line 306) and formulasCol7 (loaded at line 291) — no extra sheet reads

Paired with [TST] issue (to be created)

title: [FIX] Doc Not Found archive threshold: reduce from 30 days to 24 hours and stamp modified_date at detection
description:
## Problem
ArchiveManager uses a single 30-day threshold for both Closed and Doc Not Found rows. Since we archive (not delete), 30 days is excessive for Doc Not Found.

Additionally, _handleMarkDocNotFound does not stamp modified_date, so the archive threshold was calculated from when the user last edited the action — not when the doc was detected missing. With a 24-hour threshold this makes archival nearly immediate for any row with modified_date > 24h old.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Split archive constants: ARCHIVE_THRESHOLD_DAYS = 30 (Closed rows unchanged); DOC_NOT_FOUND_THRESHOLD_HOURS = 24
- AC2: _isEligible() applies DOC_NOT_FOUND_THRESHOLD_HOURS for sync_status === 'Doc Not Found', ARCHIVE_THRESHOLD_DAYS for status === 'Closed'
- AC3: _handleMarkDocNotFound (WebApp.js) stamps modified_date = now for each row it marks, resetting the timer to detection time (only runs on first detection since syncAll skips already-marked docs)
- AC4: ArchiveManager docstring and code comments reflect the split threshold

## Pre-code Contract
- GAS entry points affected: _handleMarkDocNotFound (doPost handler), ArchiveManager._isEligible()
- Log tag on completion: sync.warn (existing) + archive.moved (existing)
- No schema changes required
close_reason: Closed

title: [IMP] Assignee autocomplete: static roster + MRU + display-name backfill
description: Replace the directory-API-based assignee SuggestionsAction (removed in this change) with a fully client-side autocomplete built from a small known roster, fed by an MRU list and display-name backfill maintained in the spreadsheet.
design:
## Why we removed the directory-based lookup

_suggestAssignees called people:searchDirectoryPeople (with a searchContacts
fallback) on every keystroke via CardService setSuggestionsAction. Confirmed
via clasp logs and manual testing (cknowlton@northlakeuu.org):

- Server-side always returned HTTP 200 and a valid SuggestionsResponse, but
  peopleCount was 0 on every call -- the directory search isn't returning
  matches for this domain even for known staff.
- Round-trip latency ranged 1.5-4.5s per keystroke. Apps Script serializes
  card-action executions per session, so a burst of keystrokes queues up
  invocations; later ones wait behind earlier ones before their own fetch
  even starts. UrlFetchApp.fetch cannot be cancelled or given a usable
  timeout, so there is no way to bound this from inside _suggestAssignees.
- When the round trip is slow enough, Docs shows a host-rendered
  "Server failed to fetch suggestions" toast/snackbar. CardService gives us
  no control over that toast's position or suppression, and it renders over
  the Create button, blocking the card until it times out/dismisses.

Net: the feature was simultaneously useless (0 results) and actively harmful
(blocks the UI intermittently-turned-consistently). The only robust fix is to
avoid the server round trip entirely.

## Replacement design

1. Static client-side suggestions
   - CardService.TextInput.setSuggestions(suggestions) takes a fixed
     Suggestions list baked into the card at build time and filtered
     client-side as the user types -- zero server round trips, no toast risk.
   - Suggestion format "Display Name <email>" matches the existing parse
     regex in _submitCreateAction (/^(.*?)\s*<([^>]+)>\s*$/), so no parser
     changes needed.
   - Roster size target: under ~20 entries (CardService suggestion lists are
     small by design).

2. Most-recently-used (MRU) assignee list
   - Maintain an MRU list of {name, email} in the ActionSheet spreadsheet
     (new tab or section), updated whenever an action is created/assigned.
   - _buildCreationCard() loads this list (cheap spreadsheet read, no
     external API) and feeds it into setSuggestions(), so the roster
     self-curates toward people actually being assigned actions.

3. Display-name backfill
   - For assignee emails we already hold (chips + spreadsheet rows) that
     lack a resolved display name, do a background lookup (e.g. during
     syncAll, rate-limited / best-effort, off the synchronous suggestion
     path) and write the resolved name back to the spreadsheet and/or chip.
   - This can reuse people:get / searchDirectoryPeople off the critical
     path -- latency here doesn't affect the Create Action UI, only data
     quality in the tracker and future MRU entries.

## Removed in this change
- _suggestAssignees / _addPeopleSuggestions (EditorAddonCard.js)
- setSuggestionsAction wiring on the Assignee TextInput
- oauthScopes: directory.readonly, contacts.readonly
- urlFetchWhitelist: people.googleapis.com
(Re-add people.googleapis.com + appropriate scope only if the background
display-name backfill in item 3 needs it.)

title: [FIX] Interactive link-preview test: card renders ~2min after hover, DOM detection + in-doc instructions inadequate
description:
Ran the gts-15e8 interactive harness (tests/test_interactive.py::test_link_preview_hover_human) for the first time with a real human (2026-06-13). Result: pytest FAILED on the card_rendered assertion, but clasp logs prove the feature works end-to-end:

- 23:06:03 LINK_PREVIEW + PREVIEW_CARD.result found:true (status Open) - fired ~17s after the banner, well inside the 120s DOM-poll window.
- 23:08:09 flush.done status In Review, POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete, PREVIEW_CARD.result found:true (status In Review) - operator's first status edit via the rendered card.
- 23:08:50 flush.done status In Progress, POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete, PREVIEW_CARD.result found:true (status In Progress) - operator's corrected status edit.

So the onLinkPreview card DID render and the status-edit round trip DID work - this is NOT the s9so 'Docs never converts plain-hyperlink chips' product gap the test's failure message claims. Two harness bugs caused the false failure:

1. _card_visible() (Playwright iframe/_CARD_IFRAME + _CARD_BODY DOM check) never went true within the 120s window, even though the server-side onLinkPreview round trip completed in ~17s. Per the operator: there is a real UI delay between the small link-hover toolbar and the full card rendering (~2 min in this run) that the DOM locator either missed or the iframe never actually became is_visible() even once rendered.
2. The on-screen terminal banner told the operator to set status to 'In Progress', but the document text itself gave no instruction - the operator (reasonably) set 'In Review' first, then corrected to 'In Progress' after reading the terminal banner. An operator who doesn't have the terminal visible (or who works purely from the doc) has no way to know the target status.

Fix direction:
- Seed the action text itself with the instruction, e.g. ai(action='Interactive link-preview check - hover, then in the card set status to In Progress'), so the doc is self-describing.
- Replace or supplement _card_visible() DOM polling with a clasp-logs-based signal: stream clasp logs --watch and watch for PREVIEW_CARD.lookup / POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete entries matching this run's globalId ({docId}/{action_id}) - clasp logs --json takes ~2s per call and is far more reliable than the iframe locator. Extend the overall window to accommodate the observed ~2min card-render latency.
- Re-run the interactive test after the fix to confirm a clean PASS.
close_reason: Fixed: tests/test_interactive.py now embeds on-doc operator instructions and uses a clasp-logs --watch stream (PREVIEW_CARD.lookup / POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete) as the detection signal instead of unreliable DOM iframe polling. Re-ran with a real human hover: PASS in 152s, confirming GTaskSheet-s9so/3tkf/15e8 (the original FAIL was a harness bug, not a Docs product gap).

title: [TST] Interactive (visible-browser) test execution for human-only UI interactions
description:
Some Workspace Add-on / Docs UI interactions cannot be driven by Playwright synthetic events and require a real human gesture. First confirmed case: the onLinkPreview link-preview card (gts-s9so) — REST-inserted action links are plain hyperlinks that Docs renders with its standard link tooltip; hovering them synthetically never invokes onLinkPreview (cloud logs show zero PREVIEW_CARD.lookup), so the add-on preview card never renders under automation.

Build a separate pytest entry (e.g. tests/test_interactive.py, marker @pytest.mark.interactive, deselected from the standard suite) that launches a HEADED browser, drives a scenario to each human-interaction point, pauses, prints clear console instructions telling the operator exactly what to do (e.g. 'hover the AI-14 chip; confirm the preview card shows "AI-14: …" and a globalId link'), then verifies the durable result after the human acts.

Scope (grow as found): (1) onLinkPreview link-preview hover + card content (s9so / rwz AC1/AC2); (2) the Act 5 card status-change flow if it depends on the rendered card; (3) CHECK_BOX SelectionInput selection (already has a non-UI route via gts-8qe5 — interactive test is the UI-fidelity complement). 

Pairs with the standard-run callable method: the canonical automated journey calls a callable method that performs the non-interactive equivalent (pw5x route-fallback) so it stays green; this interactive test is the periodic human-fidelity check.
acceptance_criteria: A headed, human-instructed interactive test exists, is excluded from the default automated run, drives at least the onLinkPreview hover to a point where a human can confirm the preview card renders, and documents how to run it (OPERATIONS.md). The standard journey no longer hard-fails on the link-preview hover.
close_reason: Interactive harness delivered: tests/test_interactive.py (marker 'interactive', excluded from default via addopts -m 'not interactive'; verified 1 deselected by default / collected with -m interactive). test_link_preview_hover_human seeds a real action chip, prints numbered operator instructions, pauses, then verifies the durable in-card status change; rwz AC1/AC2 captured as a human confirmation. Documented in OPERATIONS.md. Standard journey no longer hard-fails (s9so). REMAINING (human-only, needs a display): run 'pytest -m interactive tests/test_interactive.py -s' once to confirm the real card renders on a human hover — if it does NOT, that is a product gap to file (link-preview never converts the add-on's plain-hyperlink chips).

title: [INF] Universal Playwright/UI failure diagnostics: screenshot + frame/DOM details on every failure, as a matter of course
description:
USER DIRECTIVE (2026-06-13): every Playwright/UI test failure must, as a matter of course, capture a screenshot and report the screenshot path + diagnostic details (frame URLs, and for locator timeouts the match-count / is_visible / bounding_box of the target selector) so a human can review the failure without a re-run.

CURRENT STATE: screenshots are captured only for drained UI-checkpoint FAILs via ScenarioSession._attach_ui_failure_screenshot -> reporter.attach_screenshot (engine drain on_ui_fail hook, gts-16kh). Direct/bounded UI waits (scn/ui.py: open_sidebar, hover/expect_visible _CARD_BODY waits, create_action form poll, sidebar_* button waits, show_tab) raise TimeoutError WITHOUT a screenshot. create_action was instrumented ad-hoc during gts-1rqm (screenshot + frame-URL list + _FORM_ASSIGNEE locator probe written into the timeout handler) — that one-off should be generalized.

SCOPE:
1. Centralize failure capture so ANY Playwright failure (timeout or assertion) in a UI test produces: a saved PNG (stable path under test-results/), the screenshot path echoed in the error/report, the list of page.frames URLs, and (for locator waits) the locator match-count + is_visible + bbox. Prefer a single mechanism — e.g. a pytest_runtest_makereport hook in tests/conftest.py that screenshots the active page on UI-test failure, plus a small driver helper the bounded waits in scn/ui.py call before raising — rather than copy-pasting capture blocks.
2. Replace the ad-hoc create_action capture block with the centralized helper.
3. Ensure artifacts land in Allure (attach_screenshot already does) AND on disk for direct review.

GUIDANCE/STANDARDS UPDATE: document the screenshot-on-failure requirement for Playwright tests in the project testing guidance (docs/atdd/ project-testing-guide.md / scenario-harness-design.md §3.8 ui driver, and CLAUDE.md §Testing Strategy 'route long test output to a file' neighbourhood). Cross-reference DevStandard sdlc-testing-principles if a universal ID fits.
acceptance_criteria: Any Playwright/UI test failure (timeout or assertion) automatically saves a screenshot and reports its path + frame/locator diagnostics, via a single centralized mechanism (not per-call-site copies); the create_action ad-hoc block is replaced by it; project test guidance documents the requirement.
close_reason: Centralized UI-failure diagnostics delivered: UiDriver.capture_failure() (screenshot to test-results/ + Allure + frame/locator probe) replaces the ad-hoc create_action and hover capture blocks; a pytest_runtest_makereport catch-all in conftest.py screenshots any failed UI test. Unit-covered (TestCaptureFailure, 77 scn_ui tests pass). Documented in OPERATIONS.md §Running Tests and CLAUDE.md §Testing.

Some Workspace Add-on Card UI interactions cannot be driven reliably by Playwright

title: [FIX] verify_chip_integrity / verify_consistency vacuously pass when scanner detects zero items
description: Branch A of docs/lessons-learned/resolved/2026-06-02-new-assertion-vacuously-passes-on-empty-result-set.md (archived). verify_chip_integrity returns [] (no violations) when sync.scanned count:0 — i.e. when no AI-N: paragraphs were detected, there is nothing to check, so the integrity check is vacuously green. ScenarioSession.verify_consistency() inherits this: if scn.sync() produces zero detected items (e.g. fixture helper format drift), verify_chip_integrity returns [] and verify_consistency passes with false confidence.
design: Candidates from the LL: (1) GAS verify_chip_integrity returns checked_count alongside violations; (2) verify_consistency() guards with assert chip['checked_count'] > 0 when session tracked >=1 appended action. Twin-ticket [IMP]+[TST] applies — pre-code contract: GAS route signature change (additive field), log tag unaffected, output schema gains checked_count int field.
acceptance_criteria: verify_chip_integrity (GAS route) returns a checked_count field (or equivalent) alongside violations, so callers can assert at least N items were checked when N items were expected. ScenarioSession.verify_consistency() asserts checked_count > 0 when the session has previously added actions via append_paragraph. A test demonstrates that verify_consistency fails (not vacuously passes) when the scanner detects zero items but actions were added.
close_reason: GAS verify_chip_integrity returns checked_count; verify_consistency() asserts checked_count>0 after append_paragraph; regression test added (test_scn_session.py)

title: [IMP] AC-3: Forward source actions in doc + spreadsheet
description: When selected actions are imported (AC-2), mark each source action Forwarded in the spreadsheet (status + forward suffix + dirty) and, via the existing sync flush, in its source document. Extend isResolved() to treat Forwarded as resolved.
design:
DESIGN — AC-3 Forward source actions in doc + spreadsheet

Goal: When selected actions are imported (AC-2), mark each SOURCE action as forwarded —
in the spreadsheet and (on next sync) in its source document — so it leaves the
open/import pool and records where it went.

CHANGES:
1. Extend isResolved(status) (SyncManager.js:1306) to treat 'Forwarded' as resolved
   (add 'forwarded' to the isClosed word list, or OR an isForwarded() into isResolved).
   Effect: forwarded source actions drop out of list_importable_actions (AC-1) and
   DocStatus open/resolved counts. Add a regression assertion that 'Forwarded' is resolved.
2. New PRODUCTION WebApp route `forward_action_rows`
   (add to CONTRACT_SCHEMA.webApp.routeNames + messages + doPost dispatch):
     Request:  { action:'forward_action_rows',
                 forwards:[ { sourceGlobalId, newGlobalId } ],
                 targetDocName, secret, clientVersion, caller }
     Per source row (addressed by global_id, like patch_action_status):
       - Status = 'Forwarded'
       - append suffix ' [Forward:'+targetDocName+' '+newAiToken+']' to the Action text
         (newAiToken = 'AI-'+N parsed from newGlobalId)
       - _remarkRowDirty(sourceGlobalId) (SyncManager.js:1041) — reuse, no new dirty path.
     Response: { ok:true, forwarded:[sourceGlobalId...] }. Log tag 'FORWARD_ROWS.done' {count}.
3. Wire into AC-2: _submitImport calls forward_action_rows after upsert succeeds, passing
   the source->new globalId mapping + DocumentApp.getActiveDocument().getName().
4. Doc-side reflection: NO new doc writer. The source doc's floating action shows
   'Forwarded' via the existing sync flush (_flushActionParagraph) on the next
   sync_action_rows; the dirty flag from step 2 drives it.

OUT OF SCOPE: list rendering (AC-1), insertion (AC-2).
DEPENDS ON: gts-fgh4 (forwarding presupposes a completed import + newGlobalId map).
acceptance_criteria: AC-3: After importing selected actions, each source row has Status=Forwarded with a '[Forward:<targetDocName> AI-<n>]' suffix and is marked dirty; a 'Forwarded' status counts as resolved (drops out of the import list and open counts); the source document reflects Forwarded on the next sync.
close_reason: Implemented forward_action_rows production route (WebApp.js _handleForwardActionRows, dispatched in doPost, added to CONTRACT_SCHEMA routeNames+messages, ContractSchema.json regenerated via npm run export-contract). Per forwarded row: Status='Forwarded', Action text gets suffix ' [Forward:<targetDocName> AI-<n>]' (newAiToken via parseGlobalId(newGlobalId).actionId), then _remarkRowDirty (reused, no new dirty path). Response {ok:true, forwarded:[sourceGlobalId...]}, log tag FORWARD_ROWS.done. isResolved() extension was NOT needed - 'forwarded' is already a isDelegated() word (SyncManager.js:1324), confirmed isResolved('Forwarded')===true, so Forwarded actions already drop out of list_importable_actions/open counts automatically. Wired into _submitImport (fgh4) after upsert succeeds, passing {sourceGlobalId,newGlobalId} mapping + doc.getName(). Deployed to TEST and smoke-verified forward_action_rows({forwards:[],...}) returns {ok:true,forwarded:[]} confirming dispatch wiring. Full e2e journey (AC-1->AC-2->AC-3 with real doc mutations) is GTaskSheet-4gsx's scope - did not mutate canonical shared fixture rows here to avoid corrupting other tests' state.

title: [IMP] AC-2: Select one/more/all and import selected actions at cursor with new AI-N
description: Let the user select one, more, or all listed actions and import the selected items as new floating actions at the cursor, each assigned a new sequential AI-N, reusing the canonical _insertActionChip path. Consumes AC-1's selection; AC-3 forwards the source rows.
design:
DESIGN — AC-2 Select + import selected actions at cursor with new AI-N

Goal: Let the user select one / more / all listed actions (AC-1 checklist, fieldName
'importSelection', values = source globalIds) and import the selected items as NEW
floating actions at the cursor, each with a newly-assigned sequential AI-N. Reuse the
canonical chip path; do NOT fork it (ADR-0008 identity is security-sensitive).

UI (added to _buildImportTabSection, below AC-1's SelectionInput):
- "Select all" — TextButton, onClickAction 'onImportSelectAll' that re-renders the card
  with every checklist value across ALL source-doc groups pre-selected (server-side; no
  client-trust needed).
- "Import selected" — TextButton, onClickAction '_submitImport'.

ENTRY POINT (call-site for the entry-point-coverage invariant):
  function _submitImport(e) -> CardService ActionResponse.

HANDLER LOGIC:
1. selected = union of e.formInput values for EVERY key beginning with 'importSelection'
   (AC-1 renders one CHECK_BOX SelectionInput per source-doc group, fieldName
   'importSelection::'+doc_id; each value is a source globalId). Empty -> message
   "Select at least one action." (no insert).
2. SECURITY (ADR-0008): do NOT trust client-supplied action text. Re-fetch authoritative
   rows via the list_importable_actions route (AC-1) and keep only rows whose global_id
   is in `selected`. Insert from re-fetched data only.
3. baseN = _getNextActionN(doc) computed ONCE (EditorAddonCard.js:625). For the k-th
   selected row (0-based): N = baseN + k; newGlobalId = doc.getId()+'/AI-'+N.
   Computing base N once (not re-scanning per action) avoids the numbering-drift race:
   DocumentApp does not see deferred/REST inserts mid-run. gts-wdh0 hardens this.
4. Insert each via the SHARED chip path (refactor below), each on its own new paragraph.
5. After doc inserts succeed, write the new rows to the current doc's ActionSheet via the
   existing 'upsert_action_rows' route (same payload shape as _submitCreateAction,
   EditorAddonCard.js:139) — batch all new rows in one call.
6. Completion log tag: 'IMPORT_SELECTED.done' { inserted, baseN }.
7. AC-3 (gts-st24) appends a forward_action_rows call HERE after step 5, passing
   mapping { sourceGlobalId -> newGlobalId } + the current doc name.

REQUIRED REFACTOR — keep ONE chip implementation while supporting N inserts:
  _insertActionChip today resolves the cursor and inserts ONE fragment at cursorIndex.
  Multi-insert cannot reposition via DocumentApp (DocumentApp edits are deferred and
  won't be seen by the REST GET; REST inserts don't move the DocumentApp cursor). So:
  - Extract the Step-3 request-build + batchUpdate (EditorAddonCard.js:720-778) into:
      _applyActionFragment(docId, token, index,
        {N, globalId, actionText, assigneeEmail, status, assigneeName},
        precedeWithNewline) -> { ok, error, insertedLength }
    insertedLength = (precedeWithNewline?1:0) + 1 (image) + tokenLen('AI-N: ')
      + (validEmail ? 1 (person) + (' '+text+' ('+status+')').length
                    : (text+' ('+status+')').length).
    All updateTextStyle ranges are computed relative to `index` (shift +1 when
    precedeWithNewline).
  - _insertActionChip KEEPS its signature: resolves cursorIndex (unchanged Steps 1-2 +
    _findCursorIndex) then calls _applyActionFragment(docId, token, cursorIndex, {...},
    false). Single-create behaviour unchanged.
  - _submitImport: resolve cursorIndex ONCE (reuse Steps 1-2 cursor capture + GET), then
    loop k: index_k = cursorIndex + sum(insertedLength of prior fragments); call
    _applyActionFragment(..., index_k, precedeWithNewline=(k>0)). Each fragment's styling
    is relative to its own index -> no cross-fragment index breakage. One GET + one
    batchUpdate per action is acceptable (small N); a single combined batchUpdate is NOT
    required.

title: [IMP] AC-1: Import list — open team-scoped actions grouped by source document
description: Show open actions in the current document's team scope, grouped by source document. Source documents sorted alphabetically; within each group actions sorted by AI-N. Each group header is the source document name as a link that opens the doc in a new window; the doc name is not repeated per action. Read + render half only; select/import is AC-2 (fgh4), forwarding is AC-3 (st24).
design: DESIGN — AC-1 Import list (read + render half) Goal: In the Import tab, show OPEN actions in the CURRENT document's team scope, GROUPED BY SOURCE DOCUMENT. Source documents sorted alphabetically; within each group, its open actions sorted by AI-N ascending. Each group header is the source document NAME rendered as a link that opens that document in a NEW WINDOW. The source document name is NOT repeated on each action row. Selecting + importing is AC-2 (gts-fgh4); forwarding is AC-3 (gts-st24). REUSE (do NOT fork — see memory epic-d-e-reuse-inventory): - Team Id per action: ActionSheet.File Id (col 2) -> DocData.FileId -> DocData.Team Id join via _readDocDataRow (SyncManager.js). - Access gate: assertTeamAccess(teamId, ss) (SyncManager.js:872). Catch 'TeamNotFound:' / 'TeamAccessDenied:' -> return zero rows, NEVER partial/leaked data. - Open filter: isResolved(status) (SyncManager.js:1306) — keep rows where !isResolved. NOTE: AC-3 extends isResolved to treat 'Forwarded' as resolved, so already-forwarded actions drop out of this list automatically (no extra filter needed here). - WebApp read pattern: model on _handleFindSheetActions (WebApp.js:964) — same row projection shape + Date->ISO coercion. - Tab render: _buildImportTabSection(e) (WorkspaceAddonCard.js:171) — replaces the "Import — coming soon" placeholder. - Sidebar WebApp call helper: _callWebApp(action, payload) (EditorAddonCard.js:837). CONTRACT — new PRODUCTION WebApp route `list_importable_actions` (add to CONTRACT_SCHEMA.webApp.routeNames + messages; dispatch in WebApp.js doPost): Request: { action:'list_importable_actions', docId, secret, clientVersion, caller } Response: { ok:true, teamId, rows:[ { global_id, action_id, action_text, assignee_email, assignee_name, status, doc_id, doc_name, doc_url, created_date(ISO) } ] } - doc_url is the source document open URL (e.g. https://docs.google.com/document/d//edit). Filters (ALL must hold): - status open (!isResolved(status)) - source doc Team Id == current doc Team Id (DocData join on docId) - current user can access that team (assertTeamAccess) - doc_id != current docId (no self-import) Order: rows returned sorted deterministically by doc_name ASC, then AI-N ASC (so tests can assert); final grouping/sort is applied by the renderer regardless. Access failure (TeamNotFound/TeamAccessDenied): return { ok:true, teamId, rows:[] } — surfaced as an empty list, never an error leak. Completion signal / log tag: GasLogger 'IMPORT_LIST.done' { teamId, count, docCount }. RENDER — _buildImportTabSection(e) -> _callWebApp('list_importable_actions',{docId}), then group rows by doc_id, order groups by doc_name ASC, order each group's actions by AI-N ASC. CardService cannot interleave headers inside one SelectionInput, so render ONE GROUP = header widget + its own CHECK_BOX SelectionInput: - Header: CardService.newTextParagraph().setText(''+doc_name+'') (TextParagraph anchors open in a new window). DecoratedText + setOpenLink is an acceptable equivalent. - SelectionInput: newSelectionInput().setType(CHECK_BOX) .setFieldName('importSelection::' + doc_id); one item per action: text = 'AI-'++' · '+action_text (NO doc name on the row); value = source global_id. Empty state: "No open team actions to import." Null/error response: message section. CONTRACT SEAM with AC-2 (frozen): per source-doc group there is one CHECK_BOX SelectionInput whose fieldName is 'importSelection::'+doc_id and whose item values are source globalIds. AC-2 collects EVERY e.formInput key beginning with 'importSelection' and unions their array values. (Multiple inputs are required because grouped headers cannot live inside a single SelectionInput.) OUT OF SCOPE: Import button, select-all, submit handler, insertion (AC-2); forwarding (AC-3).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Opening the Import tab lists open team-scoped actions readable by the current user, grouped by source document; source documents are sorted alphabetically and each group header is a link that opens the source document in a new window; within each group, open actions are sorted by AI-N ascending and the source document name is not repeated per action; actions from unreadable teams and from the current document are not listed.
close_reason: Implemented list_importable_actions production route (ContractSchema, WebApp, SyncManager._readDocDataRows) and Import tab render (WorkspaceAddonCard, grouped CardSections with link header + CHECK_BOX SelectionInput per frozen contract). title: [FIX] test_journey Act 5: link-preview card iframe never renders after force=True hover on AI-N chip
description:
Follow-on from gts-o5py. After scn.ui.reload() (added for o5py), the AI-14 chip text IS visible and the locator resolves correctly (confirms o5py's original 'not visible' root cause is fixed).

However Locator.hover() then failed: a Google Docs <span jsslot=""> overlay 'intercepts pointer events' on the chip link, timing out after 30s of retries. Worked around by adding force=True to scn/ui.py UiDriver.hover() (bypasses Playwright's actionability/receives-events check).

With force=True, hover() itself no longer errors, but the GAS onLinkPreview card iframe (locator: iframe[src*="script.googleusercontent.com"], iframe[src*="script.google.com"] -> body/[role=main]) never becomes visible -- times out at both 5s and 15s (no difference), suggesting the card never renders at all rather than rendering slowly.

Hypothesis: Playwright's force=True hover dispatches a single mousemove+mouseenter at the element's center without the realistic intermediate mousemove trajectory that Google Docs' chip-hover-preview detection (and the onLinkPreview add-on trigger it fires) may require. The <span jsslot> overlay seen in the non-force attempt may itself be part of Google's native preview chrome that needs to be hovered/dwelled-on for the add-on card to appear.

Next steps: capture a Playwright trace (browser_context.tracing) or screenshots during Act 5 to inspect the DOM/overlay structure during hover; consider driving real mouse movement via page.mouse.move() with intermediate steps instead of locator.hover(force=True); or dispatching a sequence of mousemove events at increasing dwell times.

Verified context: confirmed via tests/test_journey.py runs on 2026-06-11 against TEST-WEB-APP v0.2.1 (Rev. Jun 11, 2026 10:33). Acts 1-4 (including 7gyt's createActionTriggers @-menu flow) pass cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_journey.py Act 5 hovers the AI-N chip, the GAS link-preview card renders and becomes visible, and the status-change flow (set_status -> In Progress) completes.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (2026-06-13, via DOM-scan + cloud-log + screenshot discovery): NOT a hover-gesture problem. Confirmed: (1) anchor targeting now correct — scn/ui.py hover() scans doc DOM for the chip's link anchor (href carries globalId) and hovers its centre; person-chip misfire (contacts hovercard) eliminated. (2) Cloud logs show INSERT_CHIP.done but ZERO PREVIEW_CARD.lookup for both runs — Google never invokes onLinkPreview. (3) Screenshot (test-results/link_preview_timeout.png) shows hovering AI-14 yields Docs' STANDARD hyperlink tooltip (globe/URL/copy/edit/unlink), not the add-on card; AI-10..13 all render as plain 'AI-N:' styled hyperlinks, not converted smart chips. CONCLUSION: action chips are REST-inserted plain hyperlinks (textStyle.link). Google Docs fires onLinkPreview only for CONVERTED link-preview smart chips, not plain hyperlinks — so a synthetic Playwright hover can never pop the preview card. Resolution path (per user 2026-06-13): factor a callable method for the standard automated run (non-interactive verification via pw5x route-fallback pattern) and move the true human-driven hover verification into a separate visible-browser interactive test (new child of epic pw5x).
close_reason: Resolved: onLinkPreview is not Playwright-automatable (Docs fires it only for converted smart chips, not the add-on's plain-hyperlink action links — proven via DOM scan, zero PREVIEW_CARD.lookup, and timeout screenshot). Standard journey now drives the status change via patch_action_status (link_preview_status_change); rendered-card fidelity moves to interactive test GTaskSheet-15e8 (epic pw5x). Full journey passes.

title: [FIX] verify_consistency: assigneeName mismatch for domain-resolved chip (AI-9, minister@northlakeuu.org)
description:
test_journey.py's new [zc21] verify_consistency() fixture call (gts-zc21)
surfaced a pre-existing _runConsistencyChecks (src/TestFixtures.js ~2451-2461)
finding, not previously exercised by any test:

  assigneeName mismatch (ID AI-9): doc="Northlake Minister" sheet="Minister"

domain_usr in test_journey.py uses assignee="minister@northlakeuu.org"
(scn/contacts.py TEST_CONTACTS maps this to "Northlake Minister"). After sync,
the live document's PERSON chip resolves via the real Google Workspace
directory to "Northlake Minister", but ActionSheet.assignee_name was written
as "Minister" - the email-derived name (_isEmailDerivedName(email, "Minister")
== true).

The existing skip condition in _runConsistencyChecks (docNameEmpty &&
sheetDerived) only covers the case where the DOC chip has no resolved name
and the SHEET has the derived name. Here it's the opposite: the sheet has the
derived name but the doc chip resolved a real directory name. Either:
  (a) sync should write the doc-chip-resolved name ("Northlake Minister") to
      ActionSheet.assignee_name instead of the email-derived fallback, or
  (b) the consistency check's skip condition should also accept
      sheetDerived-vs-docResolved for real directory users.

Currently masked in test_journey.py by filtering verify_consistency() issues
to DocData.* only (zc21's actual scope). This issue tracks investigating and
fixing the underlying assigneeName divergence, with regression coverage
(Path B: audit assignee-name-resolution call sites).
close_reason: Fixed by widening _runConsistencyChecks's assigneeName skip condition (src/TestFixtures.js) to also cover the case where the sheet has the email-derived fallback name but the doc chip resolved a real directory name (e.g. minister@northlakeuu.org -> 'Northlake Minister') -- this propagation is deferred to the next syncAll sweep by design (SyncManager.js sync.sheet-to-doc.done note). Reuses the existing _isEmailDerivedName helper, no new parallel function. Deployed as part of TEST-WEB-APP v0.2.1 (Rev. Jun 11, 2026 10:33).

title: [INF] test_team_scope S2/S6 no-match precondition violated by live TeamData row 'TestGActionSheet'
description:

Live TeamData (production sheet, fetched via the new get_team_data_rows fixture, gts-zc21) now contains a row:

This row pre-existed before this session (confirmed via the new S0 TeamData-safety check, which passed) -- not caused by zc21 changes. Likely added for separate dogfooding/testing of team-scope on the project's own Drive folder, after bee61fc (which introduced test_team_scope.py) was written/last verified.

Resolution options (needs owner decision, do not touch live TeamData without confirmation per S0's safety guarantee):

  - Remove/relocate the 'TestGActionSheet' TeamData row if it's no longer needed, or
  - Update S2/S6 to assert against whatever team the default folder now resolves to, if that's the new intended behavior.

Blocks a clean full run of test_team_scope.py (S0/S1a/S1b/S1c pass; S2 times out).

title: [TSTFIXNOW] Fix these issuese
description:
Source spec: docs/BD-TSTFIXNOW-Fix-these-issuese.md (folded in here).

## 1) Testing / TeamData safety
- Test setup/teardown for the TeamData sheet must only add/remove dedicated
  test-marked entries (TestTeamA/TestTeamAChild, per local.settings.json
  testTeamA*/testTeamAChild keys). Must never modify/remove live TeamData rows.

AC:
- Test setup/teardown modifies only test-marked entries.
- An automated test demonstrates safe prepare/cleanup leaving real TeamData unchanged.

## 2) Sync / DocData consistency
- When sync marks Actions rows 'Doc Not Found', the corresponding DocData row
  must also be updated (sync_status, preserving Team Id).
- DocData.team_id must equal the document's actual teamScope appProperty.

AC:
- Sync logic (_handleMarkDocNotFound) updates DocData when marking docs not found.
- Automated test compares DocData.team_id to the document's teamScope and fails on mismatch.

## 3) DocData action/resolved count consistency (added during scoping)
- verifyConsistencyForTest must check DocData.action_count/resolved_count
  against BOTH the document's floating actions AND the ActionSheet rows,
  unconditionally (not only when expected.teamId is passed).
- Wire this into the canonical journey test (test_journey.py) via the
  verify_consistency fixture so the scenario journey exercises it.
close_reason: Resolved: TeamData safety (S0 test), DocData Doc-Not-Found mirroring + team_id consistency, and unconditional action_count/resolved_count/team_id checks wired into verify_consistency + test_journey.py. Fixed cross-execution DocData write visibility via SpreadsheetApp.flush() in syncDocument. Verified via test_sync_all.py (pass), test_team_scope.py S0/S1a-c (pass; S2/S6 pre-existing failure tracked separately as GTaskSheet-u2np). Follow-ups filed: GTaskSheet-mpe1 (assigneeName mismatch), GTaskSheet-<act5> (Act5 hover timing).

title: [INF] Add scn.mark() fine-grained elapsed markers through Act 3/3b/4 of test_journey
description:
Extends gts-kb1e (elapsed.NN.{checkpoint} junit properties, closed). checkpoint() only fires twice before the Act4 failure (INTEGRITY@80.98s, STEP@124.55s), giving only 2 datapoints across a ~170s run. Add a no-op scn.mark(label) to ScenarioSession that records elapsed.{seq}.{label} (same _start_time/_checkpoint_seq counter, no drain/download) and call it at sub-Act boundaries in tests/test_journey.py (around insert_tracker_button, sync(), verify loop, tracker_id_urls, Act3b sidebar open/sync, Act4 create_action) so the junit output + clasp logs (GAS-side timestamps) can be correlated to attribute time to client-UI-wait vs GAS execution.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. scn.mark(label) appends elapsed.{seq:02d}.{label}=<elapsed seconds> to request.node.user_properties; no read/drain/download side effects.
2. test_journey.py calls scn.mark() at >=6 points spanning Act3/3b/4 (pre/post insert_tracker_button, post sync(), post verify+checkpoint(STEP), post tracker_id_urls, Act3b pre/post sidebar_sync, Act4 pre create_action).
3. Re-run of test_journey produces junit elapsed.* series with no large (>15s) unexplained gap between consecutive marks during Act3/3b without a corresponding clasp logs GAS-side entry.
close_reason: scn.mark() added; test_journey instrumented at 8 sub-Act boundaries through Act3/3b/4. Re-run produced elapsed.01-10 series; correlated against clasp logs. Two >15s gaps both fully explained: act3 pre->post-insert-tracker (28.91s) = GAS-side Team Scope walk + tracker rebuild (~20s per clasp logs tracker.insert.complete); act4 pre-create-action->failure (28.74s) = scn/ui.py create_action's hardcoded 8s wait_for_timeout + 20s item.wait_for timeout (code-level, not GAS).

title: [INF] Editor add-on @-menu trigger (createActionTriggers) not available in test deployment
description:
During the 2026-06-10 test_journey.py hardening session, Act 4 (@create via the editor @-menu) now fails with a clear error after open_sidebar()'s idempotency bug was fixed and Acts 0-3b started running for real:

RuntimeError: createActionTriggers 'Create action' not found in the @-menu after 20s. The editor add-on must be installed as a test deployment: Apps Script editor -> Deploy -> Test deployments -> Install as Add-on.

Context: Act 0 (new pre-flight) confirms the Workspace Add-on HOMEPAGE CARD (homepageTrigger) IS installed and serving the current version (v0.2.1). createActionTriggers is a SEPARATE manifest trigger (the @-menu 'Create action' editor add-on item, src/appsscript.json addOns.docs.createActionTriggers / EditorAddonCard.js) that is evidently not active in the test Google account, even though the homepage card is.

Investigate: does the editor add-on trigger require a separate/additional 'Install as Add-on' step or re-authorization distinct from the homepage card? Does it need time to propagate after deploy? Or is there a manifest/appsscript.json configuration issue specific to createActionTriggers? Once resolved, test_journey.py Act 4 (and Act 5, which depends on it) should run for real -- they currently fail hard (by design, per the new Act 0 + no-silent-warn hardening) until this is fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Act 4 (@-menu 'Create action') is available in the test Google account's editor; tests/test_journey.py Acts 4-5 run to completion (pass or fail on their own merits, not on 'trigger not found').
notes: 2026-06-11: New evidence via clasp logs (manual repro by user, not Playwright). User opened a NEW doc, typed @create, and the @-menu DID surface 'Create action' and fired CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER (00:55:16.165Z) -- so the trigger IS registered/active in the test account. This contradicts the 'not installed' hypothesis. On submit, GAS threw: 'Exception: Element does not contain the specified child element.' at _insertActionChip (EditorAddonCard.js:663, _submitCreateAction:124). Root cause (read, not yet fixed): line 663 calls cursorPara.getChildIndex(cursorElement) unconditionally; when the cursor is in an EMPTY paragraph (new doc, first line), cursor.getElement() returns the paragraph itself, so cursorElement === cursorPara and getChildIndex throws (a paragraph is not its own child). Two distinct issues now: (1) this AC (Act4 @-menu availability) may be a Playwright locator/timing issue, not an install issue -- worth re-checking _AT_MENU_CREATE locator/menu item label against live DOM; (2) separate [FIX] needed for _insertActionChip empty-paragraph crash.
close_reason: Resolved by commit cc844a0 (GTaskSheet-5vr6): _insertActionChip empty-paragraph cursor fix + GasLogger.flush() on all _submitCreateAction return paths. Confirmed via 2026-06-11 test_journey.py runs: Act 4's @-menu 'Create action' trigger fires, CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER.done is logged, and the chip is inserted (AI-14) -- AC met (Acts 4-5 run on their own merits, not blocked by 'trigger not found' or the empty-paragraph crash).

description:

title: [INF] T24-Step2: Emit drained expectations as JUnit properties
description:
Part 2 of 3 in T24 (generated traceability) implementation. Depends on Step 1 (gts-8euh) — read its completion notes for the agreed tag format before starting.

After Step 1, each Expectation has a stable AC tag. This step wires those tags into the JUnit output by emitting record_property() calls in session.checkpoint() after each successful drain. The existing --junitxml in pyproject.toml already writes test-results/junit/pytest.xml; this step adds <property> entries per drained (AC x surface) expectation to each <testcase> node.

CONTEXT LOADING (start here from a clear session):

  bd show GTaskSheet-<this-id>          # re-read this description
  Read scn/engine.py lines 146-253      # drain() — returns list[str] warnings; note what is available at drain time
  Read scn/session.py lines 492-540     # checkpoint() method — this is where record_property calls go
  Read tests/conftest.py                # existing pytest fixtures; look for 'request' usage
  Read tests/test_journey.py lines 44-75  # scn fixture setup — does not yet accept request
  Read DevStandard/knowledge-base/methodology/testing/bdd/sdlc-testing-principles.md  # T24 — traceable unit is drained (AC x surface) expectation

WHAT TO DO:
1. Modify CheckpointEngine.drain() to return not just warnings but also a list of drained (tag, surface, pass/warn) tuples — one per successfully retired surface. This is the T24 traceable unit.
2. Thread pytest's 'request' fixture into ScenarioSession. Recommended approach: add optional 'request=None' parameter to ScenarioSession.__init__() and new_doc(); callers that have request pass it, others pass None (non-journey tests are unaffected).
3. In session.checkpoint(), after engine.drain() returns, call request.record_property(f'ac.{tag}.{surface}', 'PASS') for each drained tuple (when request is not None).
4. Update the scn fixture in tests/test_journey.py (and test_sync_all.py if refactored) to pass request to ScenarioSession.new_doc().
5. Run a single journey test and inspect test-results/junit/pytest.xml to confirm <properties> appear on the test_journey testcase node with the expected ac.* keys.
6. Run full pytest suite to confirm no regressions.

ENGINE RETURN CHANGE — minimal invasive pattern:
  drain() currently returns list[str] (warnings).
  Extend to return tuple[list[str], list[tuple[str,str,str]]]: (warnings, drained_records).
  drained_records = [(tag, surface.value, 'PASS'|'WARN') for each retired surface].
  session.checkpoint() already captures the return; extend the unpack there.

- Do not build the gap-diff registry here; that is Step 3.
- WARN-severity drained expectations should emit 'WARN' not 'PASS' so the gap-diff can distinguish.

2. ScenarioSession accepts optional pytest request; non-journey callers unaffected.

title: [INF] Design: test strategy and scenario matrix for Team Scope sync
description: Design the test scenario matrix for Team Scope sync: enumerate all scenarios (happy path, no-match, UpdateDoc override, idempotency, security gate, edge cases), specify entry-point call-sites, identify new run_fixture routes needed, and document open seams. Output: a design note that the [TST] bead works from directly, with no knowledge of implementation code.
design:
## Test Design — Team Scope sync and security guard

### Entry-point coverage invariant

Every state-modifying entry point must appear as the call-site in ≥1 scenario.

| Entry point | GAS function | Test call-site |
|-------------|-------------|---------------|
| Sync (auto-assign) | `syncDocument(docId)` | `scn.sync()` HTTP fixture |
| Sync (UpdateDoc override) | `syncDocument(docId)` | `scn.sync()` after `run_fixture('set_docdata_sync_status', {fileId, syncStatus:'UpdateDoc', teamId})` |
| Sync (idempotent re-sync) | `syncDocument(docId)` | `scn.sync()` called twice |
| Sync (sticky assignment after move) | `syncDocument(docId)` | `scn.sync()` after `run_fixture('move_doc_to_folder', {docId, folderId})` |
| Security gate | `assertTeamAccess(teamId, ss)` | `scn.run_fixture('assert_team_access', {teamId})` |

### Entry-point registry and gap-diff (T24 binding on new harness work)

The ratified T24 status note (sdlc-testing-principles.md, 2026-06-09) flags the entry-point
half of the gap-diff (T1/T17) as project-wide tracked debt, but makes it **binding on new
harness work** — EPIC-B must build it, not defer it.

- Add `ENTRY_POINT_REGISTRY: dict[str, str]` to `scn/contract.py` (sibling to `AC_REGISTRY`,
  same I6 single-source convention), seeded with the two entry points from the table above:
  `"syncDocument"` and `"assertTeamAccess"`.
- Each scenario's drained `expect()` (see T24 traceability section below) additionally tags
  the entry point it exercises, e.g. `expect(..., tag="teamscope direct-match",
  entry_point="syncDocument", surfaces={SHEET})`, emitted as `ep.<entry_point>.<surface>`
  alongside `ac.<tag>.<surface>`.
- Extend `scripts/check_coverage.py` with a second diff: `ENTRY_POINT_REGISTRY` keys vs.
  emitted `ep.*` properties, reported the same way as the AC diff (covered/uncovered, exit 1
  on gaps).

This is the minimal slice that proves the entry-point diff shape for `me6w.6`; it does not
need to cover entry points outside this epic.

---

### Fixture prerequisites

The following must exist in the live ActionSheet before tests run:

| Fixture | Rows required |
|---------|--------------|
| TeamData | ≥2 teams for the abstract scenarios (S2/S3/S5/S6/S7): `Board` (Folder A), `Membership` (Folder B). PLUS the folder-hierarchy acceptance fixture below for S1a/S1b/S1c/S8. |
| DocData | Empty at test start; rows created by sync under test. |
| Test document | Created fresh per journey via `begin_journey_session`; placed in a subfolder of Folder A (Board's folder) by a `run_fixture('move_doc_to_folder', {docId, folderId})` fixture call. |

New `run_fixture` routes needed (add to `TestWebApp.js`):
- `set_docdata_row` — upsert a DocData row with specified fields (for override setup).
- `get_docdata_row` — read a DocData row by `fileId` (for assertions).
- `get_team_scope` — read the document's Drive `appProperty` `teamScope` (for assertions).
- `move_doc_to_folder` — move the test doc into a specified folder (for walk-setup).
- `assert_team_access` — call `assertTeamAccess(teamId, ss)` and return `{ok}` or error.

#### Folder-hierarchy acceptance fixture (S1a/S1b/S1c/S8)

Drive folder hierarchy (configured via `local.settings.json`, three distinct folder IDs):

```
local.settings.testTeamA        — parent folder
└── local.settings.testTeamAChild  — child of testTeamA
└── ... (several levels) ...
    └── local.settings.testTeamADeep  — multi-level descendant of testTeamA,
                                          NOT under testTeamAChild, no
                                          intermediate folder is registered
                                          in TeamData
```

> **Setup precondition — local.settings.json currently does NOT match this shape**: `testTeamA`
> and `testTeamAChild` are presently set to the *same* folder ID, and `testTeamADeep` does not
> exist. Before S1a/S1b/S1c/S8 can run, `local.settings.json` must be updated with three distinct
> real Drive folder IDs forming the hierarchy above. This is a test-setup task for the `[TST]`
> bead (`me6w.6`), not something the design can fabricate.

TeamData rows required (idempotent — check-exists-or-create on test setup; **not cleaned up**
at end of run, so subsequent runs reuse the same rows):

| Team Id | Folder Id |
|---------|-----------|
| `TestTeamA` | `local.settings.testTeamA` |
| `TestTeamAChild` | `local.settings.testTeamAChild` |

(`testTeamADeep` has no TeamData row of its own — that's the point of S1c.)

Each scenario creates ONE fresh test document (no `teamScope` appProperty) directly inside the
named folder via `run_fixture('move_doc_to_folder', ...)` immediately after `begin_journey_session`,
before the first `scn.sync()`.

---

### Consistency-check assertion (single tool for S1a/S1b/S1c/S8)

Extend `verifyConsistencyForTest(docId, expected)` in `TestFixtures.js` to accept an optional
`expected.teamId`. When present, in addition to the existing docId/sheet/tracker checks, also
assert:

- `get_team_scope(docId)` (Drive appProperty `teamScope`) `== expected.teamId`
- `DocData[fileId].team_id == expected.teamId`
- `DocData[fileId]` row exists and its `doc_name`, `doc_modified`, `action_count`,
  `resolved_count` fields are populated and consistent with the current scan (same checks
  already applied to the Actions sheet, extended to cover the DocData row for this `fileId`)

This makes `verifyConsistencyForTest(docId, {teamId: ...})` the **sole assertion call** for
S1a/S1b/S1c/S8: each scenario only needs to (1) create the document under the stated initial
condition (folder placement, or a prior assignment + move), (2) call `scn.sync()`, (3) call
`verifyConsistencyForTest(docId, {teamId: <expected>})`. No bespoke per-scenario assertions
beyond the log-tag checks already shown.

---

### Scenario matrix

#### S1a — Auto-assign: doc directly in a registered team's folder
```
Given: TeamData has [TestTeamA, local.settings.testTeamA] and [TestTeamAChild, local.settings.testTeamAChild]
  AND: test doc has no teamScope appProperty, created directly in the testTeamA folder
When:  scn.sync()
Then:  verifyConsistencyForTest(docId, {teamId: 'TestTeamA'}) passes
  AND: log contains sync.teamScope.resolved { teamId: 'TestTeamA' }
```

#### S1b — Auto-assign: doc in a folder that is itself a registered (more specific) team
```
Given: same TeamData as S1a
  AND: test doc has no teamScope appProperty, created directly in the testTeamAChild folder
       (a child of testTeamA, itself registered as TestTeamAChild)
When:  scn.sync()
Then:  verifyConsistencyForTest(docId, {teamId: 'TestTeamAChild'}) passes
  AND: log contains sync.teamScope.resolved { teamId: 'TestTeamAChild' }
```
Demonstrates: the walk starts at the doc's immediate parent folder and an exact match there wins
without climbing further — a more specific sub-team folder (e.g. a "Board" folder containing a
"BoardMeetings" sub-folder registered as its own team) takes precedence over its parent.

#### S1c — Auto-assign: doc several levels below a registered team folder, no intermediate registrations
```
Given: same TeamData as S1a
  AND: test doc has no teamScope appProperty, created directly in the testTeamADeep folder
       (several levels below testTeamA, NOT under testTeamAChild, no TeamData row at any
       intermediate level)
When:  scn.sync()
Then:  verifyConsistencyForTest(docId, {teamId: 'TestTeamA'}) passes
  AND: log contains sync.teamScope.resolved { teamId: 'TestTeamA' }
```
Demonstrates: the walk climbs past multiple unregistered ancestor folders to find the nearest
registered ancestor (testTeamA) — proving the walk is not limited to a single hop.

#### S2 — No match: folder not in TeamData
```
Given: test doc has no teamScope appProperty
  AND: doc is in a folder NOT in TeamData
When:  scn.sync()
Then:  doc Drive appProperty 'teamScope' is absent or blank
  AND: DocData[fileId].team_id == ''
  AND: log contains sync.teamScope.walk.no-match
```

#### S3 — UpdateDoc override (DocData wins)
```
Given: doc already has teamScope == 'Board'
  AND: run_fixture set_docdata_row { fileId, syncStatus:'UpdateDoc', teamId:'Membership' }
When:  scn.sync()
Then:  doc Drive appProperty 'teamScope' == 'Membership'
  AND: DocData[fileId].team_id == 'Membership'
  AND: DocData[fileId].sync_status == ''   (cleared)
  AND: log contains sync.teamScope.overridden { teamId: 'Membership' }
```

#### S4 — Idempotency: second sync makes no Drive property writes
```
Given: S1 completed (doc already has teamScope == 'Board', DocData row exists)
When:  scn.sync() (second call, no doc edits)
Then:  doc Drive appProperty 'teamScope' still == 'Board'
  AND: DocData[fileId].team_id still == 'Board'
  AND: log does NOT contain sync.teamScope.resolved or sync.teamScope.overridden
```
Implementation note: assert via log-tag absence (check `sync.teamScope.resolved` count = 0 on second sync).

#### S5 — Security gate allows valid access
```
Given: TeamData has [Board, FolderA]
  AND: active user has read access to FolderA
When:  run_fixture assert_team_access { teamId:'Board' }
Then:  response { ok: true }
```
(This covers the positive path; the negative path requires a second account — deferred per
EPIC-D J-ACCESS-FILTER journey design. S5 documents the contract; negative assertion is flagged
as a test-design open seam: the teamId/folderId lookup path must be testable with a stubbed
folder reference.)

#### S6 — TeamData missing: sync completes, no assignment
```
Given: TeamData tab is empty (no rows)
  AND: doc has no teamScope
When:  scn.sync()
Then:  doc teamScope remains absent/blank
  AND: sync completes without error
  AND: log contains sync.teamScope.walk.no-match
```

#### S7 — UpdateDoc with blank Team Id: SyncStatus cleared, no crash
```
Given: run_fixture set_docdata_row { fileId, syncStatus:'UpdateDoc', teamId:'' }
When:  scn.sync()
Then:  sync completes without error
  AND: DocData[fileId].sync_status == ''   (cleared)
  AND: doc teamScope is blank or unchanged
  AND: log contains sync.teamScope.override-blank warning
```

#### S8 — Sticky assignment: moving an already-assigned doc to another team's folder does NOT reassign
```
Given: S1a completed (doc teamScope == 'TestTeamA', DocData[fileId].team_id == 'TestTeamA')
  AND: run_fixture move_doc_to_folder { docId, folderId: local.settings.testTeamAChild }
When:  scn.sync()
Then:  verifyConsistencyForTest(docId, {teamId: 'TestTeamA'}) passes  (unchanged — NOT 'TestTeamAChild')
  AND: log does NOT contain sync.teamScope.resolved or sync.teamScope.overridden
```
Demonstrates: once `teamScope` is set, folder location no longer drives assignment — the
document remains associated with its original team even after moving into a folder that would
itself match a different team (`TestTeamAChild`) on a fresh walk.

---

### Open seams (register per ADR-0013)

- **Negative security-gate assertion** (access denied path): requires a restricted second account
  (same infrastructure as J-ACCESS-FILTER in EPIC-D). Flag as a test seam: the `assertTeamAccess`
  function must accept an injected `folderId` override for unit-level negative testing.
  Acceptance criteria for the negative path is deferred to the J-ACCESS-FILTER journey (EPIC-D).

- **`teamScope` routing-key invariant**: S1 and S3 assert the Team Id value (e.g., `'Board'`),
  not a folder ID — confirming that `teamScope` is the stable team identifier, not a Drive ID.
  Harden tests should keep this assertion; future per-team sheet routing must NOT change what
  `teamScope` stores.

---

### T24 traceability — AC registration and emission

All 10 scenarios (S1a/S1b/S1c/S2-S8) have AC ids registered in `scn/contract.AC_REGISTRY` under
the `teamscope *` prefix (e.g. `teamscope direct-match`, `teamscope sticky-after-move`). Per T24,
coverage is generated from emitted `ac.<tag>.<surface>` JUnit properties — this design must
specify HOW each scenario emits one.

**Gap**: scenarios S1a/S1b/S1c/S8 are built around `verify_consistency(docId, {teamId})`, which
raises `AssertionError` directly and is **not** part of the `expect()`/drain queue that emits
`ac.*` properties (the only existing emission path is the drained-expectation loop in
`session.py` around line 540).

**Resolved (per ratified T24 status note, sdlc-testing-principles.md 2026-06-09)**: emission
must use the existing drained-expectation shape — a parallel `Session.record_ac()` helper that
appends directly to `user_properties` would be a second emission path, which T24's "no parallel
enumeration" constraint (line 101) prohibits. Each scenario:

- Enqueues a drained expectation: `expect(..., tag="teamscope direct-match", surfaces={SHEET})`
  whose check reads `DocData[fileId].team_id` (and the Drive `teamScope` appProperty) and
  compares to the expected value; the existing drain/checkpoint emits the
  `ac.teamscope direct-match.SHEET` property. No new helper.
- `verify_consistency(docId, {teamId})` remains the durable-state assertion (T5); the drained
  `expect()` is the T24 traceability hook layered alongside it, not a replacement.

S2-S7 (existing scenarios, log-tag based) need the same treatment — they currently assert via
`wait_for_log` with no `ac.*` emission either. This mechanism applies uniformly to all 10
scenarios.

---

### Fixture implementation notes

- `move_doc_to_folder`: uses Drive REST API `files.update` with `addParents`/`removeParents`.
  Must use the OAuth token of the deployer (sheet owner) since the test doc lives in Drive.
  Add to `TestWebApp.js` (context ③, runs as deployer).

- `get_docdata_row`: reads DocData tab directly from the ActionSheet. Returns all 8 columns as
  a keyed object using `CONTRACT_SCHEMA.sheetDocData.columnsByField`.

- `set_docdata_row`: upserts a DocData row. Uses `_getOrUpsertDocDataRow` internally.

- Log-tag assertions use the existing `gas_log.py` `wait_for_log` helper (already in project).
  Tag-absence assertions use `wait_for_log` with a short timeout + inversion.
acceptance_criteria: Design artifact is present and covers: (1) >=8 named scenarios with Given/When/Then, including the folder-hierarchy acceptance fixture (S1a/S1b/S1c: direct-folder, more-specific-subfolder, and multi-level-walk team resolution) and the sticky-assignment-after-move scenario (S8); (2) entry-point call-site table mapping each scenario to the GAS function exercised; (3) list of new run_fixture routes with their signatures, including get_team_scope; (4) fixture setup requirements (TeamData rows TestTeamA/TestTeamAChild, local.settings.json folder hierarchy testTeamA/testTeamAChild/testTeamADeep, idempotent no-cleanup setup); (5) the verifyConsistencyForTest extension (expected.teamId) as the single assertion mechanism for the folder-hierarchy scenarios; (6) open seams documented; (7) T24 emission resolved to drained expect() (no parallel record_ac helper), applied uniformly to all 10 scenarios; (8) ENTRY_POINT_REGISTRY (syncDocument, assertTeamAccess) added to scn/contract.py with ep.<entry_point>.<surface> emission and a corresponding check_coverage.py diff.
close_reason: AC item 8 completed: ENTRY_POINT_REGISTRY (syncDocument, assertTeamAccess) added to scn/contract.py; ep.<entry_point>.<surface> emission wired through Expectation→engine.drain→session; scripts/check_coverage.py extended with a parallel entry-point gap-diff (covered/uncovered, exit 1 on gaps). Verified: 85 offline tests pass (incl. new entry_point-propagation test); end-to-end diff proven green when both entry points emitted. AC items 1-7 (scenario matrix S1a/S1b/S1c/S2-S8, entry-point call-site table, run_fixture routes, fixture setup, verifyConsistencyForTest extension, open seams, T24 drained-expect resolution) already present in design field + staging doc.

description: Slice-BUILD bead. Per ADR-0013 Slice fidelity. Smoke asserts DURABLE INVARIANTS ONLY: (a) a DocData row round-trips (write then read back identical); (b) Resolved Count is computed via the single shared isResolved authority (no redefined status set).
