design:
R5-impl DESIGN — consistency single-source (authority split). Authored by R5-design (.13). Source: epic Coordination Log "R5 SEED"; 2026-06-05-Test-Review.md §R5 (closes F3); atdd-lifecycle.md §16.7.

== AUTHORITY MODEL (exactly three classes; no fourth notion) ==

1. SERVER authority = scn.verify_consistency(scope=DOC)  [scn/session.py:324]
   The ONLY path any test/helper may use to reach the GAS routes verify_action_rows + verify_chip_integrity. Sees LIVE doc state the download can miss (globalId linkage, rendered chip icons). Run standalone OR internally by every INTEGRITY checkpoint (via the read_consistency closure, session.py:511-519). Implements §16.7 checklist + chip integrity (6ov.8). Raises AssertionError on violations.

2. ARTIFACT authority = verify(on=DOC|SHEET|TRACKER) + checkpoint, over the downloaded .docx/.xlsx via the surface readers (DocReader/SheetReader/TrackerReader). Truth = "what the user downloads" (row field values). NEVER calls a GAS consistency route.

3. NO-consistency = residual JS smoke + probe layer. Asserts only liveness/shell/probe identity. Calls NO consistency route; defines NO third notion.

== CHECK-CLASS -> AUTHORITY TABLE (the documented split) ==
- globalId present/valid (linkage)            -> SERVER  (does not survive docx export; §16 line 391)
- chip status icon present+correct, chip link valid, all occurrences identical -> SERVER (verify_chip_integrity)
- doc<->sheet cross-presence (every doc AI in sheet; every sheet AI in doc)    -> SERVER (verify_action_rows)
- row field values (action_id, status, assignee email/name, sheet columns) on the downloaded artifact -> ARTIFACT (verify(on=...))
- sheet col7 doc_name/link present, col10 sync_status not an error state       -> ARTIFACT (currently done inside verify_consistency(scope=SHEET); see decision below)

== THE TWO COMPETING NOTIONS TO REMOVE (the F3 drift) ==
Both are ORPHANS (no live callers — confirmed by grep) and each is a second/third path to "consistent". Deleting them makes scn.verify_consistency() the single server authority:

A. tests/helpers/doc_inspect.py :: verify_doc_chip_integrity()  (approx lines 164-218)
   A SECOND Python path that POSTs verify_chip_integrity directly, bypassing scn.verify_consistency(). No callers. -> DELETE the function and any imports left unused by its removal.

B. tests/playwright/addon_helpers.js :: verifyConsistency  (doc+body approx lines 182-211; exported at line 276)
   The JS "third notion". smoke.test.js imports only openDocSidebar; probe.test.js imports openDocSidebar + waitForLogEntry — neither imports verifyConsistency, so removal is safe. -> DELETE the function and drop it from module.exports.

== DECISION (resolve the one ambiguity; recommended option first) ==
verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) (session.py:330-345) is ARTIFACT-class (reads xlsx, asserts col7/col10) yet lives under the consistency-authority method name.
RECOMMENDED: KEEP the method as-is (do NOT add a new method or move callers) and DOCUMENT the scope split in the docstring: scope=DOC = SERVER authority; scope=SHEET = an artifact-side convenience check over the downloaded xlsx. Rationale: minimal churn, no caller migration (test_journey.py:249 already uses scope=SHEET), and the authority each scope represents becomes explicit. This keeps "one documented authority per check class" true without a rename.

== BUILD TASKS (.14) ==
1. Delete competing notion A (doc_inspect.verify_doc_chip_integrity) + dead imports.
2. Delete competing notion B (addon_helpers.verifyConsistency) + its export entry.
3. Add/extend the verify_consistency docstring to state the scope=DOC=SERVER / scope=SHEET=ARTIFACT split and that it is the SINGLE server authority (no other code path may post verify_action_rows / verify_chip_integrity).
4. Confirm (no code change expected) the ARTIFACT path verify(on=DOC|SHEET|TRACKER) never reaches a GAS consistency route.
5. Do NOT touch GAS src/ — verify_action_rows/verify_chip_integrity (src/WebApp.js, src/ContractSchema.js) are the contract surface and stay untouched. The durable DESIGN.md/ADR write of the authority split is R5-docs (.15); .14 only lands the code in the single-authority state .15 documents.

== ACCEPTANCE (.14) — maps to .11 stub AC ==
- Exactly one documented consistency authority per check class (the table above).
- No test/helper defines a third notion: orphan JS verifyConsistency and orphan Python verify_doc_chip_integrity are gone.
- grep guard returns CLEAN: `grep -rn "verify_action_rows\|verify_chip_integrity" tests/ scn/ tests/playwright/` shows refs ONLY in scn/session.py (the server authority) and tests/test_scn_session.py (its unit test) — no doc_inspect, no addon_helpers.
- Every server-consistency call routes through scn.verify_consistency(); smoke/probe call no consistency route.
- Existing pytest stays green: test_scn_session.py::test_verify_consistency_posts_verify_route, test_journey, test_sidebar, test_tracker_view_only.

== QUALITY GATES (.14) ==
- /mnt/c/dev/venvs/uv1/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_scn_session.py tests/test_sidebar.py tests/test_tracker_view_only.py tests/test_journey_acts_1_3.py -q
- npx playwright test --list  (confirm smoke+probe only; no verifyConsistency reference)
- grep guard above returns CLEAN.

== CONTRACT / NO-SHARED-CONTEXT NOTE ==
TST-side authority spec. Touches only scn/ + tests/ + tests/playwright/ JS helpers. The GAS routes are the shared contract and are untouched. DESIGN PENDING is cleared — this field is complete.

Extended verify_consistency() docstring in scn/session.py to declare scope=DOC=SERVER authority / scope=SHEET=ARTIFACT split and single-authority invariant. Grep guard clean: verify_action_rows/verify_chip_integrity refs only in scn/session.py + tests/test_scn_session.py. 33/34 pytest pass; 1 pre-existing failure (test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync UI status read) confirmed unchanged by stash-test.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
0. CONTRACT (the only shared artifact — do not read the JS test bodies for assertions)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Acts you call (all exist, R2-impl .5 / R1-impl .2 — names verbatim):
  scn.ui.open_sidebar(addon_name="GActionSheet", timeout="15s") -> Card
  scn.ui.sidebar_sync(timeout="60s")                 # Sync Now button (bootstrap + refresh)
  scn.ui.insert_tracker_button(timeout="30s")        # Insert tracker button
  scn.ui.sidebar_set_status(target, status, timeout="15s")  # per-row status ctrl
  scn.ui.read_current() -> list[ai]   # SINGLE ai: first AI-N header of _current_card
  scn.verify(a, on=Surface.UI, within="10s")         # drained UI evidence (identity+status)
  scn.verify(a, on=Surface.TRACKER[, status=...])    # artifact-truth row fields
  scn.checkpoint(STEP, on=frozenset({Surface.UI}))   # drain UI live, in-browser
  scn.checkpoint(INTEGRITY)                           # docx+xlsx+tracker+consistency drain
  scn.verify_consistency(scope=DOC)                   # GAS server-truth authority (R5)
GAS completion log tag (already waited on inside the acts): sync.complete (per docId).
Consistency route output schema asserted by verify_consistency(scope=DOC):
  verify_action_rows -> {ok:bool, issues:[str], counts:{floating,tracker,matched}}
  verify_chip_integrity -> {violations:[{paragraph,issue}]}  (raises on any)

BINDING constraints (G1/G2):
  - UI evidence is IDENTITY(action_id)+STATUS ONLY. Row TEXT / count text / control
    presence are NOT ai state — never enqueue them as UI expectations.
  - read_current() reads ONE ai (first AI-N card). Do NOT enqueue 3 UI expectations
    expecting 3 sidebar rows — multi-row truth is TRACKER's job (verify(on=TRACKER) per ai).
  - UI verification ALWAYS routes verify(on=UI,within=) + checkpoint(STEP,on=UI).
    NEVER verify on=UI through INTEGRITY (INTEGRITY obs = {DOC,SHEET,TRACKER}).

1. FILE / PLACEMENT PLAN

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
2. PER-JS-TEST MIGRATION TABLE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
A) sidebar_action_list.test.js

title: [TST] R2-impl: add normalized scn.ui acts + one-browser-per-journey fixture
description: Implement the UI act surface specified by R2-design so UI mutations are real call-sites (sidebar Sync Now, Insert tracker button, sidebar delete/status) usable inside a Python journey, reusing the single module-scoped browser. Build to the --design populated by R2-design.
design:
R2-design spec (from gts-80mo.4). Build strictly to this. §refs are docs/atdd/atdd-lifecycle.md. Depends on R1 (UI surface drainable) — already DONE; see epic Coordination Log G1/G2 + R1-impl facts.

=== GOAL ===
Formalize "a Python journey fires Playwright as an act, reads UI as a verification" so every UI mutation is a REAL user entry point (true call-site), not the HTTP fixture shortcut. Add 4 normalized scn.ui acts, keep the one-browser-per-journey fixture, route all UI verification through the queue (R1), and obey the cost rule (§16.3 #5).

=== ACTS TO ADD (scn/ui.py, UiDriver) ===
Each is a state mutation → exactly one entry point (§16.3 #1). Match existing style: keyword-only string timeouts ("5s"), return None for mutations, driver owns ALL selectors/iframe/wait knowledge (§16.8, §16.11 #8) — no Playwright objects leak to the scenario layer. Add private selector constants alongside the existing _CARD_* / _FORM_* block; scenarios never see them.

1. sidebar_sync(self, *, timeout: str = "60s") -> None
   Real call-site: the homepage sidebar "Sync Now" button (live user sync). Replaces the scn.sync() doPost shortcut as the sync entry point (Sync Scenario C).
   Behavior: ensure the homepage sidebar card is open (reuse open_sidebar(); set _current_card); locate the Sync button inside the card frame by accessible name (button:has-text(/sync/i) or [aria-label*="Sync"]); click; wait out the busy/loading spinner (_BUSY) up to timeout (cold sync is slow → 60s default), same busy→return pattern as set_status(). Do NOT poll the sheet here — durable convergence is forced by the journey (a following HTTP scn.sync() per §16.11 #4, then INTEGRITY). This is the LIVE trigger, so no onActionSheetEdit/Dirty replication is needed (§16.11 #2).

2. insert_tracker_button(self, *, timeout: str = "30s") -> None
   Real call-site: the homepage sidebar "Insert tracker" button. Replaces the scn.insert_tracker() fixture shortcut.
   Behavior: ensure sidebar open; locate the insert-tracker button in the card frame by accessible name (/insert tracker/i or /tracker/i); click; wait out busy. Mutates the doc (tracker table inserted/refreshed).

3. sidebar_delete(self, target: ai, *, timeout: str = "15s") -> None
   Real call-site: the homepage sidebar per-row "Delete action" button. Replaces the scn.delete(ai) fixture shortcut.
   Behavior: ensure sidebar open; scope to the row matching target.action_id (the homepage card renders rows as "AI-N • …"; see Act 3b in tests/test_journey.py); within that row locate '[aria-label="Delete action"]' (selector already proven in Act 3b); click; if a confirm control appears, confirm; wait out busy. Identity addressing is by action_id (the visible AI-N row carries the same identity as the model's globalId, §16.11 #3).

4. sidebar_set_status(self, target: ai, status: str, *, timeout: str = "15s") -> None
   Real call-site: the homepage sidebar per-row status control (Sync Scenario A). Replaces the scn.set_status(ai, status) fixture shortcut.
   Behavior: ensure sidebar open; scope to the target.action_id row; open/click its status control; select `status`; wait out busy.
   NOTE: this is DISTINCT from the existing set_status(card, status), which operates on a HOVERED preview Card. Keep both. The existing one stays the preview-card gesture (takes a Card); the new sidebar_set_status takes an ai and drives the homepage card. Do not rename the existing method.

Private helpers (driver-internal): a _sidebar_card() that idempotently ensures open_sidebar() ran and returns/sets _current_card; a _sidebar_row(action_id) -> Locator that scopes per-row button lookups by the "AI-N •" row text inside the card frame.

=== MAPPING: new act -> HTTP shortcut it replaces as a true call-site (§16.9 Acts table) ===
sidebar_sync()              <- scn.sync()           (Scenario C) ; entry point: Sync Now button
insert_tracker_button()    <- scn.insert_tracker()              ; entry point: Insert tracker button
sidebar_delete(ai)         <- scn.delete(ai)                    ; entry point: per-row Delete action button
sidebar_set_status(ai,st)  <- scn.set_status(ai,st)  (Scenario A); entry point: per-row status control
Each gives an existing sidebar/tracker behavior a real-UI call-site twin, satisfying the entry-point coverage invariant (the entry point itself is the call-site, not the mechanism it delegates to).

=== VERIFICATION ROUTING (R1, queue-routed — never raw Playwright in the scenario) ===
Two kinds, keep them separate:
(a) LIVE UI feedback the card itself shows (identity + status only, per G1): enqueue verify(target, on=Surface.UI, within="10s") and drain with checkpoint(STEP, on=frozenset({Surface.UI})). read_current() (R1-impl) reads action_id from the "AI-N:" header and status from the rendered status icon of self._current_card. For a delete, use scn.expect_absent(target, on=Surface.UI) drained at a UI STEP.
    G2 BINDING: UI state is LIVE-ONLY and drained at a STEP in the Playwright phase. NEVER route on=Surface.UI through INTEGRITY — INTEGRITY's observable set is {DOC,SHEET,TRACKER}(+CONSISTENCY) and excludes UI (§16.7).
    read_current() returns a SINGLE ai from the first "AI-N:" header in _current_card. For per-action UI verification of a specific row, hover that action's preview card first (existing hover()+set/_current_card path) so read_current() reads that action; the multi-row homepage card is for FIRING acts, not for per-row UI drains. Do not extend read_current() — that is R1's contract.
(b) DURABLE correctness that the UI mutation really happened: verify on DOC/SHEET/TRACKER and drain at INTEGRITY at the HTTP-phase boundary / journey end. This is durable-surface state through INTEGRITY (correct), NOT "UI via INTEGRITY". After an async UI mutation (sidebar_set_status, sidebar_delete), force convergence with a following HTTP scn.sync() before the INTEGRITY check (§16.11 #4).

=== ONE-BROWSER-PER-JOURNEY FIXTURE CONTRACT (keep as-is; make it the documented standard) ===
- The module-scoped browser_page fixture in tests/test_journey.py is the canonical, correct pattern: launch Chromium ONCE with .auth/user.json storage_state, yield one Page for the whole journey, tear down (ctx.close/browser.close) at module end. Do not change its scope.
- UiDriver is attached once: scn.ui = UiDriver(browser_page, doc_id=scn.doc_id). ALL UI acts of a journey share that one Page/browser. NEVER launch a browser per act; NEVER open a second context.
- Non-UI work (append_paragraph, edit_sheet, sync via HTTP, queries, INTEGRITY captures) stays entirely on the cheap HTTP/fixture path and must not touch the browser.

=== COST RULE (§16.3 #5; transcribe verbatim into R2-docs .6) ===
Reserve Playwright for surfaces only the UI can show, and for exercising a real UI entry point as the call-site. Everything that does not require the browser stays on the HTTP fixture path (far cheaper). The browser cold start is amortized across all UI acts of one journey — one launch, many acts. During the Playwright phase prefer TARGETED single-surface expectations (verify(on=UI, within=) drained by checkpoint(STEP, on=UI), or a cheap verify(on=DOC) probe) and reserve INTEGRITY for HTTP-phase boundaries and the journey end. This is the explicit answer to "Playwright is expensive to spin up": amortize the one cold start, and keep non-UI acts off the browser entirely.

=== UNIT TESTS (AC3) ===
Cover each new act in tests/test_scn_ui.py (NOTE: actual path is tests/test_scn_ui.py, not scn/test_scn_ui.py as the bead AC text says). Reuse the existing mock_page (MagicMock) + driver fixtures and the TestHover/_setup_card_frame style. For each act assert: it locates the documented selector inside the card frame, calls click(), and waits out _BUSY (visible→hidden). No live browser needed.

=== JOURNEY GREEN AGAINST deploy:test (AC4) ===
Convert at least ONE Act in tests/test_journey.py to use a new sidebar act as the call-site (recommended: Act 3 insert_tracker via insert_tracker_button(), or Act 2 sync via sidebar_sync()). Guard it with the same warn-and-continue D4 pattern (try/except → warnings.warn + continue) so a deployment without the installed add-on does not fail the suite. Verify the mutation durably on TRACKER/SHEET at INTEGRITY + verify_consistency, and optionally add a verify(on=Surface.UI, within=)+checkpoint(STEP, on=UI) live probe. Deploy with `npm run deploy:test` (never raw clasp); run the journey; it must be green.

=== DO / DON'T ===
- DO honor §16 vocabulary verbatim: act / verify(on=...) / checkpoint(STEP, on=Surface.UI) / verify(on=Surface.UI, within=...) / INTEGRITY / expect_absent.
- DON'T write UI assertions as raw card.frame.get_by_text(...).wait_for(...) in the scenario (that was deviation D2, removed by R1) — route through the queue.
- DON'T route on=Surface.UI through INTEGRITY (G2).
- DON'T rename or change existing acts (create_action, set_status, hover, open_sidebar, locate); only ADD.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: (1) the scn.ui acts named in R2-design exist and each drives a real user entry point (verified by a journey using them as the call-site, not the HTTP shortcut); (2) the browser is launched once per journey (module-scoped) and shared across all UI acts; (3) scn/test_scn_ui.py covers the new acts with a mocked Page; (4) a journey exercising at least one UI act is green against deploy:test.
close_reason: 4 sidebar acts added (sidebar_sync, insert_tracker_button, sidebar_delete, sidebar_set_status) with private helpers and selectors. 25 unit tests added; 71 total in test_scn_ui.py green. test_journey.py Act 3 converted to insert_tracker_button() with D4 fallback. One-browser-per-journey fixture confirmed as documented standard.

title: [TST] Test review feedback — unify Playwright with the scn scenario model (R1–R3)
description:
Act on the 2026-06-05 Test Review (repo-root `2026-06-05-Test-Review.md`). The review found two parallel end-to-end stacks: the mature Python `scn/` scenario harness (already integrates Playwright via scn/ui.py and fires UI gestures inside one reused browser per journey) and a separate, duplicated JS Playwright suite (tests/playwright/*.test.js) that ignores the §16 model. This epic delivers the three highest-leverage recommendations:
- R1 — make UI a first-class drained surface (engine read(UI) + queue-routed UI expectations); closes review finding F1.
- R2 — standardize 'a Python journey fires Playwright as an act/verification step' with the one-browser-per-journey cost rule; closes F5 partially, formalizes the existing pattern.
- R3 — migrate the JS suite's unique coverage into scn journeys/focused tests and trim JS to a smoke/probe gate; closes F2/F4.

Canonical model: docs/atdd/atdd-lifecycle.md §16; harness design: docs/atdd/scenario-harness-design.md. Source review: 2026-06-05-Test-Review.md §3 (findings) and §4 (R1–R3).
notes:
## Model-assignment label legend
Each child carries exactly one model:* label, chosen by activity complexity:
- model:opus — design/architecture beads whose deliverable is a written spec that POPULATES the --design field of its paired build bead, unblocking it for a clean-context build.
- model:sonnet — well-specified build/implementation beads that consume the opus design (or §16 directly) and may carry their own docs.
- model:haiku — small mechanical beads with no design latitude (helper extraction, file deletion, mechanical doc edits).

## Build pattern (per recommendation R1/R2/R3)
opus design bead → writes the spec into the sonnet impl bead's --design → sonnet implements → haiku (or sonnet) does the doc/cleanup. Deps enforce the order.

## Coordination Log

R4 (minimal JS layer) intentionally NOT separately tracked — absorbed by .8/.9. Push deferred until R1 (.1-.3) is done and tests pass.
- 2026-06-05 (R1-design .1 → .2 design done): Two contract-level decisions recorded for the R1 build and downstream R2/R3.
  G1 (UI card evidence): UI matching is scoped to IDENTITY (action_id) + STATUS only — durable text/assignee/name correctness stays owned by DOC/SHEET/TRACKER. read_current() pulls action_id from the 'AI-N:' card header and status from the rendered brand-NUTS status ICON's aria-label/alt (the ACTIVE status, NOT a clickable status-button option). Open detail for the .2 impl owner: disambiguating the current status when several status controls/icons coexist in the card — prefer the chip/doc rendered status icon over option buttons. assertions.check_present_consistent gets a Surface.UI carve-out mirroring the existing TRACKER assignee_name carve-out.
  G2 (INTEGRITY excludes UI): binding decision refining harness-design §4.4 — UI is LIVE-ONLY and drained at a STEP in the Playwright phase; INTEGRITY's observable set is {DOC,SHEET,TRACKER}(+CONSISTENCY), NOT 'all author surfaces'. A queued UI expectation that no STEP drains correctly fails the §4.6 drain invariant at close(). R2 (.4/.5 — Python-drives-Playwright acts) and R3 (.7/.8 — JS migration) must route UI state checks through verify(on=UI, within=…)+STEP, never via INTEGRITY.
2026-06-05 (R1-impl .2 → done): UI surface now first-class and drainable. Key impl facts for R2/R3:

title: [FEA] Carry forward open actions from previous meetings
description:
A user wants to pull open actions from one or more previous meeting documents into the current document as floating actions, via a sidebar panel that lists all currently-open actions in the team space.

## Context
This touches identity, cross-document references, and status propagation. Key design questions are unresolved before implementation can begin — this issue is a spike to produce the decisions and a pre-code contract.

**Workflow (as described):**
A window (sidebar panel) displays currently-open actions across the team space. The user selects which actions to carry forward; they are inserted into the current document as floating actions.

**Open design questions:**

1. **Action identity on import**
   - Option A: Keep the original action ID (e.g. `AI-3`) — simple, but creates an ID collision if the same action appears in two docs simultaneously.
   - Option B: Assign a new action ID in the target document — clean identity, loses direct link to origin.
   - Option C: Encode the origin using a doc-registry shorthand, e.g. `D-1/AI-3` — preserves provenance, requires a doc-ID registry (D-1 → docId mapping) stored somewhere (team settings doc? local.settings.json?).

2. **Status update in the source document**
   - When an action is forwarded, should its status in the original document become `(Forwarded)`?
   - Should the original paragraph's chip/link be updated to point to the new document?
   - Partial forwarding (forwarded into multiple docs) — last-writer-wins or append multiple forward links?

3. **Doc-ID registry**
   - If Option C is chosen, where does the D-1 → docId map live?
   - Who writes to it (on first sync? on import? manually)?
   - How does it survive document deletion or rename?

4. **Link behaviour after forwarding**
   - The ActionSheet chip in the original doc: should clicking it navigate to the new doc's action?
   - If an action is forwarded twice, what does the chain look like?

**Minimum use-case set to decide:**
- UC-1: Forward a single open action to the current doc (happy path).
- UC-2: Action is already closed in source — blocked or skipped?
- UC-3: Same action forwarded to two different docs — what happens?
- UC-4: Source doc is deleted after forwarding — does the forwarded action still work?
notes: Pre-code contract required before either IMP or TST ticket can start. Decision spike output: chosen identity scheme, status-propagation rule, registry location. Suggest an ADR for the identity decision.
close_reason: Resolved by yb2w per Stuart; closing.

title: [TST] UC-C: cover direct tracker refresh and view-only overwrite flows
description: UC-C review found two remaining coverage gaps in the tracker-table subsystem. The original UC-C fixture scenarios `uc_c_refresh` and `uc_c_view_only` exist in src/TestFixtures.js but have no automated test consumers, so AC2/AC4 behavior is not covered by a direct scenario. In addition, the production-facing Insert tracker path is only exercised indirectly via fixture routes; no test calls the user-facing insert action as its entry point. Add focused tests so regressions in tracker refresh and overwrite behavior are caught by the suite.
design:
Strategy agreed 2026-06-03:

1. RED-PHASE ATDD APPROACH — no implementation code until tests written.

2. SPINE: extend the existing journey/scenario model (test_journey.py Act 3 pattern or test_journey_acts_1_3.py). Do not write a new ad hoc Playwright flow from scratch.

3. ONE FOCUSED UI-ENTRY-POINT SCENARIO for missing coverage:
   - create/seed doc
   - scn.sync()
   - open sidebar via scn.ui
   - click Insert tracker (the real user-facing button — this is the uncovered entry point)
   - integrity/consistency checkpoint
   - mutate exactly one value (via edit_sheet/set_status/append_paragraph)
   - scn.sync()
   - integrity/consistency checkpoint
   - assert permuted value changed; assert all other tracker rows/fields unchanged

4. DECLARE EXPECTATIONS EXPLICITLY per §16.13 — each mutation step declares its intended delta; use step checkpoint for changed value, integrity checkpoint to prove no collateral drift.

5. UPGRADE verify_consistency: tracker rows must be first-class, not just counted. Required change:
   - parse tracker rows into same normalized ai shape as doc/sheet (id, globalId, assigneeEmail, assigneeName, action, status)
   - compare per-action by id/globalId, not total row count
   - verify unchanged rows are semantically equivalent across doc + sheet + tracker
   - report per-field delta differences, not just totals

6. SHARED TRACKER NORMALIZATION CONTRACT — use the same normalized tracker-row shape for two purposes:
   a. Test assertion: compare actual snapshot vs expected snapshot
   b. Future GAS idempotency: before rewriting tracker, compare current rendered rows vs desired rows; skip rewrite if equal
   This gives one semantic definition of "tracker changed" that both paths use.

7. VIEW-ONLY OVERWRITE AC: add a scenario step that directly edits a tracker cell via DocumentApp, then calls insert_tracker again and verifies the edit was discarded. This covers AC4.

8. RESPONSIBILITY SPLIT:
   - Scenario/harness: expectations, checkpoints, consistency, mutation declarations
   - Playwright: opening sidebar and clicking real user-facing button
   - GAS implementation later: no-op skip on idempotent refresh (separate follow-up, not blocking gxot)
acceptance_criteria: Done when automated tests directly cover: (1) insert/refresh tracker from the user-facing entry point, (2) refresh after an intervening close+add/update cycle with no stale rows, and (3) tracker-cell edits being overwritten on the next refresh.

title: [TST] Verify syncAll auto-archives Doc Not Found rows after second sweep
description:
Regression coverage for gts-eg8x. Tests the two-sweep grace period: first sweep marks 'Doc Not Found', second sweep archives the row.

## Pre-code contract
- Entry point: syncAll() — must be the call-site, not a mechanism it delegates to
- Log tag: sync.archive.doc_not_found
- Output schema: row absent from Actions sheet; present in Archive sheet

## AC
1. Seed ActionSheet with a row referencing an inaccessible docId
2. Run syncAll once — assert row status == 'Doc Not Found'; assert row NOT in Archive sheet
3. Run syncAll a second time — assert row absent from Actions sheet; assert row present in Archive sheet with correct fields
4. Assert rows for accessible docs are unaffected throughout

## Notes
- Must NOT read gts-eg8x implementation before writing assertions
- Extends test_sync_all.py (same file as r3d and grxl)
- Archive surface read via scn.session.archive_rows(doc_id) — see d33z for ArchiveSheetReader

Seed ONE mixed sheet (invalid-doc row, trashed-doc row, unmodified-valid row, modified-valid row), run syncAll ONCE, and drain r3d/grxl/5u2v as separate expectations on that single sweep. nv6g adds a SECOND sweep against the same seed for the two-sweep auto-archive. title: [IMP] syncAll: auto-archive rows confirmed Doc Not Found on second sweep
description:
Extend syncAll to archive rows that are already in 'Doc Not Found' status when encountered on a subsequent sweep. One accidental trash followed by two syncAll runs is a reasonable grace period before the row is permanently moved off the Actions sheet.

## Pre-code contract
- Entry point: syncAll() in SyncManager.js
- Log tag signalling completion: sync.archive.doc_not_found
- Behaviour: on each syncAll pass, after marking inaccessible docs 'Doc Not Found', check for rows already carrying that status from a prior sweep and pass them to ArchiveManager.archive()
- Output: rows absent from Actions sheet; present in Archive sheet with their last-known field values

## AC
1. Row marked 'Doc Not Found' on sweep N is moved to Archive sheet on sweep N+1 (or later — any subsequent sweep where the row is still Doc Not Found)
2. Rows marked Doc Not Found for the first time on the current sweep are NOT archived in the same pass (grace period)
3. Rows for accessible docs are unaffected
4. GAS log emits sync.archive.doc_not_found for each archived row

title: [TST] §16.10 canonical scenario journey — ATDD harness + end-to-end test
description:
Build the canonical scenario journey defined in `docs/proposed-atdd-lifecycle.md` **§16.10** — the end-to-end ATDD test harness (Python driver + expectation/checkpoint engine + surface readers + Playwright UI layer) and the GAS-side contract additions it exercises, culminating in the runnable `test_journey`.

**Canonical source:** §16 is the canonical scenario model; §16.10 is the journey to deliver. §16.11 records the resolved design decisions (empty-create, globalId write routes, onActionSheetEdit stamping on the API path, `sync()` queue-drain, per-surface partial drain). §15 is background; §16 supersedes its API naming.

## Model-assignment label legend
Each child carries exactly one `model:*` label, chosen by activity complexity:
- `model:opus` — design/architecture beads whose deliverable is a written spec that unblocks follow-on build beads.
- `model:sonnet` — well-specified build/implementation beads that consume a design spec or §16 directly.
- `model:haiku` — small mechanical beads with no design latitude.

## Coordination protocol (read this each session)
Every child assumes a **clean context** and is written to be self-sufficient. To keep independent tracks aligned without violating the ATDD no-shared-context rule (Part 1 §2 — [IMP] and [TST] share only the contract):
1. At start, the agent reads this epic's **Coordination Log** (in this epic's `notes`, via `bd show <epic>`).
2. Durable decisions/contracts go to the planning docs (`docs/proposed-atdd-lifecycle.md`, `docs/DESIGN.md`, `src/ContractSchema.js`) — NOT here.
3. Cross-cutting *discoveries* a sibling needs (a renamed field, a gotcha, a contract gap) go to the Coordination Log via `bd update <epic> --append-notes "..."`.
4. **Do not** put [IMP] internals or [TST] assertions in the log — only contract-level facts both sides may see.

## Reusable launch prompt (copy per child)
```
You are working bead <ID> in the GActionSheet repo (branch poc/editor-addon-action-chip). Assume a CLEAN context.

1. `bd show <ID>` — read description, acceptance, design notes, dependencies, and the model:* label (work at that altitude).
2. `bd show <EPIC>` — read the Coordination Log for cross-cutting facts from sibling tasks.
3. Read ONLY the sources the bead names (e.g. docs/proposed-atdd-lifecycle.md §16.x, src/ContractSchema.js, docs/DESIGN.md). Do NOT read the paired [IMP]/[TST] sibling's code — the contract is the only shared artifact.
4. State in one line each, before coding: (a) the interface/entry-point you produce, (b) the completion signal, (c) the output you will be verified against. If any is unclear it is a CONTRACT GAP — stop and append the question to the epic Coordination Log instead of guessing.
5. Run the implementation-gate skill, then do the work. Honor the §16 vocabulary and §16.11 decisions verbatim.
6. Quality gates (tests/lint/deploy as applicable). For GAS use the package.json npm scripts, never raw clasp.
7. If you discovered anything a sibling needs: durable -> update the planning doc/ContractSchema and say where; transient -> `bd update <EPIC> --append-notes "..."`.
8. Close per session protocol: update bead status, commit, push.
```

## Dependency shape
- `model:opus` design beads (D1 Python harness, D2 GAS contract) come first and gate the build beads.
- Build beads (B*) implement against the design specs and §16.
- Verify beads (V1/V2) are the twin-[TST] partners of the GAS [IMP] beads (B6/B7).
- J1 assembles §16.10 and depends on the full harness.

title: Defect: document name not refreshed in ActionSheet Document column on sync
description: WebApp.js _handleSyncActionRows updates Action (col 5) and Status (col 6) for doc-wins existing rows but never refreshes the Document column (col 7), which stores =HYPERLINK(docUrl, docName). The docName (from doc.getName()) is written only on new row insert via docTitle variable. If a document is renamed after its actions are first captured, every subsequent sync leaves the ActionSheet showing the old document name. title: Develop tests and test assets for UC-B update an action from either side and converge
description:
Design and implement the UC-B test suite using a canonical test document shared across all UCs.

## Test Architecture

All UC tests use a single canonical fixture document containing the full set of floating action format variants. Variants are cheap to add; execution runs are expensive — so we invest in variant coverage in the document, not in separate test runs.

### Canonical Floating Action Variants (standard fixture set)

| # | Format | Assignee | Status token | Tests |
|---|--------|----------|--------------|-------|
| 1 | Chip + action text + (Open) | testAssigneeEmail | default | baseline |
| 2 | Chip + action text + (In Review) | testAssigneeEmail | non-default | free-form status preserved verbatim |
| 3 | Chip + action text only | testAssigneeEmail | absent | defaults to Open |
| 4 | Email + action text + (Done) | jane.smith@example.com | non-default | email+status |
| 5 | Email + action text only | jane.smith@example.com | absent | email, no status |
| 6 | Underscore email + action text | bob_jones@example.com | absent | name derivation (punctuation→space, title-case) |
| 7 | Plain list item, no chip/email | — | — | negative: not detected |

Each GAS fixture function resets the doc to this canonical state (or a post-sync derivative of it) before triggering the operation under test.

## UC-B Specific Scenarios

### Scenario 1: uc_b_doc_wins
Fixture: post-UC-A state (all 6 detected variants have named ranges + sheet rows).
Edits applied before Sync: mutate variants 1–3 on the doc side (status token, action text, chip swap).
Assert: all mutations propagated to the ActionSheet; named-range anchors preserved; no duplicates.

### Scenario 2: uc_b_sheet_wins  
Fixture: post-UC-A state.
Edits applied before Sync: mutate variants 4–6 on the sheet side (Status col, Action col, Assignee col).
Assert: all mutations propagated to the floating action paragraphs; anchors preserved.

### Scenario 3: uc_b_conflict_resolution
Fixture: one action where sheet Last Modified is newer, one where doc Last Modified is newer.
Assert: each side wins its own action; no cross-contamination.

### Negative case
Variant 7 (plain list item) must remain absent from the ActionSheet after every sync — assert in scenarios 1 and 2.

## Batching principle
Pack all mutations of a given direction into one Sync invocation. Do not write one test per mutation type. Narrow isolation is for troubleshooting, not for the standard suite.

## Not in scope for UC-B test phase
- Parentheses-in-action-text parser ambiguity → gts-28q (hardening)
- Tracker table edit non-propagation → UC-C fixture

title: Sync produces incorrect output: missing emails, wrong ID prefix, malformed dates
description:
Four output-formatting defects observed in GAS sync execution log (bug01.txt, 2026-05-21):

1. Floating actions not updated with email from Tracked Actions table — AI-88 has assignee cknowlton@northlakeuu.org in the table but blank email in the floating action row.
2. Tracked Actions table ID column shows bare number (2, 4, 88, 89) instead of full AI-prefix format (AI-2, AI-4, AI-88, AI-89).
3. Floating action date fields missing time component — shows YYYY-MM-DD only (e.g. 2001-05-18) instead of YYYY-MM-DD h:m.
4. Tracked Actions table date-created and date-modified fields written in ISO 8601 format (e.g. 2026-05-21T04:24:42.873Z) instead of required YYYY-MM-DD h:m format.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: After sync, a floating action row whose ID exists in the Tracked Actions table must include the assignee email from that table. AC-2: The ID column in the Tracked Actions table must render AI-N (full prefix), not bare N. AC-3: Date fields in floating action rows must include time component in YYYY-MM-DD H:MM format. AC-4: Date-created and date-modified fields in the Tracked Actions table must render YYYY-MM-DD H:MM, not ISO 8601. AC-5: Blank placeholder row inserted by _createTable must not appear after sync — the empty data row must be removed before or during the first upsert pass. AC-6: Actions with no status (blank in both floating action and table) must be written as Open after normalization — apply winner.status = winner.status || 'Open' after _resolveConflict and before upsert/rewrite.
close_reason: AC-5: _createTable now calls table.removeRow(1) after appendTable to discard the blank placeholder row. AC-6: normalization upsert loop applies nr.status = nr.status || 'Open' before each _upsertTableRow call; applySheetWins does the same. New uc_blank_status fixture and test scenario added. expected_table_row_count assertion added to uc1_new_floating.

title: Impl: error handling — fail loudly on schema/data violations
description:
Implement explicit error paths per the new §Error Handling section in CONTEXT.md. Each must log a structured 'sync.error' event via GasLogger AND surface a clear message in the sheet UI (SpreadsheetApp.getUi().alert() when running interactively from the menu; otherwise just the log).

Cases:
1. Duplicate IDs in tracked-actions table within a single document: DocumentNormalizer.js detects two table rows with the same ID; abort the sync for that document, do not write any changes, log sync.error with tag detail {kind:'duplicate-table-id', docId, id}.
2. Invalid email token in a floating action: FloatingActionParser.js detects an AI- paragraph whose assignee token isn't a valid email (bare, display-name, or mention-chip form), abort that document's sync, log sync.error with {kind:'invalid-email-token', docId, paragraph}.
3. Missing required header on tracking sheet or tracked-actions table: SheetReconciler.js / DocumentNormalizer.js detect missing columns, abort the entire sync run for that scope (sheet missing header is fatal globally; table missing header is fatal per-doc), log sync.error with {kind:'missing-header', where, missing}.

Each error path must leave sheet and document untouched (no partial writes). Use WriteGuard.wrap to scope any opportunistic preflight writes if needed.

No new test scenarios in scope for this bead — error handling tests can be a follow-up. Focus on the implementation and logged error contract.
acceptance_criteria: All three error paths produce a sync.error log entry with the documented schema; manual test: hand-craft a doc with two rows ID=1 in its table, run Sync from menu, observe alert + sync.error log; verify no partial writes occurred.
close_reason: Closed

title: [TD] Reconcile test-organization guidance: journey-embedded steps vs dedicated per-entry-point files
description:
Trigger: during the GTaskSheet-d99c/gts-1pk (configFormat) test-design discussion on 2026-07-23, the project owner made two prioritization calls that depart from prior precedent without any written guideline backing them up:
1. Fault isolation deprioritized as a factor in choosing test placement (previously the main argument for GTaskSheet-rz4k.4's one-file-per-entry-point pattern in tests/test_menu_entry_points.py).
2. Entry-point identification/coverage bookkeeping to be handled via a grep/sed-parseable inline tagging convention in journey test scripts (the existing scn.expect_callable(..., entry_point=...) kwarg) rather than via file separation.

gts-1pk is the first ticket built on these calls — coverage lands as a step group inside the existing canonical journey rather than a new dedicated test file. There is currently no documented guideline reconciling this against the rz4k.4 precedent, so the next test-design discussion has nothing to default to and will re-litigate the same tradeoffs from scratch.

Scope of review:
1. Survey existing entry-point-coverage tests (tests/test_menu_entry_points.py and any other dedicated-file, single-entry-point tests) for consistency of entry_point= tagging today — is it applied uniformly, and is there any coverage that's implicit/undocumented and wouldn't survive a grep/sed extraction pass?
2. Formalize the grep/sed-parseable convention: required tag format, where it's allowed to live (assertion call kwarg vs inline comment for steps that don't route through scn.expect_callable), and a sample extraction command that proves it works.
3. Write down the decision factors for journey-embedded-step vs dedicated-file placement (candidate factors: shared setup/doc-creation cost, fault-isolation value, revert/cleanup risk in shared journeys, number and complexity of entry points in the affected subsystem) with a stated default.
4. Decide whether "fault isolation deprioritized" is now the project default or was a one-off judgment scoped to configFormat, and say so explicitly either way.
5. Check for related consistency gaps this same discussion surfaced (e.g., other exemption-documented entry points like menuBootstrap/menuInitializeTriggers — do they follow whatever convention gets written down here?).

Deliverable: a short written guideline future test-design discussions can cite by ID (matching how T1-T24 principles are cited elsewhere in this project), placed per doc-standard.md tier guidance — likely a new section in docs/atdd/project-testing-guide.md or docs/atdd/ID-map.md if tactical/revisable, or a new ADR if the reconciliation is meant to be a durable, binding methodology decision. Retrofit any existing tests/docs found inconsistent, or explicitly log them as accepted debt if retrofitting isn't worth it.
design: Not blocking on gts-1pk/d99c — this can proceed in parallel or after; gts-1pk is referenced as the concrete precedent to examine, not a dependency to wait on.
acceptance_criteria:
- Written guideline exists (project-testing-guide.md section, ID-map.md entry, or new ADR — reviewer's call per doc-standard.md tier guidance) reconciling journey-embedded-step vs dedicated-per-entry-point-file placement, with a stated default and override conditions.
- Guideline is linked from CLAUDE.md's Testing Strategy section so it's discoverable at session start.
- Existing entry_point= tagging surveyed across the test suite; inconsistencies fixed or explicitly listed as accepted debt with rationale.
- The fault-isolation-priority question is answered explicitly (project default vs one-off) rather than left implicit.
- gts-1pk is usable as the worked example cited in the guideline once it lands.

title: [TST] configFormat: verify sampled style applies across docs, reverts to default (twin to d99c)
description:
Twin-ticket [TST] for GTaskSheet-d99c ([IMP] configFormat). Pre-code contract (per no-shared-context rule, TST owner works from this contract only — do not read d99c's implementation or SyncManager.js beyond the signature below):

Entry points under test:
- New extracted core: _configFormatForDoc(docId) (SyncManager.js) — configFormat() is refactored to a thin UI-prompt shell (SpreadsheetApp.getUi().prompt -> parse docId -> delegate to _configFormatForDoc(docId) -> same ui.alert()s). No behavior change to the menu-triggered path.
- New run_fixture case in TestFixtures.js, e.g. 'config_format', accepting {docId} and calling _configFormatForDoc(docId) directly.
- The outer configFormat()/menuConfigFormat() prompt shell is a DOCUMENTED entry-point-coverage EXEMPTION (same class as menuBootstrap/menuInitializeTriggers, rz4k.4): SpreadsheetApp.getUi().prompt() cannot execute in the run_fixture/doPost headless context (Execution-API-style calls have no bound editor UI) — reason, not silence.

GAS log tag that signals completion: configFormat.complete { docId, N, aiToken, actionText } (already implemented, SyncManager.js:1801).

Output schema to assert:
- After _configFormatForDoc(refDocId) against a reference doc whose first AI-N: action has a distinctly styled token+text, the Config sheet has exactly one 'ai_token' row and one 'action_text' row matching the sampled font family/size/color/bold/italic/underline.
- A subsequent sync/chip write in a DIFFERENT document picks up that style on its AI-N: token and action-text ranges, verified via the Docs REST GET already used by other chip-verification tests (not visually).
- After clearing the Config rows and syncing again, the exact pre-existing hardcoded style (Comic Sans MS bold purple token, inherited-default action text) is restored — the fallback path.

Test placement (decision made 2026-07-23, see linked [TD] bead for the guideline this motivates): implement as a step group inside the existing canonical journey test, NOT a new dedicated test file. Fault isolation was explicitly deprioritized by the project owner for this feature, and entry-point identification is handled via the existing inline entry_point= tagging convention (scn.expect_callable(..., entry_point=...)), which stays grep/sed-parseable without requiring one file per entry point.

Journey step sequence:
1. Seed a reference doc (distinct from the journey's main doc) with a styled first AI-N: action.
2. _post_fixture("config_format", {"docId": ref_doc_id}).
3. Assert Config sheet rows (durable-state assertion, tag entry_point="configFormat").
4. Sync the journey's own (different) doc; assert new chip writes reflect the sampled style via Docs REST GET.
5. Clear the Config rows — comment this step explicitly as "clear config, not undo to a prior style" since _configFormatForDoc has no stack/undo semantics.
6. Sync again; assert the hardcoded default style is restored (fallback-path regression guard).
design: Open seam flagged for the linked [TD] bead: no written guidance yet exists for when coverage should live as a journey-embedded step with inline entry_point tags vs a dedicated per-entry-point file (rz4k.4 precedent). This ticket is the first deliberate deviation from rz4k.4 and should be read as the worked example once implemented.
acceptance_criteria:
- _configFormatForDoc(docId) extracted from configFormat() in SyncManager.js; configFormat() delegates to it with zero behavior change to the interactive prompt path.
- New TestFixtures.js run_fixture case wired and documented as an entry-point-coverage exemption for the prompt shell, with the same rationale format used for menuBootstrap/menuInitializeTriggers.
- Journey step group added (not a new dedicated file) asserting: (a) Config sheet gets exactly one ai_token + one action_text row matching the sampled style, (b) a different document's subsequent chip write reflects that style via Docs REST GET, (c) clearing Config rows and re-syncing restores the exact prior hardcoded default via Docs REST GET.
- Each assertion tagged entry_point="configFormat" (or the applicable delegate) per the existing scn.expect_callable convention.
- pytest -x (full suite) green.
- gts-d99c closed only once this issue is green (twin-ticket rule).

title: [INF] /technical-debt v1.1 refinements (LL 2026-06-12 residuals)
description: Residuals from LL 2026-06-12 (molecule-placeholder issues stayed open). The immediate mol-66r/mol-dhd child closures were done 2026-06-12; these are the carried-forward tool refinements. Branch A: /technical-debt implicit-resolve check should also match recently-closed bead titles/close-reasons against the TITLES of open molecule-formula step children sharing a parent epic (empty descriptions defeat the current commit-vs-description match). Branch B: tune 'bd stale' threshold against this project's epic/molecule cadence (21-day-dormant placeholder children were not flagged). Branch D: add a '100%-children-closed but parent still open' check (bd's own 'eligible for close' signal has no aggregate surface).
design:
Where each refinement lands: Branch A/D -> /technical-debt SKILL.md checks; Branch B -> session-start-check SKILL.md step. Open question: is title-matching precise enough to avoid false 'superseded' calls, or does it need human confirm (as the existing implicit-resolve check already requires)? Resolved: yes, human confirm still required -- title-matching only extends candidate DISCOVERY, the existing "confirm or defer" human gate is unchanged.

RESOLUTION (2026-07-01) -- all three branches IMPLEMENTED in the named artifacts (canonical source: /mnt/c/dev/DevStandard/dot-claude/skills/{technical-debt,session-start-check}/SKILL.md, mirrored at ~/.claude/skills/; both are the same file on this host, edited in place, left uncommitted for human review per session instructions):

Branch A (implemented) -- technical-debt SKILL.md v1.1, Step 1 Aggregate: added a second implicit-resolve sub-check. Queries `bd list --empty-description --type=molecule` for placeholder step children, resolves each child's PARENT EPIC title (which encodes the feature/use-case name even when the step child's own title is generic, e.g. "Implement {{feature}}"), and matches recently-closed sibling bead titles/close-reasons against that parent-epic title instead of the step child's empty description. Flagged candidates still require human confirm/defer (unchanged gate) -- this only fixes discovery, not disposition.

Branch B (implemented) -- session-start-check SKILL.md v1.4, Step 1b: `bd stale` default (30 days) missed the 21-day-dormant mol-dhd/mol-66r step children. Tuned the session-start debt check to run `bd stale --days 14` instead of the bare default, with rationale documented inline (surfaces genuinely dormant items within this project's epic/molecule cadence without over-flagging normal multi-week epics still mid-flight). Not implemented as a persistent `bd config`/dolt-stored threshold -- bd does not expose a stale-window config key (checked `bd config list`, `bd stale --help`); the CLI `--days` flag is the only lever, so the fix lives in the session-start-check procedure that invokes it.

Branch D (implemented) -- technical-debt SKILL.md v1.1, Step 1 Aggregate: new "Eligible-for-close epics" check -- `bd list --type=epic --status=open --no-parent -n 0`, then `bd show <id>` per epic checking for bd's own "eligible for close" line. No text search needed (lower-cost than A, as the LL noted). Added a matching "Eligible-for-close epics" section to the Step 3 Present template and two new Success Criteria bullets.

No application code changed (skill/prompt docs only); pytest -x run as a courtesy check per issue instructions, no regressions expected or found.
acceptance_criteria: Each of Branch A, B, D is either implemented in the named artifact or explicitly deferred with rationale recorded on this issue.
close_reason: Confirmed: all three branches (A/B/D) implemented in DevStandard dot-claude/skills/{technical-debt,session-start-check}/SKILL.md as recorded in the RESOLUTION note. after a token — so there is no equivalent "rest after token extraction" code path today. The
closest text-pattern code is EditorAddonCard.js:92 `nameEmailMatch` for "Name <email>" form
fields, which is a different pattern/bug class than BARE_EMAIL_RE's `\s*`-eats-separator issue.

This ticket (created 2026-07-01) targets code that was already gone over a month before it was
filed — the LL-resolution note pointing Branch B here didn't check current source. No test was
added since there's nothing live to test against.

Leaving this issue OPEN (not closing) for a human decision: options are (1) close as obsolete —
the bug class can no longer occur because assignee parsing is structural (person-chip) not
regex-based, or (2) if the new checkbox+person-chip scanner (_parseParagraphAsFloatingAction /
_collectTokenParagraphs in EditorAddonCard.js) has an analogous "text remainder after chip
extraction" seam, retarget this ticket to that seam and re-scope the AC accordingly.

title: [IMP] configFormat: sample action-item style from a reference doc, apply to all future chip writes
description:
Pre-code contract:
- Entry point: new configFormat() (SyncManager.js), wired to a new Setup-submenu
  item 'Configure Action Format' -> menuConfigFormat() (MenuHandler.js). Prompts
  (SpreadsheetApp.getUi().prompt) for a Doc ID or URL, opens it, finds the first
  AI-N: floating action in document order (_scanFloatingActions(doc)[0]), samples
  font family/size/color/bold/italic/underline separately for the 'AI-N:' token
  text and the action-text content (via DocumentApp Text element per-offset style
  getters: getFontFamily/getFontSize/getForegroundColor/isBold/isItalic/isUnderline),
  and upserts two rows ('ai_token', 'action_text') into a new Config sheet
  (CONTRACT_SCHEMA.sheetConfig, ContractSchema.js).
- Application: _getActionFormatConfig() (SyncManager.js, execution-scoped cache)
  reads Config once per GAS execution. _chipBadgeStyleRequest (existing, shared by
  the doc-sync flush, Import/create-chip path, and Tracker Table ID links) reads
  its style from the 'ai_token' row instead of the current hardcoded Comic Sans MS
  bold purple -- falls back to that exact hardcoded style when Config has no
  'ai_token' row, so behavior is unchanged until configFormat is run (forward-only,
  no retroactive reformat per session decision). New _actionTextStyleRequest
  applies the 'action_text' row to the trailing action-text+status range in both
  _buildFlushRequests (SyncManager.js) and _applyActionFragment (EditorAddonCard.js)
  -- returns null (no style request, today's inherited-default behavior) when
  Config has no 'action_text' row yet.
- Completion log tag: configFormat.complete { docId, N, aiToken, actionText }.
- Output schema test will assert against: after configFormat() against a
  reference doc with a styled first action item, the Config sheet has exactly
  one 'ai_token' row and one 'action_text' row with the sampled font/size/color/
  bold/italic/underline; a subsequent sync/status-change/import chip write in a
  DIFFERENT document picks up that style on its AI-N: token and action text
  ranges (verified via the Docs REST GET used by flush, not just visually).

title: [IMP] DocData sheet's Doc Name column is a HYPERLINK to the document
description:
Pre-code contract:
- Entry point: _getOrUpsertDocDataRow (SyncManager.js:1408), the single write
  chokepoint for the DocData sheet's Doc Name column (col 2, sheetDocData.doc_name)
  -- every caller (sync_action_rows DocData refresh, mark_doc_not_found mirror,
  syncAll integrity pass, _syncTeamScope first-pass write, test fixtures) already
  funnels through it. Build the cell value as
  '=HYPERLINK("https://docs.google.com/document/d/' + fileId + '/edit","' +
  _escapeQuotes(docName) + '")' instead of the bare docName string -- fileId is
  already a required param, so no signature change or extra docUrl plumbing is
  needed. Reuses _escapeQuotes (WebApp.js, same GAS global scope) -- the exact
  pattern already used for the Actions sheet's document_formula column
  (WebApp.js:595/771/801), no new escaping logic.
- Read side unaffected: _readDocDataRow/_readDocDataRows already read doc_name
  via getValues() (computed display value), which for a HYPERLINK formula is the
  title text -- identical to today's plain-string read. No changes needed there.
- Completion signal: no new log tag -- this is a cell-formatting change, not a
  new code path.
- Output schema test will assert against: after a sync, the DocData sheet's Doc
  Name cell for a tracked doc is a HYPERLINK formula targeting that doc's
  edit URL, whose displayed title matches the document's actual name; reading
  the row back via _readDocDataRow / find_sheet_actions-style verification still
  returns the plain title text (not formula syntax) in docName, so no downstream
  consumer (integrity-pass title comparison, Import join) breaks.

title: [IMP] Sidebar action list ordered by AI-N instead of document order
description:
Pre-code contract:
- Entry point: _buildActionListSection (WorkspaceAddonCard.js) renders
  homepageState.floatingActions (sourced from _collectFloatingActionState ->
  _scanFloatingActions, which returns actions in document body order) as the
  sidebar's "Actions for this document" list. Change to a render-time sort by
  AI-N ascending (parseGlobalId(action.globalId).N), mirroring the existing
  Import-tab sort (_buildImportTabSection, same file, ~line 265-267). Actions
  without a globalId yet (newly-typed, not yet anchored/synced -- "Needs sync")
  have no N to sort by; keep them after all numbered actions, in their existing
  relative (doc) order among themselves.
- Sort only at the render layer (a local copy in _buildActionListSection), not
  in _collectFloatingActionState/_buildHomepageState -- other consumers of
  floatingActions (missing-anchor count, status summary, TrackerTable) are
  order-independent and must stay in doc-scan order for their own correctness.
- Completion signal: no new log tag -- this is a pure rendering-order change,
  verified by the displayed list's content order, not by GAS logs.
- Output schema test will assert against: a doc with action items inserted/
  anchored out of numeric order (e.g. AI-3 appears before AI-1 in the doc body)
  must render in the sidebar list as AI-1, AI-2, AI-3 (ascending), with any
  not-yet-anchored action(s) appearing after all numbered ones.

title: [TST] test_sidebar_shell_controls: Import-button locator race under GAS cold-start load
description:
Observed during gts-ishz.2 validation (2026-06-22): test_sidebar.py::test_sidebar_shell_controls
failed twice in a row (full-suite run, then isolated retry) with the same symptom:

  card.frame.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile(r"^import$", re.I)).wait_for(state="visible", timeout=30000)
  -> playwright TimeoutError

The capture_failure diagnostics dump (gts-3tkf) shows the Import button WAS present in
the frame's visible-buttons list at failure time ('Sync', 'Import', 'Notify', 'Insert Tracker', ...),
so this is not a missing/broken control -- it's a locator/render race, most likely GAS cold-start
variability under sustained load (this session ran the full suite against the live TEST WebApp
4 times in ~3 hours). The other 5 tests that failed alongside it in the same full-suite run all
passed cleanly on isolated retry; only this one reproduced twice.

Not connected to any code change in this session (EditorAddonCard.js's diff was an unrelated
GasLogger.flush() call; webSurveyPage.html is a different page entirely).

Suggested fix direction: tighten the open_sidebar -> button-visible handshake (e.g. wait on a
broader card-ready signal before racing individual button locators), or accept higher timeout/
retry budget specifically for this assertion. Needs reproduction outside of heavy-load conditions
to confirm before deciding root cause vs. just flaky infra.

title: [FIX] test_sidebar_shell_controls: intermittent 30s timeout waiting for Import button
description: Discovered during gts-ht19/rvwu full-suite verification (2026-06-20). tests/test_sidebar.py::test_sidebar_shell_controls timed out (30s) waiting for get_by_role('button', name=~import) to be visible, but the failure diagnostic's post-timeout 'Visible buttons' capture shows Import WAS present in the addon frame at that point -- suggests a render-timing race (button appears just after the assert's window) rather than a missing/broken button. Passed in all other observed runs this session (test_sidebar_header_branding, added in the same file in this session, passed both standalone and as part of the same file run where this one failed). Not confirmed as a regression -- needs 1-2 isolated reruns to establish flake rate before deciding whether to extend the timeout or investigate render latency.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Rerun in isolation 2-3x; if it reproduces, find root cause (render latency vs. selector issue) and fix; if not, conclude flaky and just extend the wait_for timeout slightly with a comment noting why.

title: [FIX] test_journey flakes on actionTrigger.done log wait (60s timeout)
description:
Full-suite pytest -x run (2026-06-20, during gts-j8cn/4tnr verification) failed at tests/test_journey.py:256 -- assert_log waiting on tag=='actionTrigger.done' (Create Action card trigger completion) timed out after 60s against the live Drive-mounted GAS log dir, then teardown raised scn.engine.DrainInvariantError on top (6 undrained [journey sync-create] expectations -- fallout from the primary failure, not a separate bug).

This is the THIRD distinct test_journey failure mode seen this session, each unrelated to the other two and to gts-j8cn/4tnr (which were independently verified green via targeted test runs):
  1. Chip-integrity 'unknown'/'other' label mismatch (fixed this session, commit 7044ee5)
  2. status-other.png 404 on GitHub Pages before the asset push propagated (resolved by waiting for Pages to publish)
  3. This one: actionTrigger.done log-wait timeout

Re-investigate fresh -- don't assume the same root cause as the prior two. Candidates to check: GAS log flush timing/Drive-mount propagation delay for this specific tag, whether the Create Action card trigger actually fired (UI timing/selector drift), or a genuine regression. Re-run in isolation first to check for flakiness vs. deterministic failure.
notes: Re-tested in isolation 2026-06-20 (during gts-ht19/rvwu verification, on the same deployed TEST build, unrelated to those issues): tests/test_journey.py::test_journey failed IDENTICALLY a second consecutive time on the same assertion (actionTrigger.done log wait, 60s timeout at Act 4 / @-menu create_action). This contradicts the original 'investigate fresh, don't assume same root cause as flaky theory' framing -- two consecutive identical failures on the same TEST deployment suggests a deterministic regression in the @-menu create-action flow (EditorAddonCard.js createActionTrigger / _submitCreateAction), not transient flakiness. Failure screenshot shows the Create-action card still open with the action text filled in -- unclear from screenshot alone whether the Create button click registered. Needs investigation into whether this is a UI-selector drift, a GAS-side regression, or a Drive-mount log-flush delay specific to this tag. Not chased further this session per backstop rule (present debt, don't work around).

title: [INF] Document/bridge the GAS-side vs Python-side log-event naming mismatch (domain.event taxonomy vs raw action/fixture names)
description:
Surfaced from the same live Axiom query (most recent 200 events, 2026-06-19/20) used to validate gts-x94a's GAS-side tag rename.

All 182 side:'gas' events in the sample use (or, pending x94a/9dss, will use) the domain.event taxonomy. All 18 side:'python' events use entirely different naming: raw snake_case action/fixture names straight off the wire (sync_all, get_docdata_row, set_docdata_row, begin_journey_session, end_journey_session, append_paragraph, sync_document) -- this is scn/reporter.py + scn/session.py's ScenarioSession._post(), per docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md SS4.1's deliberate 'name every event by what it actually did' precedence (payload.get('fixture') or payload.get('action')). Not a bug -- it's documented, intentional design for the Python side considered alone.

The gap: nobody building a single Axiom view spanning one request end-to-end (e.g. a sync_all Python call and the sync.all.start/sync.all.complete GAS sub-events it triggers) can facet across both without already knowing the two vocabularies map to the same operation. journey-logging-design.md SS4.3 ('a standalone logging service... have everything write through one sink') gestures at fixing this architecturally but is explicitly marked as open/undecided design, not committed work.

This is a documentation/decision gap, not a code defect: either (a) document the mapping (which Python action/fixture name corresponds to which GAS domain.event family) so a human or dashboard query can bridge it manually, or (b) decide SS4.3 is worth doing now and scope it as real work. Re-derive independently -- don't assume SS4.3's framing is still the right shape; check whether real dashboard usage has actually hit this gap yet.
acceptance_criteria:
Re-pull a live Axiom sample and confirm the side:'gas' vs side:'python' naming split described above still holds (data may have shifted).
Either: (a) produce a short mapping table (Python action/fixture name -> corresponding GAS domain.event family) added to docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md, with no code change required, or (b) make an explicit go/no-go call on SS4.3's unified-sink design and, if go, split it into its own scoped issue rather than doing it inside this one.
Do not implement SS4.3 as a side effect of this issue without a separate explicit decision -- it's flagged as 'open decision, needs a human call' in the design doc itself.
close_reason: Re-pulled live Axiom sample (200 events/24h, 2026-06-19): 182/18 gas/python split confirmed unchanged. Added §8 mapping table to docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md documenting which GAS domain.event family each Python action/fixture name triggers (sync_all -> full sync.*/archive.*/tracker.* cascade, sync_document -> per-doc subset, get_docdata_row/set_docdata_row -> no domain tag, generic fixture.setup as the anchor for run_fixture calls with no case-specific tag, begin/end_journey_session -> journey.begin/end, append_doc_paragraph -> test.append_doc_paragraph). Documentation only, per AC option (a) -- did not implement §4.3's unified-sink design.

title: [INF] Document GasLogger op-id correlation mechanism (gts-65g1)
description:
gts-65g1 added GasLogger.startOp()/endOp() (module-level current-op id, stamped onto every log() entry as 'op' until cleared) and wired it into syncAll(). This is undocumented outside the bead itself and the inline GasLogger.js docblock comment.

Needs a home in the docs structure (per CLAUDE.md placement rules — likely docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md, which already covers the GasLogger/Axiom design, or a new ADR if this is judged a durable architectural decision):
- The correlation mechanism itself: why module-level state is safe in GAS (each execution has its own isolated global scope, no shared memory across concurrent invocations) — this is the load-bearing assumption that makes the simple design correct.
- Current scope: only syncAll() is wired. Other multi-step entry points (journey session, import flows) were evaluated and found NOT to need it yet, because each of their handler calls only emits a single log() call (no sub-events to correlate within one invocation) — docId already serves as the de facto correlation key across the begin/end pair. Document this finding so a future contributor doesn't re-propose wiring journey-session begin/end without re-checking whether that's still true.
- Forward pointer to gts-j8cn (cross-invocation parentOp propagation, addon->WebApp) and gts-x94a (tag taxonomy cleanup) as the next steps in this area — this bead is documentation only, not a redesign.
acceptance_criteria: docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md (or an ADR, if judged durable-architecture-worthy) describes: the op/startOp/endOp mechanism, the GAS per-execution-isolated-global-scope safety argument, current scope (syncAll only) and why journey-session begin/end were excluded, and links to gts-j8cn + gts-x94a as related follow-ups.
close_reason: Documented op/parentOp correlation mechanism, GAS per-execution-isolated-global-scope safety argument, current scope (syncAll only) + journey-session exclusion finding, and links to GTaskSheet-j8cn/x94a in docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md §9.

title: [TST] Implement journey-logging-design.md: per-step timing visibility for scenario tests
description:
docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md (drafted 2026-06-19, Status: Draft) proposes
closing the gap between "a scenario test is slow/flaky" and "here is a report showing
exactly what happened and how long each step took" -- motivated by
gts-y8a0's investigation requiring ~40 minutes of manual reconstruction
(cross-referencing separate trace files, reading test source to label generic
"run_fixture" events, inferring an unlogged step's duration from gaps between files).

Key proposed pieces (see doc for full detail and tradeoffs):
1. Name HTTP trace events by actual fixture name, not the generic "run_fixture" envelope.
2. Log scn.session.ScenarioSession.new_doc()'s begin_journey_session call (currently
   invisible -- happens before the Reporter exists).
3. A standalone, independently-deployed Apps Script webapp + log sheet that both the
   Python test harness and the main GTaskSheet webapp write timestamped events to --
   decoupled from the main app's GAS execution quota (so the logger doesn't inherit
   the same slow/exhausted-quota failure mode it exists to diagnose), using a
   fast-path-write + durable-queue-and-trigger-compaction design.
4. A merge/report script reading that one shared log into one chronological,
   human-readable table per test run.
5. Baseline/variance tracking (deferred follow-up) once enough run history accumulates.

This bd issue exists so the design doesn't get lost after context clears. The doc has
several open decisions (§6) that need a human call before implementation -- this is
NOT yet approved for implementation, just tracked so it's discoverable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Human reviews docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md's §6 open decisions and either
  approves a slice for implementation (specifying which: §4.1 naming fix alone is a
  cheap first step; the standalone webapp is the larger piece) or explicitly defers
  the whole design.
- If approved: implementation follows the doc's §7 acceptance criteria for whichever
  slice was chosen.

comments.author: Stuart Donaldson
comments.text: POC confirmed (2026-06-19): Axiom ingestion+query round-trip works end-to-end against dataset 'nuuts' using axiomToken (ingest) + axiomQueryToken (query), both in local.settings.json. curl POST to https://api.axiom.co/v1/datasets/nuuts/ingest succeeded (ingested:1); APL query via https://api.axiom.co/v1/datasets/_apl found the event queryable within seconds of ingest -- no Drive-mount-style propagation delay. Decision: replace design doc's §4.3 standalone-Apps-Script-webapp+Sheet-sink with Axiom as the shared sink. Next: wire GasLogger.js (UrlFetchApp POST) and scn/reporter.py (requests POST) to this same dataset, per the latency discussion -- this should let us drop/shrink the 10s clock-skew fence and 60s poll timeout in tests/helpers/gas_log.py.

title: [FIX] test_import_access_filter intermittently times out on first show_tab("Import") under backend load
description:
Distinct from gts-y8a0 (closed -- that was a real test-script bug: missing
show_tab("Back") before a second show_tab("Import"), now fixed). This is a separate,
still-open failure mode discovered while verifying y8a0's fix: in two consecutive runs
on 2026-06-19, the FIRST show_tab("Import") call (which has been reliable in every
prior run) timed out too -- even after raising scn/ui.py's show_tab default timeout
from 15s to 30s, with zero improvement (same failure, same symptom).

Symptom: the main document editor pane shows Google Drive's "File is in trash"
interstitial ('Go to Docs home screen' / 'Take out of trash' buttons) instead of doc
content, while the sidebar/add-on iframe itself is fine (confirmed via the new
scn.ui.describe_visible_buttons() diagnostic -- 'Import' is present and visible in the
addon frame's button list every time).

A merged, manually-reconstructed timing trace (saved at
test-results/TIMING-test_import_access_filter-20260619.log; raw per-session trace
files at test-results/runs/test_import_access_filter_20260619T1817*.trace.jsonl) shows
every backend HTTP round-trip (run_fixture/sync/etc.) running 4-19s -- normal is ~1-2s
-- across roughly a dozen calls in the test's setup phase alone. Leading hypothesis:
accumulated GAS/Drive quota or rate-limit pressure from this session's unusually high
volume of repeated full-suite + isolated test reruns over several hours, not a code
regression in any of the same session's changes (gts-4tnr, the tooltip on the
Import button, or the doc_modified->last_sync_time rename) -- 25+ other tests passed
in the same runs.

Not yet confirmed: clasp logs only tails recent activity (no historical range query),
so GAS-side execution-time corroboration wasn't available retroactively for this
specific failure window. docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md (drafted same session)
proposes infrastructure to make this kind of correlation routine instead of requiring
manual reconstruction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Re-run test_import_access_filter (and ideally the full suite) once the test Drive
  account/script project has had a cooldown period since today's heavy usage, to
  confirm whether the failure is purely load-correlated (passes cleanly once load
  drops) or recurs independently of load.
- If it recurs independently of load: escalate -- this would mean the tooltip change,
  gts-4tnr, or the rename actually introduced a regression and the "load"
  theory was wrong; needs fresh root-causing.
- If purely load-correlated: no code fix needed here, but consider whether
  show_tab's timeout (now 30s, was 15s) should go higher still, and whether
  journey-logging-design.md's variance-tracking goal (§4.4) would have caught this
  pattern earlier from historical data.

title: [TST] Validate visible-button failure diagnostics, then promote to UI-testing best practice
description:
While debugging tests/test_import.py::test_import_access_filter's repeated
Locator.wait_for timeout, the only failure diagnostics available were a
screenshot and a list of frame URLs (tests/conftest.py's
pytest_runtest_makereport hook, gts-3tkf). Reconstructing the actual
cause (the test calls show_tab("Import") twice with no "Back" in between, so
the second call's button-lookup runs against the Import card's own button
set -- "Back"/"Select all"/"Import selected" -- which has no button literally
named "Import") took several screenshot reads, a headed re-run, and multiple
exploratory agent investigations to confirm by inference.

The fix just landed (this session, uncommitted alongside gts-4tnr):
added scn.ui.describe_visible_buttons(frames), a shared helper that reads
each frame's visible button accessible names via get_by_role("button") --
the same ARIA-role signature bounded waits already query, so it's free of
OCR's lossiness/cost and exactly answers "what was actually clickable when
this failed." Wired into both UiDriver.capture_failure() (bounded-wait
failures) and tests/conftest.py's pytest_runtest_makereport hook (raw
assertion/timeout failures) -- so EVERY UI test failure's report now
includes a per-frame button list alongside the screenshot.

This issue exists to close the loop the user asked for: confirm the addition
actually earns its keep on a handful of real failures (does the button list
shorten root-cause time the way it should have for the access_filter bug?),
then promote the pattern into the project's UI-testing best practices
(README.md / docs/OPERATIONS.md test-failure-diagnostics section, or
wherever gts-3tkf's screenshot convention is documented) so future
custom UI-failure capture points (if any get added) follow the same
DOM-text-over-OCR convention by default instead of reinventing it.
acceptance_criteria:
- After 1-2 real UI test failures post-merge, confirm the "Visible buttons"
  section in the failure report measurably sped up or simplified root-cause
  (a one-line note on the issue is enough evidence, not a formal study).
- If confirmed useful: add a short note to wherever gts-3tkf's
  screenshot-on-failure convention is documented (README.md test section or
  docs/OPERATIONS.md), stating that UI-failure diagnostics should capture
  DOM-derived state (visible interactive element names/roles) over OCR,
  with describe_visible_buttons() as the reference implementation.
- If NOT useful (e.g. too noisy, frames too numerous to scan): note why and
  close without promoting -- this is a validate-then-promote issue, not an
  unconditional rollout.

title: [INF] Add test.u1 (non-deployer Primary) browser auth + Drive-sharing fixture for add-on entry-point tests
description:
