title: [EPIC] Authorized web app AI editing
description:
Umbrella for verified-identity access to chip-linked board actions, covering two related
surfaces (plan: docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md):

(A) Milestone 1 — verified board-listing + sync (read-only). A recipient who clicks an
AI-N: chip lands on a page proving their Google identity (incl. external/personal @gmail,
via a static GitHub Pages + GIS front end), then sees all action items for that board
group's Drive folder, filtered, gated on folder-level access (direct or via a
domain-managed Google Group) — and can trigger a sync if they hold write access. Both
gating spikes (S1 identity, S2 folder-ACL incl. group-conferred access) PASSED
2026-07-22/23.

(B) Phase 2 (deferred) — verified-identity in-place EDIT of a single chip-linked action,
per ADR-0017.

Cross-repo split confirmed by the spikes (NUUC-Dispatch ADR-0002): NUUC-Dispatch
(sibling repo) verifies+signs identity only (external-facing, minimal scope, published
GCP project). GActionSheet (this repo) owns the folder-ACL authorization check and the
board-listing/sync surface (needs expanded Drive/Admin-SDK scopes, stays Internal-only).
Supersedes the earlier auth-code-redirect-on-/exec framing this description previously
carried.

Done when both (A) and (B) close; (A) is the active near-term target, (B) remains
deferred.

title: [IMP] Authorize chip-link identity against referenced doc's Drive ACL (Phase 2)
description: SECURITY (authorization, not just authentication). A verified identity from the Phase 2 OAuth flow (gts-6dlp) could be ANY Google account. Before exposing confidential action content or allowing an edit, the webapp MUST confirm that the verified identity has access to the referenced document (docId). Otherwise any Google-account holder who knows or guesses the chip globalId could read confidential information. This is an authorization gate layered on top of authentication, required for ADR-0017 Phase 2 to be secure.
design: Candidate mechanisms + tradeoffs: (A) Deployer-side check — Drive permissions.list(fileId) (or Drive.Files.get with fields=capabilities) and match the verified email against a direct user permission / matching-domain grant / anyone-with-link. No extra user scopes. OPEN QUESTION: requires the DEPLOYER to have rights to read that file's permissions — the deployer may not have access to arbitrary end-user docs, so this can fail for docs it can't see. (B) Request a Drive read scope from the user in the OAuth flow (e.g. drive.metadata.readonly) and probe access AS the user — works for any doc but is a SENSITIVE scope (adds a consent screen + triggers Google verification). Safe default: DENY (fall back to the Phase 1 notice / an access-denied page) whenever access cannot be positively confirmed. Open question: which mechanism, and handling of docs the deployer cannot see.
acceptance_criteria: A verified identity WITHOUT access to docId is denied confidential content + edit (notice/access-denied page); a verified identity WITH access proceeds. Negative test: a random Google account with no file access cannot read the action text even with a valid globalId.

title: [TST] R6-impl: Allure step tags + UI-failure screenshots (engine.drain hooks)
description: Implement R6 (gts-80mo.12): unify Allure report content across the Python scn/ stack and the JS Playwright smoke layer. Adds optional allure.step()/attach() hooks to engine.drain()+Reporter so every drained expectation surface shows as an Allure step named [<scenario> <ac-label>] <SURFACE>, and Surface.UI FAIL-severity check failures attach a page screenshot.
design:
ACTIVATION DESIGN (80mo.12 / R6) — populated 2026-06-11.

Goal: report.* tags carry [<scenario> <ac-label>] into Allure step names; UI-surface
FAIL-severity check failures attach a screenshot; JS smoke retains traces (already true).

1. scn/reporter.py (Reporter):
   - import allure (allure-pytest>=2.13 already a hard dep; allure.step()/attach() are
     no-ops outside an active allure-pytest run, safe for unit tests).
   - Enhance step() context manager: in addition to existing trace timing, wrap the
     yielded block in `allure.step(f"{phase} {name}" + (f" {detail}" if detail else ""))`.
     Single mechanism -> every ACT/QUERY/UIACT/CHECK already routed through step()
     gets an Allure step "for free" (uniform report, no per-call-site changes).
   - New method allure_step(self, name: str) -> contextmanager: returns allure.step(name).
     Used by engine.drain() (below) for the per-surface CHECK granularity that lives
     INSIDE the drain loop, below the existing step() call in session.checkpoint().
   - New method attach_screenshot(self, page, name: str) -> None: if page is not None,
     `allure.attach(page.screenshot(), name=name, attachment_type=allure.attachment_type.PNG)`,
     wrapped in try/except Exception (swallow) so a screenshot failure never masks the
     original AssertionError.

2. scn/engine.py (CheckpointEngine.drain):
   - Add two optional params, both default None (fully backward compatible — existing
     tests/test_scn_engine.py calls unaffected; engine.py stays allure-import-free):
       step_cm: Callable[[str], ContextManager] | None = None
       on_ui_fail: Callable[[Surface, str, str], None] | None = None
   - Wrap each per-surface check (the check_fn(...) call AND the CALLABLE branch,
     drain() lines ~213-225) in:
       cm = step_cm(f"{e.tag} {surface.value}") if step_cm else contextlib.nullcontext()
       with cm:
           <existing check logic>
   - Immediately before `raise AssertionError(error)` (FAIL severity, line ~236): if
     surface == Surface.UI and on_ui_fail is not None, call on_ui_fail(surface, e.tag, error)
     THEN raise. (WARN path unchanged — no screenshot, screenshots are for hard failures.)

3. scn/session.py (ScenarioSession.checkpoint):
   - Pass step_cm=self._reporter.allure_step to engine.drain().
   - Pass on_ui_fail=self._attach_ui_failure_screenshot (new private method):
       def _attach_ui_failure_screenshot(self, surface, tag, error):
           if self.ui is not None:
               self._reporter.attach_screenshot(
                   self.ui._page, name=f"{tag} {surface.value} FAIL"
               )

4. JS side (tests/playwright/playwright.config.js): NO CHANGE NEEDED. Already configured
   with allure-playwright reporter -> test-results/allure-results, screenshot:
   'only-on-failure', video: 'retain-on-failure'. Docs bead should document/confirm this
   as the JS-side half of "report reads uniformly", not re-implement it.

5. Backward compatibility / unit-test impact: tests/test_scn_engine.py, test_scn_session.py,
   test_scn_reporter.py call drain()/step()/Reporter() without the new params/methods —
   all new behavior is additive and no-op when allure-pytest isn't actively collecting
   (allure.step/attach are documented as safe outside a run). No existing assertions
   should change.

ACCEPTANCE (impl bead):
- A deliberately-failing Surface.UI PRESENT_CONSISTENT expectation (new unit test in
  tests/test_scn_engine.py or test_scn_session.py, using a fake page with .screenshot()
  returning bytes) results in attach_screenshot being called with that page and a name
  containing the tag + "UI" + "FAIL".
- engine.drain() unit tests confirm step_cm is invoked once per (expectation, surface)
  with name f"{tag} {surface.value}" when provided, and drain() behaves identically
  (same return value, same exceptions) when step_cm/on_ui_fail are omitted.
- Existing test suite (tests/test_scn_engine.py, test_scn_session.py, test_scn_reporter.py,
  test_scn_ui.py) passes unchanged.
- A live test_journey run (or test_ui_smoke) followed by `npx allure generate
  test-results/allure-results -o <out> --clean` produces a report whose steps for
  drained expectations are named "[<scenario> <ac-label>] <SURFACE>".

DOCS (docs bead, after impl):
- Document the unified Allure step naming convention + UI-failure screenshot attachment
  in docs/OPERATIONS.md (§Test observability) and/or docs/atdd/harness-design.md (once
  gts-ruoa creates it — otherwise note in OPERATIONS.md and cross-reference later).
- Confirm/document JS smoke (tests/playwright/*.test.js) already retains
  allure-playwright traces+screenshots via playwright.config.js — no code change, just
  record the "uniform across both stacks" closure of F6.
acceptance_criteria: See --design for full acceptance detail. Summary: drain() gains optional step_cm/on_ui_fail params (backward compatible, no-op when omitted); Reporter gains allure_step()/attach_screenshot(); session.checkpoint() wires both; existing scn unit tests pass unchanged; a live run + npx allure generate shows tagged steps and a UI-failure screenshot attachment.
notes:
LIVE VERIFICATION (2026-06-11, TestExec-001): the deferred acceptance
criterion (live test_journey run + npx allure generate showing
"[<scenario> <ac-label>] <SURFACE>"-tagged steps) is now confirmed. The
generated Allure report (test-results/TestExec-001/allure-report) shows
steps like "[journey sync-create] DOC/SHEET", "[journey tracker-present]
TRACKER", "[journey onSyncNow] SHEET", "[journey ui-create] DOC/SHEET" as
nested Allure steps under each ACT/UIACT/QUERY step, all passed. Run done
as part of gts-yuvq's live verification (no separate run needed).
on_ui_fail/attach_screenshot path not exercised this run (Act 5's failure
was a raw exception, not a drained UI FAIL) -- pre-existing scope note, not
a defect.
close_reason: Implemented step_cm/on_ui_fail hooks in CheckpointEngine.drain(), Reporter.allure_step()/attach_screenshot()/step() Allure wrapping, and session.checkpoint() wiring. Unit tests extended in test_scn_engine.py/test_scn_reporter.py/test_scn_session.py (233 scn unit tests pass). Live Allure-report verification (npx allure generate against a real test_journey run) deferred — requires deployed GAS WebApp.

title: [INF] Per-execution TestExec-NNN folders with README + Allure index
description:
Test artifacts (test-results/runs/*.trace.{log,jsonl}, test-results/gas-logs/<timestamp>/, allure-results/, ad-hoc top-level .log files) are currently scattered with no correlation to which deployed GAS version/revision was being tested, which test package was run, or what question the run was investigating. Surfaced during the 2026-06-11 o5py/mpe1/u2np/7gyt session, which involved 5 redeploys and 3 test runs that were hard to retroactively distinguish.

Proposal:
1. Each pytest invocation gets its own test-results/TestExec-NNN/ folder containing all artifacts for that run (trace.log, trace.jsonl, gas-logs/, allure-results/ + generated allure-report/, pytest stdout).
2. TestExec-NNN/README.md (auto-generated) records: deployed GAS version/revision (from npm run verify:test output), test file(s)/package executed, the question/issue being investigated (free-text, supplied by the invoker), and a pass/fail summary.
3. A lightweight top-level test-results/INDEX.md or generated index.html lists each TestExec-NNN with its README excerpt + summary + link to that run's allure-report/index.html.

Allure's own history/trend feature (history/ carried between allure generate runs) covers cross-build trend graphs but not per-run narrative metadata - the custom README+index layer is additive, not a replacement.
acceptance_criteria: Running the test suite produces a self-contained TestExec-NNN/ folder with trace logs, gas-logs, allure-report, and a README.md documenting deployed version + test package + investigation question + pass/fail summary. A regenerable top-level index lists all TestExec-NNN runs with README excerpts and links to their allure-report.
close_reason: Implemented scripts/run_test_exec.py: wraps pytest in self-contained test-results/TestExec-NNN/ folders (traces via SCN_RUN_DIR, GAS logs via SCN_GAS_LOG_DIR, Allure report, JUnit, README with deployed-version + pass/fail summary, regenerated INDEX.md). title: [RESEARCH] Probe-tier chip hover trigger via canvas pixel coordinates
description: Why: smoke.test.js's '@smoke link preview chip is present in test doc' test currently soft-passes because its selector (`.kix-canvas-tile-content a, .docs-smartchip-container a`) can never match — Google Docs renders the AI-N: link text AND its leading link-preview icon entirely onto a single `.kix-canvas-tile-content` element. There is no DOM , , or chip element to locate or hover. What's confirmed (2026-06-10 investigation against live clone doc 1lrSOUVuB9in9aTINIFyfvLm4cu1jFeb09bHbEHBFROk, AI-1): - DOM search near the rendered "AI-1:" link (screen pos ~x=275,y=651) found nothing but ruler tick marks — zero chip/link/icon DOM nodes. - Only real DOM nodes in the content area: the user-avatar and the .kix-canvas-tile-content itself (x=185,y=145, 816x1056). - `#docs-link-bubble.appsElementsLinkPreview` (the singleton hover-preview overlay) does NOT exist in the DOM on initial page load — Docs creates it lazily on first hover anywhere. When populated (captured via manual devtools hover), its `data-url` attribute carries the chip's URL including globalId, e.g. `https://northlakeuu.org/NUTS/action?c=view&globalId=%2FAI-1`. This is the right assertion target once a hover can be triggered. Candidate approaches to get real pixel coordinates for page.mouse.move(): 1. Place the text cursor on the AI-N: link via Find/keyboard navigation, then read `.kix-cursor`'s getBoundingClientRect() (cursor IS a real positioned DOM element) — leading candidate, lowest setup cost. 2. Toggle Docs "screen reader support" (Tools > Accessibility) to switch to DOM-based rendering with real elements — heavier setup, may change other behaviors. 3. Compute position from canvas bounding rect + known document layout (font size, line height, paragraph order) — fragile, breaks on content changes. Scope: this is probe-tier (tests/playwright/probe.test.js), not smoke-tier — per OPERATIONS.md, smoke must stay fast and not assert artifact/consistency state. Outcome of this research issue should be either a working chipHover probe assertion on #docs-link-bubble[data-url*=globalId], or a documented conclusion that it's not practically automatable, with smoke.test.js's soft-pass left as the permanent design.
close_reason: Resolved: working chipHover probe assertion implemented in tests/playwright/probe.test.js. The native Docs link-preview bubble (#docs-link-bubble.appsElementsLinkPreview) is reproducibly triggerable WITHOUT mouse hover: focus .kix-appview-editor, Ctrl+F, type 'AI-N:', Enter, Escape — the cursor lands on the link (keyboard equivalent of 'click once on the link'), and the bubble's href/[data-url] carry ?c=view&globalId=<docId>%2FAI-N, readable via page.evaluate. Confirmed reproducible 2x against a fresh isolated doc (ScenarioSession.new_doc + sync). Pre-existing unrelated finding spun off as GTaskSheet-p8w0 (npm run probe currently reports 'No tests found' due to testIgnore). Details in bd memory key 39jk-link-bubble-ctrlf-trigger.

title: [INF] check_coverage.py: detect entry_point= tags on sessions missing request=
description:
Twice now (test_b7, then test_sidebar in gts-rz4k.3) an entry_point= tag
was added to a scn.verify()/expect_*() call, but ScenarioSession.new_doc(settings)
was missing request=request -- so the tag silently never reaches JUnit and
check_coverage.py still reports the entry point as deferred/uncovered, with no
direct error pointing at the cause.

Idea: either (a) scn/session.py warns/raises if entry_point= is used on a
session with no Reporter (request=None), or (b) check_coverage.py / a small
lint script greps for entry_point= kwargs alongside ScenarioSession.new_doc(
calls lacking request= in the same test module.

Low priority -- discovered as a recurring footgun, not blocking any current work.
close_reason: Implemented via a runtime guard instead of the originally-suggested static lint: ScenarioSession._enqueue() (scn/session.py) now raises ValueError if entry_point= is set on a session built without request= (NullReporter, silently drops ep.* coverage). Catches the bug at the call site instead of after a full pytest run. Covered by tests/test_scn_session.py::test_entry_point_without_request_raises and two companion tests.
